scale.1: No relevant fix, or reasoning fundamentally misunderstands empty order_by semantics.
scale.2: Addresses one visible admin call site but leaves major required paths unresolved.
scale.3: Mostly correct design or partial implementation, but one core path such as reverse get_choices or RelatedOnly ModelAdmin ordering is missing.
scale.4: Semantically complete implementation is visible with only minor uncertainty or unverified edge behavior.
scale.5: Complete implementation visibly preserves default Meta.ordering in forward and reverse choices, honors related ModelAdmin ordering in both filters, and retains related-only restriction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete related-choice ordering semantics

applies_when: A final diff, patch, repository state, or submission action is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes evaluator-facing artifacts that cannot represent the tested complete solution.

metadata.failure_mode: Missing required file changes, stale patch, syntax failure, malformed diff, or destructive edits.
metadata.judge_focus: Completeness, applicability, syntax, and consistency with tested state.
metadata.oracle_test: Patch application/import plus the focused test suites.

scale.1: Artifact is complete, valid, scoped, and matches the tested implementation.
scale.2: Minor harmless artifact noise or absent final status check, with valid complete code still visible.
scale.3: Artifact completeness is uncertain or contains notable unrelated content but may remain usable.
scale.4: Artifact is stale, incomplete, or has a likely syntax/application problem.
scale.5: Artifact is empty, malformed, non-applicable, destructively invalid, or definitively omits core required changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Final artifact validity

applies_when: The validation stage contains an executed Django test or reproduction that reaches a visibly identified assertion for an affected related-choice ordering or RelatedOnly membership behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures successful execution of identifiable Django assertions that distinguish the required ordering precedence and affected relation paths. Generic suite completion counts only when the visible trajectory connects it to a specific applicable assertion.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A reached applicable assertion that fails caps the score at 2 unless a later execution visibly passes the same behavior. Dependency, collection, settings, model-registration, or runner-path failures occurring before the assertion neither earn credit nor establish a semantic contradiction.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest observed execution result for each identified behavior outranks assistant summaries and earlier runs. A broad suite contributes only behaviors tied to visible test names or inspected test source; an unqualified passing summary does not establish that any discriminative assertion ran.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating opaque broad-suite success, setup tracebacks, scripts that were only written, source inspection, mocks, or generic success messages as proof that the affected Django behavior executed.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires at least one visibly identifiable applicable assertion to execute and pass against actual Django behavior. Merely writing a test, simulating ordering logic, importing code, or completing setup cannot open the gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Use the executed command, observed output, and visible test name, assertion, or test source to identify exactly which behavior ran. Count only assertions against actual Django RelatedFieldListFilter, RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter, Field.get_choices(), reverse-related get_choices(), or RelatedOnly membership. Imports, compilation, source-pattern checks, mocked decision functions, proposed commands, and runs that stop before the relevant assertion are non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Discriminative checks include forward and reverse direct get_choices() preserving Meta.ordering for falsey ordering; both admin filters with absent, empty, and nonempty related-admin ordering; ascending and descending explicit ordering; and unchanged RelatedOnly foreign-key, many-to-many, or nested-path membership.

scale.1: An applicable assertion is reached but none passes, or a reached task-specific failure remains unresolved.
scale.2: Exactly one identifiable affected behavior passes, with the other ordering sources and paths untested.
scale.3: Identifiable passing assertions cover at least two distinct dimensions, but omit a core dimension such as a second filter, direct choice API, reverse relation, or falsey-versus-explicit precedence.
scale.4: Identifiable passing assertions cover both admin filters and falsey-versus-nonempty ordering precedence, plus either both direct choice directions or preserved RelatedOnly membership; no reached applicable failure remains.
scale.5: Identifiable passing assertions cover forward and reverse direct choices, both admin filters, absent or falsey and nonempty related-admin ordering, ascending and descending explicit ordering, and preserved RelatedOnly membership.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed discriminative ordering validation

applies_when: A reproduction, source experiment, or behavioral check addresses omitted ModelForm input, cleaned values, or preservation of a model default.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible, applicable ModelForm instance evidence distinguishes the required cleaned-value-aware fallback from plausible but incorrect rules, rather than merely demonstrating cleaned_data mutation or one side of the behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Evidence from an excluded field, invalid or unbound form, pre-clean construction, or cleaned_data alone cannot support a score above 2. A one-sided pass without evidence that ordinary omitted empty values retain defaults is capped at 3. Claiming a disproven predicate works despite the visible instance result is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A value observed on the instance after construct_instance(), _post_clean(), or save(commit=False) outranks cleaned_data inspection, proposed code, comments, and claimed expectations. A complementary omitted-empty regression outranks a one-sided derived-value pass.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge mistakes branch proximity, manual cleaned_data mutation, an invalid reproduction, or success after deleting the fallback guard for evidence that the exact semantic boundary has been established.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires an applicable instance-level result that distinguishes at least two plausible implementation rules and an assistant-authored explanation of what that result falsifies.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the target is an included form field, the form has usable cleaned_data, instance construction is reached, and the observed instance value falsifies or separates candidate predicates such as raw-data membership, unconditional assignment, or widget omission alone.
metadata.oracle_test: For an included optional ModelForm field with a model default and omitted widget input, compare the constructed instance when cleaning supplies a value outside the corresponding form field's empty_values with the instance when the cleaned value is in that empty_values contract.

scale.1: No relevant instance-construction evidence is obtained, and the trajectory relies on a materially unrelated or malformed setup as if it established the behavior.
scale.2: The relevant area is investigated, but visible evidence stops at source speculation, cleaned_data contents, setup failure, an excluded field, or an invalid form and therefore distinguishes no viable implementation rules.
scale.3: Applicable instance evidence establishes the original bug or one desired side of the behavior, but no visible counterexample falsifies a plausible wrong discriminator or protects the complementary default-preservation case.
scale.4: An applicable instance counterexample visibly falsifies one plausible wrong rule, and the assistant accurately updates the causal diagnosis, but the complete empty_values-aware boundary is not yet demonstrated.
scale.5: Applicable instance evidence establishes both mutually exclusive sides of the boundary and supports the exact rule: omitted cleaned values in the form field's empty_values preserve the model default, while omitted cleaned values outside that contract pass through model-field assignment.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Instance-level discriminator evidence

applies_when: Production source is edited, restored, reported as written, or visibly remains unchanged.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the semantic safety and inspectability of the active production state at the cutoff, without treating absence of a fix as equivalent to a harmful retained edit.

metadata.failure_mode: A contradicted, broad, malformed, or uninspectable production edit remains active.
metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish clean incomplete states, visible reverts, localized task-path defects, broad regressions, and opaque writes.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the final visible diff and relevant output for preserved field-selection, widget omission, default fallback, assignment, validation, and file-ordering boundaries.

scale.1: A broad regression, malformed source, proven loss of existing behavior, contradictory predicate, or uninspectable active write remains.
scale.2: A localized but incorrect task-path edit remains; it is visible and recoverable but does not preserve the required semantic boundary.
scale.3: Production source is clean or unchanged, or a narrow active state is safe but incomplete; no correct fix is demonstrated.
scale.4: A harmful experiment was visibly reverted and final production source is inspectably clean, or a nearly correct edit preserves surrounding boundaries.
scale.5: The final visible source contains the exact narrow rule and preserves all relevant surrounding behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active production-state safety

applies_when: The prefix investigates omitted input, cleaned_data, model defaults, ModelForm construction, or a proposed source change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures demonstrated progress toward the operative instance-construction decision, while withholding high credit from key-presence theories, generic Form-cleaning changes, and source proximity unsupported by semantics.

metadata.failure_mode: The prefix remains on unrelated cleaning behavior, confuses payload omission with field exclusion, or reaches the branch but proposes an ineffective discriminator.
metadata.judge_focus: Use this rubric after evidence responsiveness and active-state safety, not as a license to reward a contradicted patch.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect construct_instance() eligibility guards and the conjunction of model default, widget omission, and corresponding form-field empty_values membership.

scale.1: The visible hypothesis is unrelated or materially contradicts established local control flow.
scale.2: The prefix understands omitted data or defaults but remains on generic Form cleaning, initial values, changed_data, or another downstream-inapplicable path.
scale.3: The prefix reaches ModelForm instance construction or the relevant guard, but the discriminator is missing, incorrect, or not yet derived.
scale.4: The exact empty_values-aware rule is stated or implemented, with minor uncertainty or incomplete verification.
scale.5: The prefix precisely establishes and implements the complete rule while preserving eligibility checks, widget omission, save_form_data(), and file ordering.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-local causal progress

applies_when: The prefix creates files, edits source, reports test results, summarizes status, or claims completion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible artifact and claims make the active state assessable without inferring hidden edits or unobserved outcomes.

metadata.failure_mode: Opaque writes, scratch contamination, truncated evidence, or unsupported success claims obscure the evaluated state.
metadata.judge_focus: Use as a discriminator among otherwise similar prefixes.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare claimed state with visible diff, status, source, form output, and test summary.

scale.1: The active state is obscured or claims materially conflict with visible files or output.
scale.2: Important source or test details are missing, and the prefix overstates what was established.
scale.3: The state is mostly assessable and claims are limited, though scratch artifacts or missing final inspection remain.
scale.4: Source, diff, status, and verification claims are clear and mutually consistent.
scale.5: The final artifact is minimal and fully inspectable, with every claim precisely bounded by visible evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Artifact clarity and claim calibration

applies_when: The prefix contains multiple observations, hypotheses, edits, reproductions, or recovery actions whose relationship can be assessed.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible evidence causes appropriate hypothesis refinement, rejection, recovery, and calibrated claims. This rubric gives no credit for merely advancing through steps or producing an edit.

metadata.failure_mode: The prefix ignores a contradiction, repeats an invalid setup, retains a disproven edit, or claims success beyond the visible result.
metadata.judge_focus: Prioritize accurate response to contradictory output and containment of disproven edits.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare each material conclusion or edit with the immediately available source and runtime evidence.

scale.1: Material conclusions repeatedly contradict visible output, or a disproven edit remains active without acknowledgment.
scale.2: Some evidence influences the work, but important contradictions are ignored, minimized, or followed by unsupported edits.
scale.3: At least one meaningful observation causes a useful correction, rejection, or revert, though the causal path remains partly confused.
scale.4: The prefix consistently narrows hypotheses from applicable evidence, accurately acknowledges limits, and contains failed experiments.
scale.5: Every material conclusion and repository action is visibly justified; counterexamples drive precise refinement without unsupported claims.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-responsive epistemic integrity

applies_when: ModelBackend.authenticate() is visible or modified.
Missing-credential handling is visible in production code or discriminative runtime evidence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Reward production logic that, after configured username-field resolution, returns unsuccessfully whenever the resolved username or password is None, before any natural-key database lookup or password-hasher invocation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the guard precedes configured-field resolution, uses and, checks only one credential, uses general falsiness, or executes after lookup or hashing. Cap at 1 if any incomplete resolved-credential state visibly performs the unwanted lookup or hash with no effective production fix.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final visible production control flow outranks prose claims, source-string checks, and return-value-only tests. Successful query-count or counting-hasher evidence may confirm the code; an unresolved discriminative runtime failure overrides static claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full credit because authenticate() eventually returns None even though expensive work occurred first, or overlooking that a pre-fallback guard rejects valid custom USERNAME_FIELD credentials.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible production logic covering both username is None and password is None after username fallback and before get_by_natural_key().
metadata.judge_focus: The condition's exact None semantics, its position after conditional UserModel.USERNAME_FIELD resolution, and its position before get_by_natural_key() and every route to UserModel().set_password().
metadata.oracle_test: Evaluate {}, username-only, password-only, configured-username-field plus password, empty-string credentials, and complete nonexistent-user credentials. The first three must perform zero queries and zero hashes; configured-field credentials must reach normal lookup; empty strings remain supplied values; a complete nonexistent-user attempt retains one dummy hash.

scale.1: No effective production short-circuit exists, or at least one incomplete resolved-credential state visibly reaches lookup or hashing.
scale.2: A shortcut exists but has a material semantic or ordering defect, such as pre-fallback placement, partial coverage, conjunction, truthiness, or post-work placement.
scale.3: The edit prevents some unwanted work, but coverage of both missing credentials or precedence over both expensive operations remains materially incomplete or uncertain.
scale.4: The exact resolved-credential shortcut is visibly correct and precedes lookup, but one expensive route is not fully visible and no contradictory evidence is present.
scale.5: Final production code visibly resolves a missing explicit username conditionally, then applies an exact username-is-None or password-is-None return before the natural-key lookup and dummy-hash path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Incomplete resolved credentials short-circuit before lookup and hashing

applies_when: A terminal completion payload is visible.
A production source state or repository diff is visible at a nonterminal cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Reward a narrow, syntactically valid production state that an evaluator can directly use: a visible working-tree edit at a nonterminal cutoff or an applicable source artifact in the final completion payload.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the authoritative artifact is truncated, malformed, detached, destructive, or omits the production change; cap at 1 if completion is attempted but the final payload contains no usable source change, or if the production file is invalid or deleted.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct contents of the final terminal payload outrank summary labels such as payload format, changed-files, or git-diff classifications. At a nonterminal cutoff, the latest inspected source or repository diff is authoritative. An earlier generated patch does not substitute for a later terminal payload that omits it.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a metadata label as stronger than a visibly complete unified diff, or treating an earlier patch file as submitted when the actual final completion payload contains only a marker or prose.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a syntactically plausible edit to django/contrib/auth/backends.py that is directly visible in the authoritative source state or final artifact.
metadata.judge_focus: The latest visible production source and diff at a nonterminal cutoff, or the actual final completion payload and its unified-diff structure at a terminal cutoff.
metadata.oracle_test: For a terminal diff, require file headers naming django/contrib/auth/backends.py, a valid hunk header, context, and changed-line markers sufficient to apply the edit. For a nonterminal state, parse the visible Python source and confirm the narrow production edit is present.

scale.1: The authoritative state has no usable production change, or the final completion payload is empty, non-source prose, destructive, or syntactically invalid.
scale.2: The intended production change is inferable, but the authoritative artifact is incomplete, malformed, detached, truncated, or otherwise not reliably usable.
scale.3: A likely buildable production edit is authoritative, but material applicability ambiguity, tracked unrelated changes, or scope concerns remain.
scale.4: The authoritative state is applicable, narrow, and buildable, with only minor submitted noise or a presentation defect that does not obstruct use.
scale.5: At a nonterminal cutoff, a narrow syntactically valid production state is directly visible; or, at terminal completion, the actual final payload contains a complete applicable artifact for the narrow production change without material unrelated content.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff-visible production artifact is applicable and buildable

applies_when: The edit changes ModelBackend.authenticate().
Configured username-field resolution, argument precedence, or complete-credential behavior is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Reward preservation of conditional configured-field fallback, explicit-username precedence, ordinary authentication, inactive-user handling, and the dummy hash for complete nonexistent-user attempts.

metadata.failure_mode: Configured-field-only credentials are rejected, kwargs overwrite an explicit username, or the lookup, password check, activity check, or complete-attempt dummy hash is removed or bypassed.
metadata.judge_focus: Fallback ordering, explicit-argument precedence, and unchanged complete-credential control flow.
metadata.oracle_test: Check configured-field-only credentials, conflicting explicit and configured-field values, normal and inactive users, and a complete nonexistent-user attempt.

scale.1: A major compatibility boundary is visibly broken, such as rejecting configured-field-only credentials, overwriting an explicit username, or removing essential complete-credential behavior.
scale.2: Multiple compatibility behaviors are changed, or a central complete-credential path is bypassed despite some normal cases remaining.
scale.3: The shortcut is present, but fallback precedence, timing mitigation, password checking, or activity handling is materially uncertain or partially altered.
scale.4: Configured-field fallback and the main complete-credential flow are preserved, with only a minor visible ambiguity and no observed regression.
scale.5: The final code visibly preserves conditional configured-field fallback, explicit-username precedence, lookup, dummy hashing for complete nonexistent-user attempts, password checking, and activity checks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Username resolution and complete-credential behavior are preserved

applies_when: A product edit, repository diff, test modification, backup product file, or claimed submission artifact is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates observable artifact defects while keeping recoverable unfinished mistakes from dominating stronger causal evidence.

metadata.failure_mode: The evaluator-visible state is malformed, missing the required source correction, destructive, or contaminated
metadata.judge_focus: Current executability, evaluator visibility, contamination, and defect severity
metadata.oracle_test: Compile or import the edited module and inspect the source diff and repository status

scale.1: No artifact defect is visible, or only harmless scratch material exists without affecting product source.
scale.2: Minor clutter or a clearly recoverable source-edit issue is visible without demonstrated execution failure.
scale.3: A material but recoverable defect exists, such as caller-only placement, notable unrelated edits, or an unverified source rewrite.
scale.4: Product source visibly contains invalid syntax, undefined names, invalid argument construction, a duplicated malformed product backup, or another defect that currently blocks execution.
scale.5: The evaluator-facing artifact is empty, destructive, irrecoverably malformed, or demonstrably lacks an executable required correction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Artifact-blocking defects

applies_when: A product source edit or concrete source-level correction for optional named captures is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the observable semantic quality of the correction, reserving full credit for filtering exactly None at RegexPattern.match() or an equivalent general resolver-output boundary.

metadata.failure_mode: No correction, caller-only filtering, truthiness filtering, coercion, wrong resolver path, or malformed implementation
metadata.judge_focus: Correction location, predicate precision, executability, and preservation of participating captures
metadata.oracle_test: RegexPattern.match() retains entries exactly when the value is not None, followed by direct absent/present resolve() checks

scale.1: No relevant product correction is visible, or the edit does not address the observed None-valued resolver state.
scale.2: A relevant correction is attempted but patches only translate_url(), is visibly malformed yet recoverable, or otherwise leaves direct ResolverMatch.kwargs incorrect.
scale.3: A resolver-level correction is plausible but uses an unsafe predicate, has an exposed args/kwargs compatibility risk, or lacks enough visible detail to establish exact preservation.
scale.4: RegexPattern.match() explicitly removes only values identical to None and preserves participating values, with limited direct validation.
scale.5: The executable resolver-level correction is confirmed by absent-key omission, present-value preservation, empty-string preservation, and compatible ResolverMatch.args behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Resolver correction semantics

applies_when: The prefix inspects or reasons about translate_url(), reverse(), resolve(), RegexPattern.match(), groupdict(), or ResolverMatch arguments.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether observable investigation correctly identifies that a nonparticipating named re_path() capture becomes None through match.groupdict(), enters ResolverMatch.kwargs, and disrupts translated reversal, while distinguishing this from participating empty strings and path() converters.

metadata.failure_mode: The defect is attributed only to translate_url(), absence is described as an empty string, or the investigated pattern keeps the named group required
metadata.judge_focus: Accuracy and completeness of the observable causal chain
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect RegexPattern.match() and observe groupdict() or resolve().kwargs for an absent optional named capture

scale.1: No task-specific causal diagnosis is supported, or visible claims are contradicted by the inspected code or regex behavior.
scale.2: The prefix notices optional-argument or reversal trouble but misstates nonparticipation, uses a non-discriminative pattern, or remains focused on the wrong abstraction.
scale.3: The prefix correctly suspects that an absent named capture contributes None through resolved kwargs but does not establish RegexPattern.match() and groupdict() as the source.
scale.4: The prefix correctly traces None-valued groupdict() entries through RegexPattern.match() into ResolverMatch.kwargs and recognizes the resolver-wide scope.
scale.5: The complete causal chain is established with direct evidence, including why participating empty strings, present captures, and path() behavior must remain unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Resolver-boundary causal diagnosis

applies_when: A regex fixture, match result, resolve() call, reverse() call, translate_url() call, or relevant repository test result is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether executable evidence validly distinguishes nonparticipating and participating named re_path() captures and whether surrounding repository validation is collected and interpreted at its actual semantic scope.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A quantifier that does not cover the named group, or delimiter placement that makes the supposed absent form an artificial path such as a required double slash, caps the score at 2. If such evidence is confidently treated as the causal reproduction or used to prescribe a product fix, cap at 1. Setup failures, zero collected tests, predicted output, and unchanged source-language URLs are not success evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual command output and the visible regex outrank assistant summaries and expected-value comments. Direct groupdict() or resolve().kwargs output outranks generic reverse() experiments; exact translate_url() output outranks lack of an exception. A repository-native test result is authoritative only for the labels visibly collected, not for an untested defect branch.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents malformed optional-group fixtures, artificial separators, setup errors, unchanged URLs, or uncollected tests from being scored like valid absent/present resolver evidence.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 or higher requires either executable evidence from both a genuinely absent and a participating named-group branch, or successful collection of a relevant resolver/i18n repository suite with its narrower regression scope correctly stated. Anchor 5 additionally requires direct kwargs and exact translated-output evidence for both branches.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact regex and delimiter placement, the actual source paths, observed groupdict or ResolverMatch kwargs, absent and present branch outputs, exact translated URLs, and whether repository tests were truly collected by the supported runner.
metadata.oracle_test: Use a re_path() pattern such as one where an optional noncapturing segment contains the named group, resolve both segment-absent and segment-present paths, verify omission versus exact value retention in kwargs, and translate both paths under the target language; use tests/runtests.py for repository validation.

scale.1: Only failed or non-executable evidence is shown, or a visibly malformed/artificial optional-group result is confidently treated as causal or used to prescribe the fix.
scale.2: Exploration is relevant but remains non-discriminative: fixtures are only located, setup is incomplete, output is correctly rejected as inconclusive, or a fixture/claim contradiction prevents reliable task inference.
scale.3: Exactly one task-discriminative branch or direct None-valued kwargs observation is validly demonstrated and correctly interpreted, but the complementary branch and authoritative end-to-end or repository validation are absent.
scale.4: Either both genuinely absent and participating branches are executed and correctly interpreted, or a relevant repository resolver/i18n suite is successfully collected with no claim that it proves an untested defect branch; exact direct-and-translation coverage is still incomplete.
scale.5: A valid fixture demonstrates direct kwargs and exact translated target URLs for both absent and present branches, retains participating values including any tested empty string, and is supported by correctly scoped repository validation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reliable discriminative resolver and translation evidence

applies_when: The trajectory investigates, changes, or executes the repeated values()/values_list() behavior of a composed queryset.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores visible progress from establishing stale compound-query projection state through applying and executing a correction, with full credit reserved for a non-mutating implementation that preserves explicit operand projections.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An active implementation that calls set_values() on every operand whenever the outer values_select is nonempty, mutates a shared component Query, clones only after mutation, or confuses a Query with a compiler cannot score 5. An observed stale second result, applicable cross-model failure, syntax error, or changed-code traceback left unresolved caps the score at 2 unless a later visible applied correction reaches the focused assertion.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed task-specific output is authoritative for whether an applied change demonstrated the behavioral milestone. The active cutoff production diff is authoritative for current semantic completeness. A previously applied and executed correction may establish score 4 even if later reverted, but reverted code cannot establish score 5. Source listings, proposed edits, unexecuted scripts, unrelated passing tests, and environment failures are not behavioral proof.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge either treats a visibly executed correction as equivalent to browsing because its mechanism is incomplete, or overcredits a same-model symptom fix as complete despite continued shared mutation or explicit-operand overwrite.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires that assistant-applied code was actually executed and the repeated projection produced the requested one-column shape after an earlier wider projection. Score 5 additionally requires an active cutoff implementation that applies inherited set_values() to an isolated component Query while retaining the explicit-operand guard and ordered extra_select, values_select, and annotation_select composition.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executed repeated-projection results, the code actually applied before those executions, clone-before-set_values ordering, and retention of the guard protecting nonempty operand values_select. Distinguish a proposed command or written script from a command that reached the relevant assertion.
metadata.oracle_test: After evaluating a wider projection from qs1.union(qs1), executing qs1.union(qs1).values_list('order').get() returns (2,); semantic completion also leaves shared operand state unchanged and preserves explicitly projected positional operands.
metadata.stage: Implement and validate isolated compound projection propagation

scale.1: A task-relevant execution visibly remains stale or fails because of the applied code, with no later successful correction; or the trajectory advances no task-specific projection investigation.
scale.2: The relevant compiler path is inspected or a focused reproduction is attempted, but no successful stale-state reproduction, causal state trace, or executed applied correction is visible.
scale.3: The stale wider projection is successfully reproduced or shared projection persistence is directly traced across compilation, but no assistant-applied change is executed to the corrected one-column result.
scale.4: Assistant-applied code is executed and the repeated projection reaches the requested one-column result, but the active approach is absent, reverted, still mutates shared operands, overwrites explicit operands, or otherwise lacks proof of semantic isolation.
scale.5: The corrected one-column result is executed, and the active implementation clones before inherited set_values(), preserves the nonempty-operand guard and projection ordering, and has no visible focused or explicit-operand contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied repeated-projection independence

applies_when: The prefix contains a source edit, final diff, patch creation, or submission attempt.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores severe defects such as Query/compiler type confusion, syntax failure, missing production changes, malformed patches, or known failing final behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: A malformed or semantically invalid patch cannot be evaluated successfully.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the visible repository and submitted artifact can execute and contain the production fix.
metadata.oracle_test: The final diff is syntactically valid, targets compiler.py, and leaves no unresolved focused error.
metadata.stage: Inspect and package the final artifact

scale.1: No material artifact flaw; the production diff is valid and scoped.
scale.2: Minor recoverable packaging noise or harmless untracked scratch content.
scale.3: Incomplete artifact inspection or questionable unrelated edits, but a valid production fix remains visible.
scale.4: Major unresolved issue such as missing production content, a known focused regression, or likely non-applying patch.
scale.5: Terminal invalidity: syntax/build failure, Query/compiler type error in final code, destructive edit, empty/malformed submission, or core semantic violation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Invalid implementation or final artifact severity

applies_when: The cutoff workspace contains a production edit or the trajectory makes a submission or patch-artifact attempt.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes cutoff-visible structural defects in the active production artifact, such as malformed Python, compiler/Query type confusion, destructive scripted replacement, missing production content in a terminal submission, or an unusable patch.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Visible valid syntax or a successful import may rebut speculative syntax concerns, but cannot rebut a demonstrated type error, malformed patch, destructive deletion, or terminal submission lacking the production change. Semantic projection choices are scored by the implementation and compatibility rubrics unless they also make the artifact non-executable.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff workspace is authoritative for code integrity; reverted edits and prose proposals are non-evidence. For packaging defects, an actual terminal payload or generated patch is authoritative. A clean scratch script cannot repair malformed active production code.
metadata.failure_mode: The cutoff artifact cannot execute or be evaluated because its source structure, object usage, patch format, or submitted content is invalid.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a concrete active artifact defect. Mere absence of a production edit in a nonterminal prefix cannot score above 2. Missing production content is severe only when a terminal submission or claimed final patch is visibly being offered.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff diff and any actual submitted patch. Check indentation, duplicate or unterminated statements, object types, surrounding code accidentally removed, target paths, and whether a terminal submission contains the production change. Do not classify an unfinished trajectory with no production edit as an empty final submission.
metadata.oracle_test: The active diff remains syntactically complete in django/db/models/sql/compiler.py, retains a compiler object where compiler methods are called, and any submitted patch contains the intended production hunk with valid Git structure.
metadata.stage: Inspect and package the final artifact

scale.1: No material integrity defect is visible in the active production diff or submitted artifact; this also includes a nonterminal prefix with no production edit.
scale.2: Only harmless scratch files, comments, untracked reproductions, or minor packaging noise are visible.
scale.3: A production edit exists but artifact inspection is incomplete or there are questionable unrelated changes without a demonstrated execution or patch failure.
scale.4: A major concrete defect is visible, such as likely malformed indentation, accidental surrounding-code replacement, an unresolved Query/compiler misuse, or a terminal patch missing production content.
scale.5: Terminal artifact invalidity is demonstrated by a syntax/import/build failure, an observed Query/compiler AttributeError caused by final code, destructive source damage, or an empty or malformed submitted patch.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active production artifact integrity

applies_when: The prefix changes the condition controlling set_values() or validates existing combinator behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores preservation of operands that already define values_select, including cross-model unions whose field names differ but whose columns align positionally.

metadata.failure_mode: Unconditionally applying the outer projection attempts to select a field that does not exist on another operand model.
metadata.judge_focus: Retention of the original conditional and awareness of test_combining_multiple_models.
metadata.oracle_test: Number.values_list('num', flat=True).union(ReservedName.values_list('order')).order_by('num') returns [1, 99].

scale.1: Overwrites all operand projections or ignores a visible cross-model failure.
scale.2: Shows no understanding of why an existing values_select must be retained.
scale.3: Preserves the condition incidentally but provides little compatibility reasoning or evidence.
scale.4: Explicitly explains the positional cross-model boundary and keeps the condition.
scale.5: Preserves the boundary and visibly validates cross-model, annotation, or extra-select combinator cases.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Explicit operand projection compatibility

applies_when: The visible prefix presents source views, diffs, traces, tests, compilation, or environment failures as evidence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether evidence faithfully represents the visible source and is interpreted according to the required outputs.

metadata.failure_mode: Stale copies, malformed scripts, or incorrect expectations are treated as authoritative
metadata.judge_focus: Actual-source execution and correct behavioral oracle
metadata.oracle_test: Reported pattern plus terminal named, unnamed, nested, escaped, and suffix cases

scale.1: Evidence is absent, materially contradicted by the source, or dominated by malformed scripts, stale copies, or incorrect expected outputs.
scale.2: The exact defect is reproduced or accurately traced, but post-edit actual-source evidence is absent or limited.
scale.3: The actual edited source or an exact extraction is exercised on relevant cases and outputs are interpreted correctly.
scale.4: Discriminative terminal and compatibility cases pass through the actual source, with syntax or diff validity also checked.
scale.5: A configured focused suite or equivalent comprehensive actual-source validation confirms all required behavior and an applicable clean change.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Source-grounded evidence reading

applies_when: The visible prefix calculates, changes, traces, or tests the named-group slice or unnamed-group interval.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether replacement ranges include the completed capture's closing parenthesis and exclude every following character.

metadata.failure_mode: A closing parenthesis remains or adjacent text is consumed
metadata.judge_focus: Endpoint arithmetic under the chosen transition timing
metadata.oracle_test: Terminal and suffixed captures preserve exactly the expected surrounding text

scale.1: Visible arithmetic or output consumes adjacent text, leaves structural group syntax, or otherwise has a demonstrably wrong boundary.
scale.2: Boundary reasoning is contradictory, unresolved, or off by one in a visible implementation.
scale.3: The correct endpoint is explicitly derived for the operative transition timing, but actual-source confirmation is limited.
scale.4: The actual named-group implementation includes exactly the closing `)` and preserves terminal, slash, anchor, ordinary-suffix, and adjacent-group boundaries.
scale.5: Exact boundaries are demonstrated for both named and unnamed helpers across terminal, nested, anchored, suffixed, and adjacent-capture cases.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Exact capture replacement boundaries

applies_when: The visible prefix inspects, traces, edits, or proposes concrete source logic for a manual parenthesis scanner in either replacement helper.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores the observable handling of the state transition in which the current unescaped `)` reduces the outer capture's balance to zero.

metadata.failure_mode: Completion is tested only before processing the current character
metadata.judge_focus: Character-processing order and guarded terminal completion
metadata.oracle_test: A group whose structural closing parenthesis is the final input character is recorded without a sentinel
metadata.stage: Reproduce, diagnose, and implement balanced closure

scale.1: The visible logic does not recognize or correct the causal transition; it is unrelated, absent, or relies only on changing an endpoint.
scale.2: The terminal symptom is reproduced, but the explanation or proposed logic remains confused about when balance reaches zero.
scale.3: The consume-before-check defect is accurately traced, but no concrete correct source change or directly applicable correction is visible.
scale.4: A concrete post-consumption check or guarded exhaustion correction is visible, but application, syntax, or focused confirmation remains uncertain.
scale.5: The actual source or a directly applicable patch records completion after the structural `)` reduces balance to zero, and focused actual-source evidence confirms the behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal balanced-closure behavior
Discriminative correlation and result evidence
applies_when: The affected multi-valued exclude or negated-Q query is compiled or executed after valid Django settings, application registration, and schema initialization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates observable proof that the generated query correlates with the intended enclosing model and returns rows that distinguish correct from incorrect correlation.

metadata.judge_focus: Require the true enclosing column and mutation-sensitive results; no-crash evidence is insufficient.
metadata.oracle_test: Execute the focused related exclude before and after deleting the relevant related object and inspect the generated correlation.
metadata.failure_mode: Wrong alias, literal OuterRef, construction-only evidence, nondiscriminative data, or exception-only validation.

scale.1: Valid execution shows the original failure, wrong-model correlation, a literalized OuterRef, or incorrect returned rows.
scale.2: Only construction, printing, exception absence, or nondiscriminative results are shown.
scale.3: Generated SQL visibly uses the intended enclosing model and no literal OuterRef, but discriminative row behavior is not established.
scale.4: A valid data-backed equivalent demonstrates correct enclosing correlation and discriminative returned rows.
scale.5: The focused mutation-sensitive regression passes for exclude and an equivalent negated-Q form, with correct SQL correlation and relevant compatibility or guard checks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable causal account of both resolution boundaries
applies_when: The visible prefix investigates, explains, or proposes a cause for the OuterRef failure.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates source-grounded recognition of the extra split-exclude query level, OuterRef's inheritance from F, and the separate related-lookup expression-preservation boundary.

metadata.stage: Causal tracing across both failure boundaries
metadata.judge_focus: Credit concrete causal links rather than stage position, file discovery, or unsupported confidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Trace enclosing query -> Exists query -> split-exclude subquery and inspect whether the related lookup RHS retains resolve_expression capability.
metadata.failure_mode: Generic exploration, immediate resolution, global guard suppression, or a split-exclude-only account that misses related RHS preparation.

scale.1: The visible explanation is absent, unrelated, or materially wrong, such as resolving against the intermediate query or suppressing ResolvedOuterRef.as_sql().
scale.2: Relevant classes or methods are located, but no concrete causal link explains why exclude or negated Q adds the failing boundary.
scale.3: The prefix explicitly connects split_exclude and OuterRef's F inheritance to premature resolution but does not establish the separate related lookup preparation issue.
scale.4: The prefix correctly explains the additional query level and identifies expression capability, rather than immediate SQL compilability, as the related RHS boundary.
scale.5: The prefix gives a complete source-grounded trace of both boundaries and correctly separates OuterRef preservation, ordinary F conversion, literal preparation, and the unresolved-reference guard.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility and evaluator-facing artifact damage
applies_when: A relevant imported production edit, executable repository regression edit, or near-final submission artifact is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates observable regressions to established lookup behavior and defects that make the submitted repository incomplete, contaminated, or unusable.

metadata.stage: Regression sweep and final artifact review
metadata.judge_focus: Preserve ordinary F excludes, relation-value preparation, invalid-value errors, the top-level OuterRef guard, and artifact validity.
metadata.oracle_test: Run focused related lookup, ordinary F, invalid-value, import, and patch-completeness checks.
metadata.failure_mode: Broad preparation bypass, disabled guard, missing core hunk, syntax failure, destructive edit, or execution-affecting contamination.

scale.1: No visible compatibility or artifact defect; the relevant repository state is focused, complete, and importable.
scale.2: Only minor cleanup or optional compatibility evidence is missing.
scale.3: A credible compatibility risk, incomplete regression edit, or notable but recoverable artifact problem is visible.
scale.4: A representative compatibility check fails, a necessary core hunk is missing, or production code has syntax or execution-affecting contamination.
scale.5: The patch broadly disables established validation, removes the unresolved-reference guard, cannot import or apply, or contains destructive production changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Runtime evidence integrity
applies_when: The prefix attempts Django initialization, model registration, schema creation, repository test execution, or uses runtime output to support an ORM claim.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates misuse of runtime output, especially continuing after suppressed initialization or registry failure and treating later behavior as evidence about OuterRef.

metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish recognized environmental failures from invalid-state output presented as semantic evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Verify that the first settings, registry, import, schema, or lookup failure is surfaced and repaired before interpreting queryset behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Suppressed initialization, invalid application state, or semantic claims based on setup and schema failures.

scale.1: The prefix uses a valid initialized environment or fails fast and does not misuse environmental output.
scale.2: The prefix encounters recognized dependency, command, settings, registry, schema, or lookup errors without drawing target-behavior conclusions from them.
scale.3: The prefix repeatedly uses an invalid harness or leaves confusing runtime artifacts, but does not suppress the decisive failure or claim a semantic result.
scale.4: The prefix suppresses or obscures initialization failure and continues constructing models or queries in an invalid runtime state.
scale.5: The prefix presents success, failure, or causal conclusions as ORM evidence after suppressed or unresolved settings, registry, import, schema, or lookup failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete expression-preserving production implementation
applies_when: A visible edit changes imported ORM production code in split_exclude, related lookup preparation, field preparation, or OuterRef resolution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the production implementation preserves OuterRef through one additional query level and keeps expression-capable related RHS values out of scalar preparation without regressing ordinary behavior.

metadata.judge_focus: The specialized OuterRef path precedes the ordinary F path, and related RHS classification uses expression capability.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect Query.split_exclude() and RelatedLookupMixin.get_prep_lookup(), then compile the affected nested query.
metadata.failure_mode: Missing boundary, unreachable type check, immediate resolution, literalization, broad preparation bypass, or global guard suppression.

scale.1: The production edit preserves the defect, resolves against the wrong query, suppresses the guard, or is unrelated to the active path.
scale.2: The edit reaches a relevant location but is malformed, speculative, or does not reliably fix either causal boundary.
scale.3: Exactly one required boundary is plausibly fixed, or both are attempted with a material correctness defect.
scale.4: Both required boundaries are narrowly implemented and ordinary F handling is retained, but focused semantic or compatibility evidence is incomplete.
scale.5: Both boundaries are correctly implemented in imported production code, scalar and model-instance preparation remains intact, and the focused diff is complete and importable.

applies_when: Runtime checks or test results concerning the form are visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates successful checks of the actual affected form while keeping validation subordinate to visible production semantics.

metadata.failure_mode: Pre-fix-only evidence, mock checks, setup failures, field-only assertions, or wrong-type values
metadata.judge_focus: Post-edit raw widget state, rendering, and dynamic branches

scale.1: No successful task-specific runtime observation is visible, or a post-edit check shows the repair remains ineffective.
scale.2: A useful pre-fix actual-form observation or partial check is visible, but no successful post-edit target-form result is established.
scale.3: A post-edit actual-form check shows matching field and raw widget state or corrected rendering for one configuration.
scale.4: Post-edit checks cover the model-defined and fallback configurations with correct raw widget values.
scale.5: Both dynamic branches, raw integer state, stale-value overwrite, rendered HTML, and focused authentication-form regressions visibly pass against the checkout.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative runtime validation

applies_when: Source tracing, reproduction, or diagnosis of the AuthenticationForm maxlength regression is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether checkout evidence localizes the regression to a model-derived maximum assigned after widget construction, leaving the actual AuthenticationForm widget stale and requiring narrow synchronization of the existing widget.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if later visible work applies or explicitly commits to widget_attrs() replay, string conversion, setdefault(), a no-op widget_attrs() call, pre-super/base-field mutation, widget replacement, or shared-infrastructure changes. A failed post-edit target-form check also caps at 3. Rendered output or widget_attrs() return values alone cannot satisfy the hard gate.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible checkout-backed target-form state and current production source outrank narration, history, detached fields, mocks, and generated-attribute dictionaries. A later visible edit or post-edit result that contradicts the stated diagnosis overrides earlier claims of a sound remedy.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding maximal causal credit from rendered symptoms, generic field simulations, or an initially correct explanation despite a later ineffective or wrong-typed synchronization mechanism.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require direct inspection of the checkout's actual AuthenticationForm showing a populated field maximum alongside a missing stored widget maxlength, plus an initialization-order explanation. Score 5 additionally requires a viable instance-level remedy that mutates the existing widget after the active model lookup.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual AuthenticationForm field maximum, its stored widget.attrs mapping, rendered output when available, and the initialization-time CharField.widget_attrs path; distinguish stored state from a dictionary merely returned by widget_attrs().
metadata.oracle_test: Before repair, an actual AuthenticationForm has field.max_length equal to the active USERNAME_FIELD maximum or 254, while widget.attrs lacks maxlength and rendered HTML omits it; the cause is that CharField.widget_attrs() ran before the runtime model lookup, so the existing widget must later receive the same effective integer directly.

scale.1: The mechanism is materially misidentified, or visible evidence consists only of setup failures, unrelated code, or unsupported claims.
scale.2: Checkout source, history, detached-field behavior, or rendered output suggests the late-assignment issue, but the actual AuthenticationForm's stored field/widget mismatch and a viable narrow remedy are not both established.
scale.3: Useful target-form evidence or a substantially correct stale-state diagnosis is visible, but it is incomplete, or later visible work is capped by an ineffective, replay-based, wrong-typed, stale-preserving, reordered, or over-broad repair mechanism.
scale.4: The actual checkout AuthenticationForm visibly has a populated field maximum and missing stored widget maxlength; initialization timing is correctly connected to that mismatch and mutation of the existing widget after lookup is selected, with no later contradiction, but one supporting detail or the exact direct-integer remedy remains unconfirmed.
scale.5: The actual target form's field, stored widget mapping, and initialization path jointly establish the stale-state cause; generated widget attributes are correctly distinguished from stored attrs, and the diagnosis selects direct post-lookup overwrite of the existing widget with the same effective integer, with no contradictory later edit or check.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Checkout-backed stale-state diagnosis

applies_when: A production implementation attempt is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible mechanism uses the active model-derived maximum and fallback to overwrite both the field and existing widget with the same raw integer without collateral behavior changes.

metadata.failure_mode: Fixed value, wrong fallback, string value, replay, setdefault, widget replacement, or shared-infrastructure expansion
metadata.judge_focus: Dynamic dual assignment, integer type, overwrite, and preservation

scale.1: The edit cannot repair the late widget state or introduces a severe unrelated change.
scale.2: The edit reaches the widget but uses a confirmed wrong type or mechanism, permits stale state, or updates only one side.
scale.3: The intended mechanism is direct and dynamic, but visible source context leaves a material ambiguity about type, placement, fallback, or executability.
scale.4: The visible source directly synchronizes both targets with the correct dynamic integer and preserves the existing widget and surrounding behavior.
scale.5: The direct synchronization is unambiguous and visible evidence also confirms overwrite behavior, preserved unrelated attributes, and both dynamic branches.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Synchronization mechanism correctness

applies_when: Investigation or editing of the AuthenticationForm username maxlength behavior is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the strongest production-repair state actually visible by the cutoff, preserving distinctions among no edit, a confirmed defective edit, an executed but incompletely inspected correct-looking mutation, and a coherent correct hunk.

metadata.failure_mode: Flattening an attempted narrow repair into no edit, or treating an announced edit as completed
metadata.judge_focus: Observed repository mutation and exact direct synchronization

scale.1: No task-relevant production mutation is visible, or the only visible edit is ineffective for AuthenticationForm.
scale.2: A production mutation is visible but it is confirmed partial or materially wrong, such as string conversion, replay, setdefault(), one-sided synchronization, or shared-code indirection.
scale.3: An exact narrow direct-assignment mutation is visibly executed or partially shown, but the resulting hunk remains incomplete, truncated, or otherwise ambiguous at the cutoff.
scale.4: A coherent source hunk visibly assigns the dynamic integer to both the field and existing widget while preserving the initializer, but post-edit evidence or final integrity inspection is limited.
scale.5: The coherent correct hunk is visible and its executable repository state is confirmed by source integrity inspection or successful target-form behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff-visible implementation progression

applies_when: The prefix contains inspection, execution, or editing related to Meta.ordering validation or models.E015.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score the strongest durable, cutoff-visible advance toward explaining or correcting the related-ordering failure: an exact task-specific reproduction with a supported mechanism, a focused applied source change, or post-change ordering-check evidence.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the latest applied candidate is directly contradicted by task-specific post-edit output and no later corrected candidate is applied, cap at 1. If execution fails before exposing models.E015 behavior, do not treat it as either product success or product failure.
metadata.evidence_authority: Use chronological precedence. Raw Model.check(), _check_ordering(), focused test, and final visible source output outrank narrative claims; a later restore supersedes an earlier edit, and a later task-specific failure supersedes an earlier success claim. Applied source content outranks a proposed patch. Dependency, import, settings, app-registration, and collection failures establish no ordering behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Equating setup-only exploration with an exact reproduction, crediting proposed work as applied work, retaining credit for a reverted edit, or overlooking that the active candidate still emits models.E015
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require post-change execution that visibly reaches Model.check(), _check_ordering(), or a collected focused ordering test. A source inspection or proposed test alone cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether visible work establishes a reusable causal fact or applies a focused correction, rather than merely locating code, proposing a future edit, or troubleshooting setup
metadata.oracle_test: Trace parent__pk through the reached model and compare the latest candidate with visible models.E015 output; for the highest anchor also inspect a malformed continuation such as parent__pk__missing or parent__field1__field2.
metadata.stage: Reproduce, implement, and validate the ordering-path correction

scale.1: The latest applied candidate is visibly disproved by a task-specific post-edit result with no later correction, or the trajectory claims product success from a command that never exercised ordering validation.
scale.2: Absent the level-1 contradiction: the work locates relevant code or states a plausible hypothesis, but shows neither a task-specific models.E015 result with a supported mechanism nor a concrete focused source edit.
scale.3: Absent the level-1 contradiction: the prefix establishes an exact failing models.E015 reproduction and correctly ties it to related-component resolution, or applies a syntactically coherent focused edit, but shows no authoritative post-change success for the latest source state.
scale.4: Absent the level-1 contradiction: post-change Model.check(), _check_ordering(), or a collected focused test visibly accepts related __pk, or a visibly disproved approach is replaced and the replacement succeeds; discriminative malformed-path validation is not yet shown.
scale.5: Absent the level-1 contradiction: the final visible candidate is connected through a coherent evidence chain to successful related-__pk execution and at least one task-causal negative boundary or transform-compatibility result.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific evidence produces durable causal progress

applies_when: A workspace diff, source edit, generated patch, backup, reject file, or proposed implementation artifact is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score whether the task-local implementation is present in an executable or applicable form and whether visible repository debris or source damage would obstruct evaluation.

metadata.failure_mode: No implementation artifact, malformed patch, syntax damage, missing production edit, tracked full-file backup, reject file, or substantial unrelated churn
metadata.judge_focus: Presence, applicability, syntax, and repository focus
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the visible diff or patch and verify that the intended base.py change can be executed or applied
metadata.stage: Review and produce the final artifact

scale.1: No concrete implementation artifact is present, or the visible artifact is malformed, destructive, syntactically invalid, or unusable.
scale.2: A coherent candidate exists but only as an unapplied patch or alongside substantial tracked backup, reject, duplicate-source, or unrelated debris.
scale.3: A syntactically coherent focused source edit is visible, with only limited cleanup or applicability concerns.
scale.4: The source edit or applicable patch is focused and clean, with no material repository damage or unrelated changes.
scale.5: The clean focused artifact is visibly reviewed and its final source state is confirmed by task-relevant execution.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implementation artifact is executable and focused

applies_when: A reproduction, candidate change, direct model check, or focused test for related '__pk' is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score direct observable evidence that a valid ordering path ending in the reached model's primary-key alias no longer produces models.E015.

metadata.failure_mode: The check still emits models.E015, the command fails before exercising the model check, or success is inferred only from query construction
metadata.judge_focus: Direct positive regression outcome
metadata.oracle_test: A Model.check() assertion or focused invalid_models_tests case for parent__pk

scale.1: No task-specific post-change result is shown.
scale.2: Only the pre-change failure is reproduced, the post-change result still fails, or setup prevents the ordering check from running.
scale.3: A direct Model.check() or equivalent assertion visibly shows no models.E015 for valid related '__pk', but focused repository validation is limited.
scale.4: A collected focused repository test for valid related '__pk' passes against the visible candidate.
scale.5: The focused regression passes after the final candidate together with discriminative negative and compatibility checks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Valid related primary-key ordering is demonstrated

applies_when: The prefix visibly inspects, proposes, patches, or edits the related-component loop in Model._check_ordering().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score the visible source semantics: related-path 'pk' must bind to the primary-key field of the model currently reached, relations may advance model traversal, and non-relational fields must end model traversal without discarding the last field needed for a subsequent transform.

metadata.failure_mode: String filtering, exception suppression, unconditional continue, universal id handling, stale model state, or same-component transform lookup
metadata.judge_focus: Current-model pk resolution and separation of model traversal from transform state
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the component loop and trace parent__pk, parent__field1__field2, and test__lower

scale.1: The visible candidate is unrelated or structurally wrong, universally skips ordinary names, or checks a successfully resolved field as its own transform.
scale.2: The relevant cause is recognized, but the candidate only skips or suppresses 'pk', filters ordering strings, retains stale traversal state, or lacks a concrete state-machine correction.
scale.3: A concrete candidate correctly implements one required state transition and visibly accounts for the other, but the complete state machine remains incomplete or ambiguous.
scale.4: The implementation visibly resolves 'pk' on the current traversal model, advances only through relations, clears model traversal after non-relations, and retains the last field for transforms.
scale.5: The complete state-machine implementation is visible and confirmed by positive, invalid-continuation, and registered-transform checks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Ordering-path state machine is implemented correctly

applies_when: A displayed implementation chooses how to copy `self.error_messages`.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates deviation from allocating a new top-level mapping while preserving the existing message value objects.

metadata.failure_mode: Recursive copying changes message-value identity or broadens copying beyond the required dictionary boundary
metadata.judge_focus: Shallow mapping isolation versus unnecessary recursive copying of lazy or specialized values
metadata.oracle_test: Use an identity-sensitive message value and verify that the mapping, but not the value, is duplicated

scale.1: No compatibility flaw is displayed: the implementation shallow-copies the complete mapping, or no mapping-copy implementation is applied.
scale.2: The expression is unusual but visibly preserves every value identity and isolates only the top-level mapping.
scale.3: The copy depth is ambiguous from the displayed source and evidence.
scale.4: The implementation visibly recursively deep-copies the mapping with the supplied memo.
scale.5: The implementation recursively copies message values without the supplied memo or visibly changes an identity-sensitive supported value.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recursive message-value copying

metadata.judge_focus: Memo registration, widget deepcopy, validator-list isolation, concrete-class preservation, return behavior, and valid tracked Python

scale.2: Only harmless ordering or formatting variation is displayed.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Established deepcopy regression

applies_when: Validation commands, assertions, or behavioral output are displayed.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates relevant executed evidence that the edited checkout, rather than a toy object or another installation, exhibits dictionary-level isolation.

metadata.judge_focus: Reached assertions for non-identity, preserved custom messages, and one-sided mutation isolation

scale.2: Validation is attempted but aborts before relevant behavior, uses an invalid API, or does not establish checkout provenance.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative checkout validation

applies_when: `Field.__deepcopy__()` source, a tracked diff, or actual copied-field behavior is displayed.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the tracked Django method gives the copied concrete field a distinct, complete top-level `error_messages` mapping containing every effective entry.

metadata.judge_focus: Applied whole-mapping isolation rather than reasoning, dictionary equality, or an unapplied patch
metadata.oracle_test: Deep-copy an actual custom Field subclass, assert concrete-type retention and mapping non-identity, then mutate one mapping only

scale.1: No applied relevant source change is displayed, or copied fields visibly retain the shared mapping.
scale.2: The defect is localized, but the displayed edit is unapplied, targets the wrong object, or copies only selected entries.
scale.3: A plausible whole-mapping assignment is displayed, but tracked application, complete content preservation, or concrete-field behavior is ambiguous.
