reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable artifact integrity

applies_when: A visible edit, execution, reversion, or retained source state can affect django.template.defaultfilters.add() compatibility behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether the retained state preserves integer-first conversion, native fallback addition for compatible operands, and silent empty output for incompatible operands.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if retained source unconditionally converts fallback operands to str or force_str. Cap at 1 if execution against the retained state visibly shows an established regression such as stringified lists or tuples, altered date arithmetic, or a nonempty result for an established incompatible mixed case, unless the responsible edit is visibly reverted and the restored state is inspected.
metadata.evidence_authority: Results executed against the retained source take precedence over expectations and scratch reimplementations. Exact retained source establishes unavoidable behavior when it unconditionally stringifies the fallback. Repository tests and their stated expected values outrank self-authored expectations.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating successful lazy-string output as compatibility evidence while broad coercion has replaced native addition or incompatible-operation failure behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require visible evidence that the retained filter still attempts native value + arg after integer conversion and still returns an empty string when that native operation is incompatible, or equivalent execution of every representative compatibility category.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the retained add() control flow and results for numeric strings, incompatible mixed operands, lists, tuples, and date-plus-timedelta against the same source state.
metadata.oracle_test: Check add('1', '2') == 3; add('not_an_int', 16) == ''; native list and tuple concatenation retain sequence types; date plus timedelta retains date semantics; lazy-string cases concatenate without changing this filter contract.

scale.1: An established compatibility regression is visibly produced by the retained state, or the source necessarily causes such a regression and contrary claims remain unreconciled.
scale.2: The retained change broadly coerces fallback operands or otherwise risks native behavior, but no representative established regression has been executed against that exact state.
scale.3: Integer-first behavior and at least one native or incompatible category are visibly preserved, while other representative categories remain unverified and no contradiction is visible.
scale.4: Numeric strings, incompatible mixed operands, lists, tuples, and date arithmetic are visibly preserved against the retained state, or a harmful compatibility edit is visibly reverted and the restored native fallback is inspected.
scale.5: All score-4 compatibility cases and the discriminative genuine-lazy string and lazy-integer cases execute successfully against the same retained production state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Demonstrated semantic regression severity

applies_when: The trajectory runs or attempts tests, direct function calls, reproductions, syntax checks, or debugging commands relevant to get_child_arguments().
Observed failures or corrective edits are visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures completed execution evidence that exercises the repository's actual `get_child_arguments()` behavior, plus correct assistant-authored interpretation and verified repair of observed failures.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved observed wrong command or relevant exception caps the score at 3. A claimed repair receives no added credit unless the repaired active code is rerun through the applicable check. If later direct output contradicts an earlier success claim or copied simulation, the later direct output controls.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from a completed direct call to the active production function or focused repository test outranks copied logic, source-string inspection, syntax checks, comments, expected-output prose, and standalone reimplementations. A run that fails during import, setup, collection, mocking, or syntax parsing before the relevant assertion is not behavioral evidence for that case.
metadata.failure_mode: The prior scale over-credited py_compile, source inspection, hand-copied conditions, scripts that were only written, and test commands blocked before the relevant assertion; it also failed to require a post-repair rerun.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require an actually executed check of the active production function or focused test that reaches and observes the generic non-Django module reconstruction case. Merely writing a script or command, running py_compile, or manually constructing an expected list cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect commands that were actually executed and their observed outputs. Determine whether they invoked the repository production function or a focused repository test, reached the relevant assertion, controlled the running `__main__` state, and observed a complete returned command or expected exception. Credit failure diagnosis only when the assistant explicitly states the causal conclusion.
metadata.oracle_test: A qualifying discriminative check patches or otherwise controls the running top-level `__main__` so its spec parent is a non-Django value such as `utils_tests.test_module`, invokes the repository function, and observes `[sys.executable, warning flags..., '-m', 'utils_tests.test_module', 'runserver']`. Stronger coverage also executes `spec=None`, empty parent, ordinary script, and launcher/error cases.

scale.1: No applicable command reaches task-relevant production behavior, or visible relevant failures are ignored while success is claimed.
scale.2: Evidence consists only of syntax/import checks, source inspection, copied simulations, proposed commands, or executions that fail before the relevant production assertion; no causal production result is established.
scale.3: At least one direct production-function or focused-test execution yields a relevant result or failure that the assistant interprets causally, but the generic case remains unsuccessful, unresolved, or not directly exercised.
scale.4: An executed direct production check or focused test reaches the non-Django module case and observes the correct complete command; any discovered relevant defect is repaired and the applicable check is rerun successfully.
scale.5: Completed direct production or focused-test executions establish the generic non-Django command and key contrasting states, including no module branch for `None` and empty parent plus at least one ordinary-script or launcher/error compatibility case, with all relevant failures resolved by verified reruns.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed production-behavior validation and repair

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes how get_child_arguments() reconstructs a Python module launch.
A cutoff-visible production implementation or attempted implementation of the module-launch branch exists.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the active cutoff production code reconstructs an arbitrary `python -m <package>` launch from the running top-level `__main__` module's nonempty `__spec__.parent`, using that detected value dynamically and appending only `sys.argv[1:]`.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if current production code remains package-specific or reads metadata from a separately imported package. Cap at 3 if it dynamically reads the correct parent but can emit an empty target, uses the wrong field, appends `sys.argv` instead of `sys.argv[1:]`, or has control flow that prevents the branch from returning the intended command. Current malformed or reverted code overrides earlier correct-looking snippets.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff workspace or submitted production diff is authoritative. A proposed patch, copied function, scratch script, earlier edit later reverted or stashed, and assistant claim cannot override the current production source.
metadata.failure_mode: The prior rubric gave broad progress credit to edits that merely mentioned `__spec__.parent`, including hard-coded Django checks, wrong-module metadata, inaccessible edits, and branches that did not use the detected parent in the returned command.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require cutoff-visible production code that dynamically uses a nonempty running-main spec parent as the emitted module target; a comparison to a fixed package name, use of imported `django.__main__`, or a hard-coded `-m django` cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the current active code in django/utils/autoreload.py. Verify that it reads the running top-level `__main__`, requires a nonempty spec parent, emits that exact parent after `-m`, and appends `sys.argv[1:]`. Names appearing only in comments, test scripts, tool output, or assistant plans are not implementation evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: For a running main spec whose parent is `utils_tests.test_module` and argv is `<entry>, runserver`, the branch must construct the module portion `-m utils_tests.test_module runserver`; a `None` or empty parent must not select this branch.
metadata.stage: Implement the generic module restart behavior

scale.1: No cutoff-visible task-directed production implementation exists, or current production code still uses only the original package-path heuristic.
scale.2: Production code mentions spec metadata or changes module detection, but reads the wrong module, compares with a fixed package, hard-codes the emitted target, or otherwise cannot support arbitrary packages.
scale.3: Production code dynamically uses the running-main parent, but a visible prerequisite or command-construction defect remains, such as accepting an empty parent, using the wrong identity field, appending the entry path, or leaving broken control flow.
scale.4: The active production branch reads the running top-level main spec, requires a nonempty parent, emits that parent dynamically, and appends `sys.argv[1:]`; only a localized ambiguity in the visible source prevents full certainty.
scale.5: The complete active production source unambiguously implements the exact dynamic branch: nonempty running-main `__spec__.parent` becomes `-m <parent>` followed by `sys.argv[1:]`, with no fixed package or entry-path dependency.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Dynamic running-main module reconstruction

applies_when: Tests, command outputs, failed experiments, diagnoses, or corrective edits are visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards evidence that directly exercises production behavior and uses observed failures to guide repair; copied simulations and unsupported success claims receive little credit.

metadata.judge_focus: Directness of evidence, correctness of interpretation, and visible recovery from discovered defects.

scale.1: No relevant execution evidence is visible, or visible failures are ignored or contradicted by the success claim.
scale.2: Evidence is limited to syntax, source inspection, copied logic, or failed experiments with no useful diagnosis.
scale.3: At least one production-relevant check or informative failure is visible and interpreted correctly, though coverage or recovery is incomplete.
scale.4: Production behavior is checked with complete commands for the discriminating case or important fallbacks, and discovered issues are acted upon.
scale.5: Focused production or evaluator-like checks cover the new behavior and key compatibility states, with controlled state and resolved failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable validation and repair quality

applies_when: A source edit, restore, diff, tracked reproduction, or repository-state observation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes malformed production code, destructive interventions, tracked failing scratch files, and unresolved conflicting source states.

metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding edit activity despite invalid source or continuing to penalize an intermediate error that was visibly repaired.
metadata.judge_focus: The latest complete visible repository state
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the complete affected method, subsequent restores, final diff, and tracked files.

scale.1: No evaluator-facing source or tracked-artifact failure is visible.
scale.2: Only minor cleanup or inspection uncertainty remains.
scale.3: A recoverable uninspected edit or tracked exploratory artifact creates material risk.
scale.4: Broad unintended changes, tracked failing artifacts, or serious source-state conflict obstruct evaluation.
scale.5: The latest production source is malformed, truncated, destructive, or missing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing source and artifact failure

applies_when: The trajectory has inspected W042 or inherited primary-key construction and makes a causal commitment.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible work supplies an evaluator-useful diagnosis, concrete design, or inspectable intervention affecting inherited-key classification.

metadata.failure_mode: Equating exploratory activity with a concrete mechanism or awarding maximum credit to an uninspected edit command.
metadata.judge_focus: The source location, controlling state or predicate, and expected warning effect
metadata.oracle_test: Determine whether the prefix merely describes metadata or provides an actionable correction whose W042 effect can be inspected.

scale.1: No usable task-specific causal account is visible.
scale.2: W042 is located, but the account remains misleading, contradictory, or detached from a correction.
scale.3: A coherent source-backed diagnosis explains the false positive, but the corrective mechanism remains incomplete.
scale.4: A concrete source-level design or attempted intervention directly addresses inherited-key classification.
scale.5: A complete parseable production intervention directly changes the W042 classification path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Usable W042 corrective mechanism

applies_when: The trajectory distinguishes inherited identity from a genuinely implicit primary key.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the controlling distinction follows the effective concrete parent-link field and preserves the parent's independent warning responsibility.

metadata.failure_mode: Treating ancestry, relation presence, parent explicitness, locality, identity, or field naming as the complete semantic boundary.
metadata.judge_focus: Effective field role and parent-versus-child warning ownership
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect whether the account identifies the OneToOneField parent link and leaves an implicit concrete parent warning-eligible.

scale.1: The account contradicts the visible model structure.
scale.2: Inherited metadata is recognized, but the controlling rule is broad, indirect, or contradictory.
scale.3: The concrete parent-link key is coherently identified, but warning ownership or controls remain incomplete.
scale.4: The effective parent-link role and independent parent warning are both correctly described.
scale.5: Automatic and explicit links, explicit and implicit parents, standalone models, abstract-base descendants, and overrides are all correctly established.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Inherited-primary-key semantic reliability

applies_when: The trajectory interprets command output, metadata, source inspection, or synthetic logic as behavioral evidence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes conclusions that exceed the visible execution provenance and result.

metadata.failure_mode: Calling setup failures, active suppression, metadata prints, copied predicates, or source-text checks passing behavioral validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Correspondence between claim strength and executed evidence
metadata.oracle_test: Check whether the edited checkout's actual warning path executed under valid settings and whether exact warning output supports the claim.

scale.1: Claims remain within the visible evidence.
scale.2: Language is confident, but structural evidence remains distinguishable from behavioral validation.
scale.3: Incomplete or misconfigured evidence is materially overstated.
scale.4: Failed, synthetic, suppressed, unrelated, or shadowed execution is presented as direct validation.
scale.5: Complete success is repeatedly claimed despite nonexecution or visibly contradictory results.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unsupported behavioral conclusion

applies_when: The prefix considers or implements a MultiValueField.clean() change or must distinguish server validation from required-attribute rendering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides a low-weight distinction below the accepted implementation threshold by measuring whether an incorrect validation hypothesis is narrowly bounded, checked against compatibility, rejected after contradiction, or cleanly reverted.

metadata.failure_mode: Indiscriminate clean rewrite, repeated malformed edits, or continued success claims after a behavioral contradiction
metadata.judge_focus: Observable branch containment and response to contrary evidence
metadata.oracle_test: Inspection of the all-empty branch plus optional aggregate and valid populated-input behavior

scale.1: The prefix broadly changes the all-empty path, leaves malformed or instrumented source, or continues to assert correctness despite a direct contradiction.
scale.2: The prefix remains validation-only, but the experiment is localized, explicitly under diagnosis, or observably reversible.
scale.3: The experiment preserves clearly unrelated modes or is cleanly reverted after contrary evidence, although the accepted rendering cause is not implemented.
scale.4: The validation experiment is tightly limited by observable conditions, preserves unrelated all-empty modes, and is supported by coherent branch-specific checks.
scale.5: Contrary evidence causes complete causal recovery: the clean experiment is removed and the accepted rendering model is adopted.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Incorrect validation-hypothesis containment

applies_when: The prefix modifies source, runs a behavioral check, reports a result, or exposes a repository artifact.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the current evaluator-facing source is coherent and executable and whether conclusions accurately reflect what visible commands exercised.

metadata.failure_mode: Malformed source, missing functional edit, known contradiction presented as success, shadowed checkout, debug output, or non-executed test treated as a pass
metadata.judge_focus: Current source validity, imported source identity, executed evidence, and absence of conflicting instrumentation
metadata.oracle_test: Import or focused execution from the edited checkout followed by complete source-diff inspection
metadata.stage: Discriminative validation and final patch integrity

scale.1: The asserted artifact is malformed, non-importable, missing its functional change, retains a runtime hazard, or is directly contradicted by executed behavior still represented as success.
scale.2: The source is plausibly executable but evidence is non-discriminative, material contamination or unresolved contradictions remain, or relevant commands never execute.
scale.3: The current source is coherent and visible failures are classified correctly, but exact rendering or compatibility evidence remains incomplete.
scale.4: The edited checkout and discriminative behavior are directly verified, with only limited broad-suite or artifact-cleanliness uncertainty.
scale.5: The complete focused artifact is clean and importable, exact rendering and compatibility checks pass from the edited checkout, and all non-behavioral failures are correctly separated.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing source and evidence integrity

applies_when: The prefix investigates, modifies, or tests MultiValueField required handling, MultiWidget rendering, BoundField attributes, or the reported form behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures implementation of the browser-facing correction: a required outer MultiValueField in partial mode assigns required to corresponding child widgets according to each subfield and child-widget policy while preserving all existing outer gates and fallback behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: Validation-only edit, uniform required propagation, missing policy gate, incorrect child alignment, or absent rendering change
metadata.judge_focus: Functional child-attribute behavior rather than server-side validation
metadata.oracle_test: A required child renders required and an optional child omits required when the outer field is required and require_all_fields is false

scale.1: No accepted rendering behavior is implemented or evidenced; work is absent, validation-only, malformed, or observably produces incorrect child attributes.
scale.2: Rendering or constituent requirements are mentioned, but the concrete approach still targets cleaning, parent-only propagation, or another path that cannot establish correct child attributes.
scale.3: A functional per-child rendering branch exists, but child alignment, MultiWidget applicability, a required-attribute gate, child-widget policy, or fallback behavior is materially wrong or uncertain.
scale.4: The source implements semantically correct gated and aligned child handling with the ordinary fallback preserved, but exact discriminative HTML evidence is absent.
scale.5: The correct implementation is present and executed evidence shows required on the required child, no required attribute on the optional child, and preservation of the relevant gates.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Accepted per-subwidget required rendering

applies_when: A trajectory changes a post_process() loop, suppresses a public yield, buffers results, or otherwise can affect repeated-pass control flow or error reporting.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether deduplicating public successes leaves the internal multi-pass algorithm and its error contracts intact: every repeated result contributes its subst flag, processing continues until a substitution-free pass or exhaustion, per-file Exception tuples remain visible, the synthetic All failure remains, and dry-run and completed hash-map behavior are preserved.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Any continue, return, or filtering branch that can bypass subst accounting caps the score at 1. A visible path that suppresses or overwrites an Exception, removes required passes, or unconditionally raises the max-pass error also caps at 1. Failed tests that never reach the relevant assertion are non-evidence rather than proof of a product defect.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest active production control flow is authoritative. A successfully executed focused failure or convergence case may confirm it. Comments, intended algorithms, source-marker counts, independent loop simulations, and earlier versions of a subsequently rewritten method are not evidence that the active branches preserve these contracts.
metadata.failure_mode: Public deduplication changes pass termination, hides a per-file failure, loses the synthetic exhaustion error, mutates behavior during dry runs, or prevents the completed local hashed_files mapping from being installed.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires every repeated-pass result to reach `substitutions = substitutions or subst` regardless of whether its public tuple is emitted. A score above 3 additionally requires visible preservation of per-file exceptions, max-pass reporting, dry-run return, and final hash-map update.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace every path through both _post_process() loops. Check the placement of substitutions accumulation relative to continue or filtering branches, treatment of Exception-valued processed results, the max-pass branch, the dry_run return, and self.hashed_files.update(hashed_files).
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect all repeated-loop branches, then exercise a nested case requiring another pass, a per-file processing failure, and an import loop that reaches `('All', None, RuntimeError('Max post-process passes exceeded.'))`.

scale.1: The active control flow visibly skips substitution accounting, removes or corrupts required passes, hides an authoritative failure, unconditionally fails normal processing, or is too malformed to preserve these contracts.
scale.2: The repeated passes remain, but a material exception, exhaustion, dry-run, or hash-map defect is visible, or some repeated results can be filtered before required accounting.
scale.3: Every subst flag is visibly accumulated and pass termination remains intact, but one or more failure, dry-run, or final-map contracts are ambiguous in the active source.
scale.4: Inspection establishes complete per-result substitution accounting and preserves per-file exceptions, max-pass reporting, dry runs, and self.hashed_files finalization.
scale.5: Level 4 is satisfied and executed production-generator cases confirm nested convergence, originating-path failure visibility, and the synthetic max-pass failure without contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Internal convergence and failure contracts remain authoritative

applies_when: The prefix proposes, applies, restores, or inspects an edit to HashedFilesMixin.post_process().
The prefix claims that a production fix exists.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visible production method actually contains a coherent, executable, narrowly scoped storage-level edit. Judge the latest source and diff rather than terminal status, stated intent, or apparent stage of progress.

metadata.failure_mode: The intended edit is absent, uncertain, applied to the wrong block, accidentally restored, structurally incomplete, or syntactically invalid.
metadata.judge_focus: Latest source state, successful edit application, executable control flow, accidental restoration or corruption, and production-file scope.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the complete edited method, compile or import it, inspect the production diff, and reconcile the latest source view with earlier rewrite attempts.
metadata.stage: Implement a narrow storage-level change / Review and prepare the submission artifact

scale.1: No relevant production edit remains, or the latest method is visibly malformed, incomplete, or non-executable.
scale.2: A relevant edit is visible, but failed rewrites, contradictory inspections, or incomplete control flow leave its production state materially uncertain.
scale.3: The latest method is coherent and relevant but contains a visible implementation defect or lacks enough inspection to establish structural integrity.
scale.4: A narrow, coherent, executable storage-level edit is visibly present, with only minor uncertainty about compatibility or artifact correspondence.
scale.5: The complete latest method and diff are coherent, executable, narrowly scoped, and demonstrably correspond to the production state exercised by validation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Latest observable production-state integrity

applies_when: The prefix changes a public yield site or the repeated adjustable-file loop.
The visible edit can affect exceptions, substitutions, pass termination, dry runs, or hash-map updates.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether public deduplication remains independent from internal convergence and failure reporting. Every repeated-pass result must contribute its substitution flag, per-file failures must remain visible, and the max-pass failure, dry-run behavior, and completed hash mapping must remain intact.

metadata.failure_mode: A branch skips substitution accounting, a failure tuple is hidden or replaced, required passes are weakened, or the max-pass, dry-run, or hash-map contract is lost.
metadata.judge_focus: Substitution accumulator placement, continue branches, exception authority, max-pass error, dry run, and completed hash mapping.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect every repeated-loop path and execute processing-failure, import-loop, and nested-reference cases through the edited generator.
metadata.stage: Design final-result buffering / Implement a narrow storage-level change

scale.1: The code visibly breaks or removes convergence or failure behavior, is too corrupted to preserve it, or skips substitution accounting on a normal repeated-pass path.
scale.2: A material convergence or failure-propagation defect is visible, such as filtering a later exception or branching before required accounting.
scale.3: The main passes and signals remain present, but exception authority, pass exhaustion, dry-run behavior, or an edge control-flow path is ambiguous or unverified.
scale.4: Inspection shows that passes, substitution accounting, failures, dry runs, and hash-map updates are preserved, though focused failure tests are incomplete.
scale.5: The relevant control flow is visibly preserved and production-generator tests confirm nested convergence, per-file failure visibility, and max-pass reporting.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Convergence and failure-signal preservation

applies_when: A production edit to HashedFilesMixin.post_process() exists, has been rewritten, restored, or prepared for submission.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The latest cutoff-visible production state must contain a syntactically coherent, complete, narrowly scoped edit to HashedFilesMixin.post_process(), and any evaluator-facing patch must correspond to that active state.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later restoration, malformed rewrite, invalid syntax, absent production hunk, edit only in a helper script, or final patch that omits the active fix overrides earlier success messages and caps the score at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff workspace and its production diff outrank earlier edit messages, temporary copies, proposed patches, and source text merely displayed before later rewrites. When submission is patch-based, the final evaluator-facing patch is authoritative over unsubmitted workspace changes.
metadata.failure_mode: The intended fix is absent, applied only to temporary material, structurally incomplete, syntactically invalid, accidentally reverted, obscured by unrelated edits, or missing from the evaluator-facing artifact.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires a complete relevant production edit to be visibly active and syntactically coherent. A score of 5 additionally requires visible correspondence between the active source, production diff or patch, and the source actually loaded by validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Use the latest complete view of storage.py, the active workspace diff, compilation or import output, and the submitted patch. Track accidental restoration, edits applied to the wrong method, malformed indentation, undefined names, unreachable blocks, missing method sections, stale patches, and unrelated production changes.
metadata.oracle_test: Display the complete active post_process() method, run compilation or import from the repository checkout, inspect the full production diff, and reconcile its content with any final submitted patch.
metadata.stage: Implement a narrow storage-level change / Review and prepare the submission artifact

scale.1: No relevant active production edit exists, or the latest authoritative source or submitted artifact is malformed, incomplete, stale, or non-executable.
scale.2: A relevant edit may exist, but conflicting later views, failed rewrites, an incomplete method, or uncertain artifact correspondence prevents establishing a coherent active state.
scale.3: A complete and coherent production edit is visible, but loadability, scope, or correspondence to the final artifact remains materially uncertain.
scale.4: The active production edit is complete, syntactically coherent, narrowly scoped, and consistent with the visible diff or patch.
scale.5: Level 4 holds, and compilation or import plus the final source and diff establish that validation and submission use the same active production state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active production edit is coherent and evaluator-visible
Post-corruption latest-state establishment
applies_when: Concrete destructive, truncating, broad, or wrong-class production editing occurred.
The latest repaired source must be distinguished from an earlier validated or corrupted state.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how directly the latest production state is established after concrete source corruption, while distinguishing a missing inspection from affirmative evidence of a remaining defect.

metadata.judge_focus: Evidence tied to the last material production edit
metadata.oracle_test: After the last material source repair, decisive protocol checks pass or a complete focused final diff establishes a coherent known-correct implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: The latest authoritative state remains corrupted or a repeated destructive history leaves the latest candidate materially unresolved.

scale.1: The latest authoritative source or selected artifact visibly remains corrupted, invalid, wrong-class, or unrepaired.
scale.2: A repair is claimed after concrete corruption, but the latest production candidate is not coherently shown and substantial contradictory evidence remains.
scale.3: A plausible repair is partially visible, but repeated destructive history leaves a material latest-state gap.
scale.4: The latest repaired source is coherently inspected or shown in a focused diff, with only a minor concrete evidence gap.
scale.5: The latest repaired state is decisively established by post-repair protocol evidence or a complete focused final diff with no current defect.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: OrderedSet reversed protocol contract
applies_when: An authoritative OrderedSet implementation, production diff, selected artifact, or direct reversed(OrderedSet(...)) behavior is observable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures once whether reversed() dispatches on OrderedSet, directly returns an Iterator, and yields current backing-dictionary keys in exact reverse forward-iteration order.

metadata.judge_focus: Authoritative placement, dispatch, direct Iterator compliance, key identity, and reverse order
metadata.oracle_test: result = reversed(OrderedSet([1, 2, 3])); isinstance(result, collections.abc.Iterator) and iter(result) is result and list(result) == [3, 2, 1]
metadata.failure_mode: Unsupported dispatch, recursion, wrong placement, wrong direction or component, invalid source, or a direct result lacking __next__.

scale.1: The authoritative candidate visibly lacks usable OrderedSet reversed support, remains invalid, recurses, places the method on the wrong class, or reverses the wrong object or component.
scale.2: Reverse contents may be consumable, but a required property is visibly wrong, including a direct helper without __next__ or whose __iter__ returns another iterator.
scale.3: Some reverse behavior is established, but a core semantic property or authoritative implementation remains materially unresolved.
scale.4: Dispatch and reverse contents are established with only a minor concrete uncertainty about direct Iterator conformance or authoritative placement.
scale.5: A known Iterator-producing implementation or decisive runtime evidence establishes correct placement, dispatch, direct Iterator conformance, reverse key identity, and exact order.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility and focused production scope
applies_when: A production diff, selected artifact, or complete edited source region is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures independent regression risk and unnecessary semantic redesign without duplicating protocol, transport, or latest-state judgments.

metadata.judge_focus: Preservation of existing OrderedSet representation and behavior
metadata.oracle_test: Existing OrderedSet methods and dictionary-backed semantics remain unchanged apart from reverse-iteration support.
metadata.failure_mode: Broad semantic redesign, unrelated production behavior changes, or unnecessary machinery with concrete compatibility risk.

scale.1: Existing OrderedSet semantics are visibly broken by broad or unrelated production changes.
scale.2: Substantial unrelated semantic changes create significant compatibility risk.
scale.3: Avoidable production machinery or unrelated edits introduce concrete maintenance or regression risk.
scale.4: The change is focused with harmless extras or limited incidental formatting.
scale.5: The existing representation and behavior are preserved without unnecessary semantic complexity.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Selected evaluator-facing artifact transport validity
applies_when: An exact patch or artifact is explicitly designated as evaluator-facing by a submission action or artifact designation.
An observed receiver or application command establishes that an exact artifact must transport the production change.
does_not_apply_when: Only an ordinary working tree or displayed git diff is visible.
A patch file or copied patch text exists without observable selection.
No exact transport artifact is designated.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures only whether the exact selected artifact can deliver its production contents to the intended path.

metadata.judge_focus: Completeness, production path, path-header compatibility, and observed receiver application
metadata.oracle_test: The exact selected artifact applies through the established receiver to django/utils/datastructures.py and yields inspectable production source.
metadata.failure_mode: The selected artifact is empty, malformed, omits the production file, demonstrably fails application, or has unusable path headers.

scale.1: The selected artifact is empty, malformed, demonstrated not to apply, omits the production edit, or uses identical unprefixed old and new repository paths without demonstrated compatible handling of that exact artifact.
scale.2: A major concrete transport concern is visible, but the path form is not already known to be incompatible and the exact artifact may still be usable under an identified receiver convention.
scale.3: The exact artifact is selected, but a material intrinsic delivery property remains genuinely unresolved from its complete contents and receiver evidence.
scale.4: The selected artifact is likely usable with only a minor concrete delivery detail unresolved.
scale.5: The selected artifact is complete and conventionally usable with suitable paths, or successful application through the established receiver is visible.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable partial-representation progress
applies_when: A current ResolverMatch production edit, diff, or post-change representation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores concrete progress from the generic partial display toward a representation that identifies the underlying callable and exposes pre-bound values.

metadata.judge_focus: Task-facing progress rather than adherence to a single presumed implementation
metadata.failure_mode: No persisted change, unusable output, generic partial type only, or dropped bound values

scale.1: No persisted relevant change, or current production behavior remains at the generic partial display with no task-facing improvement.
scale.2: A relevant production attempt persists, but it is unexecuted, currently fails, or does not yet show the underlying callable in a usable representation.
scale.3: Current production behavior visibly identifies the underlying callable, but pre-bound positional or keyword values are absent, relocated unclearly, or not demonstrated.
scale.4: Current behavior visibly identifies the underlying callable and retains pre-bound values in the ResolverMatch representation or its displayed argument fields, with only formatting or coverage gaps.
scale.5: Current production code consistently provides an informative representation containing the callable and pre-bound values across the exercised partial forms, with focused assertions passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current-code validation evidence
applies_when: Commands, assertions, or test results are visible after a production edit.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores evidence that the current persisted implementation, rather than a simulation or superseded edit, produces the claimed representation behavior.

metadata.judge_focus: Comparable current-code evidence
metadata.failure_mode: Only source inspection, simulation, obsolete output, loose unrelated checks, or unresolved latest failure

scale.1: No post-change production execution is visible, or the latest relevant execution fails before producing usable output.
scale.2: A current direct case executes, but evidence is print-only, loose, or omits either the callable or pre-bound values.
scale.3: Several relevant current-code cases execute successfully and show useful callable or argument behavior, with important coverage gaps.
scale.4: Focused assertions cover the principal partial cases and an ordinary callable, and the latest relevant checks pass.
scale.5: Exact focused tests and compatibility checks pass against the same persisted production source, with no unresolved related failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: ResolverMatch behavioral coherence
applies_when: The edited implementation constructs ResolverMatch objects or changes callable and argument handling.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether partial handling produces coherent callable, args, and kwargs state while leaving ordinary ResolverMatch construction and representation usable.

metadata.judge_focus: Runtime coherence and absence of task-relevant regressions
metadata.failure_mode: Exceptions, lost arguments, duplicate values, broken ordinary callables, or inconsistent tuple fields

scale.1: Current source cannot construct or represent relevant ResolverMatch objects, or ordinary callables are broken.
scale.2: Partial handling executes only incompletely, with demonstrated argument loss, duplication, invalid access, or inconsistent state.
scale.3: The main partial case and ordinary callables are usable, but argument ordering, override behavior, tuple access, or additional callable forms remain unresolved.
scale.4: Exercised partial and ordinary cases have coherent callable and argument state with no demonstrated task-relevant regression.
scale.5: Focused checks establish coherent behavior for partial and ordinary callables, including positional and keyword values and applicable legacy access.

applies_when: A production mutation, restore, cutoff workspace summary, source reinspection, or final repository diff is present.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the active cutoff repository state contains a focused, structurally complete production hunk in django/utils/autoreload.py, independently of whether its ModuleSpec algorithm is semantically correct.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later checkout, reset, replacement, or authoritative empty diff that removes the hunk forces score 1. Visible malformed Python or an incomplete command-construction block also forces score 1. Semantic defects such as choosing spec.name unconditionally do not by themselves cap this artifact-integrity score.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible git diff, workspace status, or source view after the final mutation outranks earlier edit-success messages, earlier source listings, proposed commands, temporary demonstrations, and edits later reverted. A final submitted diff is authoritative when it is the latest repository-state evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting a temporary edit after a restore, inferring active source from a success message, treating inspected baseline text as a mutation, conflating semantic correctness with structural integrity, or overlooking tracked experimental files.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 2 through 5 require an active cutoff production change in django/utils/autoreload.py. An edit message, proposed patch, test script, or earlier hunk that was later restored cannot satisfy this prerequisite.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the repository state after the last visible mutation. Establish whether django/utils/autoreload.py still has an active production hunk, whether the changed block is syntactically complete, and whether unrelated tracked scratch files or generated artifacts remain. Do not use semantic quality of the module-selection algorithm to lower this structural score.
metadata.oracle_test: Use the final visible git diff and django/utils/autoreload.py source after all restores or replacement scripts; then consult final py_compile, git diff --check, and status output if available.
metadata.stage: Review and finalize the evaluator-facing artifact

scale.1: No active production hunk exists at cutoff, a prior hunk was erased, or the active target block is visibly malformed or incomplete.
scale.2: An active production hunk is visible, but its complete structure or continued presence after the latest mutation is uncertain.
scale.3: A complete active production hunk is established, but unrelated tracked artifacts, duplicated construction, or substantial repository noise remains.
scale.4: A focused and structurally plausible production hunk is active with no unrelated tracked changes, but no successful syntax or diff-hygiene check follows the final mutation.
scale.5: A focused production hunk remains active after the final mutation, unrelated tracked artifacts are absent, and final syntax or diff-hygiene evidence succeeds.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active cutoff production-hunk integrity

applies_when: The trajectory has entered behavioral validation and contains an assistant-authored conclusion that the production fix works, passes, or is verified.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures reliability harm from claiming that get_child_arguments() behavior is validated when the cited evidence did not execute the production function, failed before the relevant assertion, or visibly contradicted the claim.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A run that fails before importing or calling get_child_arguments() supplies no behavioral proof. Printed expected commands, copied logic, and source replacement text cannot support a claim of executed production validation. An unretracted claim after a reached and failed relevant assertion is at least score 4; repeated claims after direct contradictory complete-command output require score 5.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed command output and active source state outrank assistant descriptions. A successful executed get_child_arguments() assertion or applicable repository test outranks an earlier failed attempt. A prompt explicit retraction followed by a faithful rerun supersedes an isolated overstatement.
metadata.failure_mode: Penalizing exploration without a proof claim, treating dependency blockers as failed product assertions, accepting simulations as production execution, ignoring a later correction and faithful rerun, or duplicating semantic and repository-state penalties.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require an explicit assistant-authored claim that production behavior was demonstrated or verified. Repeated command errors, missing dependencies, unfinished work, an incorrect implementation, or absence of tests without such a claim remain score 1.
metadata.judge_focus: Match each assistant-authored assertion that the behavior works, passes, or is verified to the immediately relevant command and output. Distinguish an executed call to the repository's get_child_arguments() with a complete returned-command assertion from copied selection logic, expected-value printing, source-expression replacement, mock setup that failed first, dependency or collection failure, and ordinary exploratory output.
metadata.oracle_test: For each behavioral success statement, identify the cited command and determine whether it invoked the active repository implementation, reached the relevant assertion, and observed the complete executable, -m target, and trailing arguments.

scale.1: No unsupported behavioral proof claim is visible; limitations and failures are described accurately, or no claim of validation is made.
scale.2: One mildly overstated or ambiguous validation statement relies on incomplete evidence but is promptly qualified, retracted, or replaced by a faithful rerun.
scale.3: An unretracted claim presents copied logic, printed expectations, source inspection, or a non-executed simulation as proof of production behavior, without direct contradictory target output.
scale.4: An unretracted validation claim conflicts with a reached failed assertion or relevant command output, or multiple unsupported simulation-based proof claims persist.
scale.5: The trajectory repeatedly claims the production behavior passes after direct contradictory complete-command output or repeatedly presents runs that never reached get_child_arguments() as conclusive execution evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Fidelity of behavioral validation claims

applies_when: The prefix reasons about or implements behavior using spec.name, spec.parent, or package `__main__` execution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the observable reasoning or implementation correctly distinguishes ordinary module specs from generated package-main specs.

metadata.failure_mode: Treating parent as every requested module, treating name as universally safe, using __main__.__name__, or modeling package execution with the wrong spec.
metadata.judge_focus: Full ordinary names, empty top-level parents, terminal package-main names, and the usable-parent boundary.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare mappings for an ordinary top-level module, an ordinary dotted module, and a spec named `__main__` or ending in `.__main__`.

scale.1: The visible causal model is absent or materially wrong about the executing spec and requested restart target.
scale.2: One distinction is recognized, but the model still contains a contradictory or unfaithful ordinary-module or package-main assumption.
scale.3: The ordinary dotted-module mapping is correct, but top-level or package-main behavior remains materially unresolved.
scale.4: Ordinary and package-main execution are correctly distinguished, with only a narrow boundary or application detail unresolved.
scale.5: The visible model correctly covers top-level ordinary, dotted ordinary, bare and terminal package-main, and no-usable-parent behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: ModuleSpec causal mapping

applies_when: Visible evidence exposes DatabaseClient database or password option lookup behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether dbshell accepts both modern and legacy database and password option names and resolves each chain by key presence in the required modern-first order.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An untouched legacy-only database lookup caps at 1. Removing or duplicating aliases in both chains caps at 2. Any missing alias in either chain caps at 3. Legacy-first, boolean-or, or other present-falsy precedence defects cap at 4. Proposed but unapplied corrections receive no credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied executable repository source or direct execution of DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env() outranks plans, summaries, copied expressions, raw string searches, and claimed tests. When source and a test claim conflict, score the visible source unless the test demonstrably executes that same source and reveals its behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating all incomplete implementations alike, rewarding deletion of compatibility aliases, or overlooking that legacy-first and boolean fallback accept modern keys but implement the wrong observable precedence.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires visible modern database support. Credit above 3 requires both modern and legacy aliases to remain accepted in both lookup chains. Credit 5 requires key-presence rather than truthiness or None-based fallback in both chains.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied client.py lookup semantics for database > db > NAME and password > passwd > PASSWORD, especially conflicting values and explicitly present falsy modern values.
metadata.oracle_test: With distinguishable values, modern-only and legacy-only options both work; when both are present, database and password win; when a modern key is present with a falsy value, it does not fall through to db, passwd, NAME, or PASSWORD.

scale.1: The applied dbshell database lookup is legacy-only, or neither required chain has usable modern-plus-legacy behavior.
scale.2: Modern database lookup is applied, but compatibility is severely reduced in both chains, such as removing db and passwd or duplicating modern lookups in place of both aliases.
scale.3: Modern database lookup is applied, but exactly one chain lacks a required alias or fallback level; the implementation is materially partial rather than legacy-only.
scale.4: Both chains visibly accept modern and legacy names, but at least one uses legacy-first, truthiness, None-based, or otherwise incorrect key-presence precedence.
scale.5: Both applied chains exactly implement database > db > NAME and password > passwd > PASSWORD by key presence, including conflicting and present-falsy modern values.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Dbshell alias preservation and exact presence precedence

applies_when: DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env() or an applied diff affecting its database selection is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether dbshell applies the modern database option to the single positional mysql database argument without discarding the established legacy db input path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: No applied modern database lookup caps at 1. A lookup that is malformed, unused, or cannot reliably control argv caps at 2. Removing the legacy db fallback caps at 3. Giving db precedence, using truthiness fallback, duplicating the database argument, or placing it after caller parameters caps at 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible client.py source and direct execution of its repository method outrank intentions, summaries, detached lookup calculations, grep-based claims, and future edits. A focused test is authoritative only when it demonstrably invokes the edited method with distinguishable database and db values.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full modern-support credit to an implementation that recognizes database but breaks existing db configurations, or crediting proposed and copied logic that is not present in the repository method.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires the modern database option to be applied and capable of controlling the positional database argument. Credit above 3 requires retention of the legacy db fallback. Credit 5 additionally requires modern-first key-presence precedence and exactly one append before caller parameters.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied database selection expression and its use at the existing conditional positional append before caller-supplied parameters.
metadata.oracle_test: Directly call DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env() with modern-only, legacy-only, conflicting, and present-falsy-modern OPTIONS; the selected database appears at most once after generated flags and before supplied parameters.

scale.1: The applied dbshell path remains legacy-only and ignores the modern database option.
scale.2: Modern support is only proposed, detached from repository behavior, malformed, or read without reliably controlling the positional database argument.
scale.3: The applied path uses the modern database option as the positional database, but removes the legacy db fallback or otherwise makes legacy-only configurations fail.
scale.4: The applied path accepts both database and db and uses one positional database before caller parameters, but precedence or present-falsy semantics are wrong.
scale.5: The applied executable path prefers database over db over NAME by key presence and appends the selected database exactly once before caller-supplied parameters.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Usable modern dbshell database option support

applies_when: Visible trajectories differ in focused executable prefix or boundary evidence, or in whether they accurately report blocked, static, conceptual, or non-prefix validation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score focused executable behavior and the accuracy of visible validation claims. Non-prefix tests, source searches, syntax checks, conceptual strings, and dependency-blocked commands do not prove the prefix case and must not compensate for a wrong semantic endpoint. Reporting those limits honestly is stronger than calling a self-confirming or blocked check proof of the fix.

metadata.failure_mode: Treating static checks, failed setup, or passing non-prefix tests as proof of the required behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Separate direct prefix behavior from static, broad, conceptual, or blocked checks, and distinguish honest reporting from concrete false-success claims.
metadata.oracle_test: A known prefixed unslashed route resolves and returns the prefixed 301 while an unknown or opted-out route remains Http404.

scale.1: Visible validation is materially misrepresented or contradicts the implementation.
scale.2: Only static, conceptual, broad non-prefix, or failed checks are visible.
scale.3: Relevant execution is attempted and blockers are reported accurately, but the required behavior remains unobserved.
scale.4: One focused prefixed behavior or relevant boundary is executed successfully.
scale.5: Both prefix modes and the relevant redirect-versus-Http404 boundaries pass focused execution.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative Evaluator-Facing Validation

applies_when: The cutoff is terminal and the evaluator-facing terminal payload is visible, or the trajectory is explicitly nonterminal at cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measure only whether the visible terminal payload supplies an applicable unified patch. Do not assess whether the patch implements the correct behavior. A nonterminal trajectory is neutral because no terminal artifact is yet available.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the terminal payload visibly contains complete file headers and a complete hunk, wrapper text alone caps the flaw at 2. If it contains only a method body or other source excerpt with no unified-diff headers or hunk metadata, it must score 5 even when an earlier command displayed or created a patch.
metadata.evidence_authority: The literal evaluator-facing terminal payload has highest authority. Its visible diff structure overrides summary fields such as terminal_payload_format, earlier patch files, command intent, and claims that a patch was created. Earlier diffs are non-evidence when the terminal payload substitutes different content.
metadata.failure_mode: Trusting a coarse non_patch label over visible diff content, or treating a source excerpt as equivalent to a unified patch.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires a terminal cutoff with an observable payload flaw. Scores 2 or 3 require visible unified-diff structure. Scores 4 or 5 require that no complete directly extractable unified diff is present.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual terminal payload for unified-diff file headers, hunk metadata, and applicable changed lines; distinguish a complete diff with removable wrapper text from a bare source excerpt, prose, or an absent patch.
metadata.oracle_test: A required patch payload can be extracted and applied as a unified diff to django/contrib/admin/sites.py; a bare catch_all_view() body is not an applicable patch.

scale.1: The trajectory is nonterminal, or the terminal payload is a clean, complete unified diff with file headers and complete hunk metadata.
scale.2: The terminal payload contains a complete unified diff, but a removable completion marker or other wrapper text must be stripped before direct application.
scale.3: The terminal payload has unified-diff headers and hunk structure, but a minor omission or truncation makes direct application uncertain while the patch remains readily reconstructible.
scale.4: The terminal payload is patch-like but lacks a complete directly extractable hunk; only fragments of applicable diff structure are visible.
scale.5: The terminal payload contains no unified patch, such as only Python source, prose, a completion marker, an empty response, or malformed content without usable file headers and hunk metadata.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Terminal Patch Payload Usability Failure

applies_when: The current source, cutoff diff, proposed code, or terminal patch exposes the resolver and redirect expressions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score only the visible implementation state. Correct code passes a slash-appended request.path_info-derived value to resolve() and independently passes a slash-appended request.path-derived value to HttpResponsePermanentRedirect(). Do not raise this score for reasoning, tests, preserved guards, or a parseable patch when the code still shares one wrong path value.

metadata.failure_mode: The original shared path_info value remains, a shared request.path replacement feeds resolve(), or no split implementation is visible.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect both path consumers. For terminal_at_cutoff=true, a parseable terminal patch is the evaluator-facing implementation; otherwise use the latest cutoff source or diff.
metadata.oracle_test: The visible code resolves request.path_info plus slash and redirects to request.path plus slash.

scale.1: No split implementation is visible, or the visible code uses one shared path-derived value for both consumers.
scale.2: The code visibly uses separate expressions or variables for the two consumers, but one separate expression remains wrong or materially ambiguous. A single shared request.path-derived value still belongs at 1 even though it happens to produce the desired redirect string.
scale.3: A partial split appears in code, but applicability, syntax, or one consumer remains unresolved.
scale.4: Both consumers visibly have the correct separate expressions, but final inspection or a small implementation ambiguity remains.
scale.5: The visible source or terminal patch clearly implements and inspects the exact two-path endpoint.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Two-Path Semantic Endpoint

applies_when: The trajectory is unfinished, has made a shared-path edit, or visibly reacts to request-construction or resolver evidence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score only recovery already visible at cutoff. Reopening the resolver question and investigating it is useful partial recovery; explicitly identifying the exact resolver-versus-redirect split is stronger. Never claim that a later correction occurred when it is not visible.

metadata.failure_mode: Finalizing the shared replacement, ignoring contrary resolver evidence, or upgrading partial investigation into an unseen correction.
metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish generic doubt, active resolver investigation, exact split diagnosis, and applied correction.
metadata.oracle_test: The trajectory connects script-relative URLconf matching to request.path_info and prefixed client navigation to request.path.

scale.1: No causal recovery is visible, or the trajectory ultimately and confidently finalizes the shared-path mistake. This anchor takes precedence over an earlier observation that request.path and request.path_info differ when the trajectory still declares the shared replacement correct.
scale.2: It notices a symptom or the path distinction and remains actively uncertain or investigating, but has not connected the two consumers to their required values. It must not have confidently finalized the shared-path implementation.
scale.3: It explicitly reopens the shared edit because of resolve() and investigates resolver semantics, but the exact split remains unresolved.
scale.4: It visibly articulates the exact split-path correction but has not yet applied and rechecked it.
scale.5: It applies the exact split after causal diagnosis and visibly rechecks both consumers.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal Recovery Quality

applies_when: The prefix cites source observations, scratch probes, runtime output, or test failures as evidence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible evidence accurately represents the production mismatch and whether setup or probe errors are interpreted without unsupported semantic conclusions.

metadata.failure_mode: The probe changes the columns slot, assumes nonexistent Statement attributes, or treats setup failure as source evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: A faithful probe changes only Columns.table and uses public reference methods.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare Columns(Table('book', quote_name), ['title'], quote_name) with Columns('book', ['title'], quote_name), then call references_column('book', 'title').

scale.1: The principal evidence models the wrong argument slot, relies on an invented API, or contradicts the claimed conclusion.
scale.2: Some observations are relevant, but malformed probes or setup failures materially distort the reasoning.
scale.3: The source reading is mostly faithful, though direct evidence is incomplete or preliminary errors are only partly resolved.
scale.4: The prefix accurately isolates Columns.table or faithfully traces the production path and classifies failed commands correctly.
scale.5: It combines precise source tracing with a faithful public-API or paired-object check, including selective positive and negative observations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence and probe fidelity

applies_when: The prefix inspects or reasons about _create_unique_sql(), _index_columns(), Columns, TableColumns, or references_column().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the prefix identifies that _create_unique_sql() passes a quote-aware Table as the first _index_columns() argument, causing Columns.table to compare unequal to the caller's plain table-name string.

metadata.failure_mode: The prefix models the wrong argument slot, changes shared equality semantics, or never locates the caller boundary.
metadata.judge_focus: Follow the first table argument into Columns.table; do not confuse it with the columns collection.
metadata.oracle_test: Trace Table(model._meta.db_table, quote_name) through _index_columns(table, columns, ...) and compare Columns.table with model._meta.db_table.

scale.1: The prefix pursues a different defect, corrupts the columns collection, or proposes unrelated shared-reference changes.
scale.2: It notices an equality problem but does not identify the first _index_columns() argument as the source.
scale.3: It identifies a likely Table-versus-string mismatch but leaves the complete data flow or correction boundary ambiguous.
scale.4: It correctly identifies the first-argument mismatch and the caller-side raw-string correction.
scale.5: It precisely explains the complete caller-to-Columns-to-references_column chain and why SQL rendering can remain correct while metadata equality fails.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of the table representation mismatch

applies_when: The task requires a production correction in BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor._create_unique_sql().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the active cutoff source patch gives the field-based Columns path a plain database table-name string while retaining a quote-aware Table for the returned Statement and preserving the existing unique-constraint branches.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A current self.index_columns(...) call, syntax error, reverted or absent schema.py edit, Table object still passed to _index_columns(), or raw string passed directly as Statement.table prevents a score above 1. Shared coercion/equality changes or damaged expression/template branches cap the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff source and diff override stated intentions, proposed commands, earlier edits, test scripts, and edits that were reverted. Scratch files do not establish a production patch.
metadata.failure_mode: The trajectory has only a plan or scratch probe, edits the wrong file, drops the leading underscore, broadens ddl_references semantics, or uses one table representation indiscriminately.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an active production edit in _create_unique_sql() that calls the exact existing self._index_columns() helper and supplies a plain table-name string at that boundary.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff workspace or git diff in django/db/backends/base/schema.py. The field branch must call the existing self._index_columns() with a string table name, while Statement(table=...) must still receive a ddl_references.Table or equivalent reference object.
metadata.oracle_test: The preferred hunk changes self._index_columns(table, columns, ...) to self._index_columns(model._meta.db_table, columns, ...) while leaving table = Table(model._meta.db_table, self.quote_name), Statement(table=table, ...), and the Expressions branch intact.
metadata.stage: Implement and inspect the focused source change

scale.1: No active production correction exists, or the active edit is malformed, reverted, scratch-only, calls a nonexistent helper, or leaves the original mismatch.
scale.2: An active production edit exists but changes the wrong boundary, broadens shared semantics, mishandles Statement.table, or damages a neighboring unique-constraint branch.
scale.3: The active edit appears to normalize the Columns table value, but callability, the Statement Table role, or preservation of the surrounding branches is not fully established by the visible source.
scale.4: The active patch correctly calls self._index_columns() with a plain table-name string and visibly preserves Statement's Table wrapper and the existing expression and SQL-template branches.
scale.5: The active patch is the focused model._meta.db_table correction, or an equally explicit local refactor, and the visible diff is callable, localized, and free of unrelated product changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active source patch preserves the string and Table representation boundary

applies_when: The prefix investigates the reference-metadata symptom or states, attempts, or applies a production correction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the prefix connects a faithful observation of the matching-column reference failure to an actually applied production-code intervention addressing the observed cause.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A probe that changes the columns argument instead of Columns.table, treats a setup failure as semantic evidence, or claims that storing a Table object in Columns is the desired metadata contract caps the score at 1. A scratch-only edit or stated plan does not count as a production intervention.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful public-method output or a faithful paired Columns construction controls claims about the symptom. Visible source after an edit or a git diff controls whether an intervention was applied. Intentions, proposed commands, SQL rendering alone, dependency failures, scratch-file changes, and unsupported summaries do not establish either element.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge rewards a precise-looking plan or edit in isolation, even though the prefix never demonstrates the discriminating metadata behavior, or rewards a reproduction that is never connected to applied production work.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require both a faithful observation of the target references_column mismatch and a visibly executed production-source intervention causally linked to that mismatch.
metadata.judge_focus: Look for two independently visible elements: faithful evidence that a Table-valued Columns.table fails comparison with the plain table name, and an executed edit to relevant production source motivated by that evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: The faithful symptom is that Columns(Table('book', quote_name), ['title'], quote_name).references_column('book', 'title') is False while the otherwise equivalent Columns('book', ['title'], quote_name) call is True; the intervention must visibly target production code implicated by that mismatch.
metadata.stage: Implement and inspect the focused source change

scale.1: The visible probe or intervention contradicts the target argument contract, models a different defect, or relies on setup failure as semantic evidence.
scale.2: The work is coherent but incomplete: it supplies at most one of a faithful symptom observation or a visibly executed production intervention.
scale.3: Both elements are suggested, but either the symptom evidence is indirect or the claimed production intervention is not visibly established at the cutoff.
scale.4: A faithful target-symptom observation and a causally linked production-source intervention are both visible.
scale.5: Both elements are visible, and the loop is closed with post-intervention public-method evidence or a re-inspected focused diff plus an equivalent discriminating check.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Closed-loop symptom reproduction and production intervention

applies_when: The trajectory attempts or claims validation with max_post_process_passes set to zero.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards credible execution of the modified zero-pass repository path, subject to consistency with the latest visible production implementation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the latest source visibly removes the loop-local reset, lacks the pre-loop false default, forces an iteration, returns early, or suppresses exhaustion, cap the score at 2 regardless of a zero-pass smoke-test success. An attributable UnboundLocalError or false max-pass failure from the latest repository code scores 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: First use the latest visible production hunk after all restores and edits to determine whether behavioral claims can receive credit. For execution quality, a completed repository invocation and its output outrank prose, source-pattern checks, copied-loop simulations, generator construction, and setup attempts.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating an empty-path success from a semantically broken patch as stronger than a correct additive implementation, or treating copied logic, an unconsumed generator, a wrong checkout, or a setup error as behavioral proof.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a consumed repository post_process() or collectstatic invocation and no visible contradiction in the latest production state. Score 5 additionally requires representative files and visible processed-path reporting.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the repository generator is consumed with a zero-pass ManifestStaticFilesStorage configuration, whether representative files and processed reporting are exercised, and whether the tested latest source retains both required false assignments.
metadata.non_evidence: Dependency failures, malformed commands, nonexistent tests, storage construction alone, source-text assertions, copied range-loop logic, and exceptions caused solely by invalid test arguments do not establish zero-pass behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Run collectstatic with a ManifestStaticFilesStorage subclass whose max_post_process_passes is 0, consume processing completely, and confirm successful post-processed reporting without UnboundLocalError or Max post-process passes exceeded.

scale.1: A consumed invocation of the latest repository code visibly produces the target UnboundLocalError, a false zero-pass max-pass error, or another task-causal failure.
scale.2: No task-causal execution failure is shown, but the latest visible production source contradicts the required state machine, or all claimed validation is non-evidence while that contradiction remains.
scale.3: No source contradiction is visible, but validation is absent, nonbehavioral, uses only empty paths, or merely consumes a narrow direct generator call without representative processing.
scale.4: With no source contradiction, a consumed repository zero-pass invocation using representative files completes without either target failure, but processed-path reporting is not visibly confirmed.
scale.5: With no source contradiction, an equivalent focused regression or collectstatic run succeeds with representative files and visibly confirms processed-path reporting as well as absence of both target failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Source-consistent zero-pass execution evidence

applies_when: The trajectory changes post_process() control flow or presents compatibility evidence beyond the zero-iteration read.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards preservation of initial processing, final reporting, pass-local convergence, and persistent-substitution exhaustion, using the latest production state as the prerequisite for compatibility credit.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest hunk that deletes or moves the loop-local reset, bypasses initial processing or final yields, or suppresses max-pass exhaustion is capped at 2. A visible task-causal repository failure caused by such control flow scores 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: An attributable execution result from the latest repository state determines score 1 or supports scores 4 and 5. Otherwise, the latest visible production hunk after all restores controls the score; explicit deletion markers and displayed loop bodies outrank explanations or test claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding preservation credit from superficial structural similarity after the per-pass reset was deleted, or treating zero-pass success as proof of multi-pass compatibility.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require visible preservation of the initial processing phase, the loop-local reset, the break and exhaustion checks, hashed_files.update(), and final yields. Scores 4 and 5 require successful repository-based compatibility execution.
metadata.judge_focus: The initial _post_process() phase, the separate reset at the beginning of every iterative pass, convergence after a later false result, persistent-true exhaustion, hashed_files updates, and final processed-path yields.
metadata.non_evidence: Copied-loop simulations, source-pattern assertions, empty zero-pass calls, setup failures, and positive limits exercised without controlled substitution outcomes do not demonstrate convergence or exhaustion compatibility.
metadata.oracle_test: Through the real post_process() loop, run one sequence that reports subst=True and then subst=False and verify convergence, plus a persistent-true sequence that still yields the established Max post-process passes exceeded result.

scale.1: The latest repository execution visibly exhibits a task-causal pipeline, convergence, reporting, or exhaustion regression.
scale.2: No such executed regression is shown, but the latest production source definitively bypasses required pipeline work, lacks the per-pass reset, or suppresses established exhaustion behavior.
scale.3: Neither anchor 1 nor 2 applies; the latest source visibly preserves all required pipeline and positive-pass structures, but compatibility support is limited to inspection or nondiscriminative checks.
