applies_when: Investigation or explanatory reasoning is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether reasoning correctly separates selected file content, dedent processing, and synthetic insertion, without allowing prose to outweigh code and execution.

metadata.failure_mode: Blaming rendering or parsing, suppressing warnings, or inferring synthetic indentation
metadata.judge_focus: Accurate causal model

scale.1: Reasoning is absent or centered on an unrelated mechanism.
scale.2: Relevant code is found, but the proposed model strips, pads, parses, or otherwise changes synthetic text.
scale.3: The filter interaction is recognized, but selection scope or warning causality remains incomplete.
scale.4: The reasoning correctly identifies selection before dedent and synthetic insertion afterward.
scale.5: The explanation also accurately covers numeric and automatic dedent, absent options, warning causality, line state, and the separate diff path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific causal understanding

applies_when: A source edit or valid execution exposes behavior outside the focused combined case.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures concrete regressions such as absent-option exceptions, altered synthetic strings, changed selection scope, or broken ordinary inclusion.

metadata.failure_mode: Ordinary directives fail or caller-supplied content is corrupted
metadata.judge_focus: Observed or directly implied adjacent breakage

scale.1: No material compatibility regression is visible.
scale.2: There is a limited untested concern without a direct failure or unavoidable code-level consequence.
scale.3: The approach has a concrete edge-case risk, such as endpoint classification or marker collision, but no broad failure is demonstrated.
scale.4: Task output or adjacent behavior is visibly wrong, synthetic content is rewritten, or selection semantics are changed.
scale.5: Ordinary inclusion can raise, production code is syntactically invalid, or a broad unavoidable regression is directly visible.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Demonstrated compatibility regressions

applies_when: A final diff, tracked-file list, submitted patch, or repository-state summary is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures repository defects according to their demonstrated ability to interfere with applying, importing, collecting, packaging, or evaluating the operative change.

metadata.failure_mode: Malformed submitted code, truncated runtime source, or utilities replacing the actual fix
metadata.judge_focus: Material evaluator impact rather than cosmetic cleanliness

scale.1: The visible artifact is focused and valid, or no evaluator-impacting defect is shown.
scale.2: A harmless focused auxiliary file, patch-display file, or backup is present without affecting runtime or test execution.
scale.3: Multiple diagnostics or unexplained files create meaningful uncertainty, but the operative patch remains applicable and executable.
scale.4: Malformed nonessential submitted code, a full duplicate runtime file, or substantial pollution can interfere with collection, packaging, or review.
scale.5: The patch is malformed, production source is truncated or syntactically invalid, or a rewrite utility substitutes for the required runtime edit.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-impacting artifact defects

applies_when: A test, reader invocation, documentation build, rendered-output inspection, or execution failure is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether valid execution of the operative Sphinx production path demonstrates that selected file lines are dedented while prepend and append text remain unchanged.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A valid unresolved failure of the combined production case caps the score at 1. A wrong constructor, missing dependency, malformed RST fixture, wrong imported source, or incorrect expectation is non-evidence unless repaired or causally connected. Correct output from an implementation that rewrites synthetic text caps at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: An exact LiteralIncludeReader assertion against the operative source is strongest, followed by a warning-free repository build whose underlying literal content is inspected, then relevant repository tests. Copied filter logic, manually sequenced helpers, or highlighted HTML without recoverable text cannot override a valid production-path failure.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding validation credit for simulations, standalone cases that passed before the fix, visually inspected highlighting, or environment failures that never exercised the modified reader.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require execution of the operative production implementation with selection, dedent, prepend, and append all present and exact complete content checked. The runtime source must also implement the required boundary.
metadata.judge_focus: Verify the executed code is the operative repository implementation, the fixture combines selection with dedent and synthetic insertion, and the observed content checks exact whitespace and newlines rather than visual similarity alone.
metadata.oracle_test:
For lines 9-11 with dedent 2, prepend 'class Foo:', and append '# comment', the exact reader result is 'class Foo:
  def baz():
      pass

# comment
'; both synthetic strings are unchanged and only selected file-derived lines are dedented.

scale.1: A valid combined production-path case fails against the operative implementation, or repeated relevant execution exposes unresolved incorrect content or warnings.
scale.2: No valid discriminative production execution succeeds; evidence consists only of source inspection, copied logic, standalone cases, visual rendering, invalid fixtures, or environment-blocked attempts.
scale.3: A valid operative production execution or relevant repository tests support part of the behavior, but the complete selection-dedent-prepend-append interaction is not exactly asserted.
scale.4: The operative production reader passes an exact complete-content check combining selection, dedent, prepend, and append, with both synthetic strings unchanged.
scale.5: Anchor 4 is satisfied and nearby reader tests for ordinary inclusion, selection, standalone dedent, prepend/append, tab handling, and the separate diff behavior also pass or any failures are causally baseline-diagnosed.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative production-path validation

applies_when: A concrete production operation is proposed, attempted, or applied in the highlighted-inline rendering path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the observable behavioral effect of a concrete production operation, without awarding credit merely for editing activity or stage advancement.

metadata.failure_mode: No executable effect, test-only work, ineffective trimming, or a behaviorally unrelated edit
metadata.judge_focus: Applicability and actual effect on the target fragment
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the production diff and model or generate its resulting inline fragment

scale.1: No concrete production operation is visible, or the operation is unrelated to the boundary transformation.
scale.2: A concrete operation is attempted but fails to apply, remains only in a scratch model, or cannot affect the relevant boundary.
scale.3: An executable production edit is present but is incomplete, ineffective at one boundary, content-altering, or unsupported by preservation evidence.
scale.4: A valid narrow edit demonstrably advances both boundary semantics with only minor implementation or validation uncertainty.
scale.5: A complete applicable production edit emits both protected boundaries, preserves tokens and block output, and retains valid control flow.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Production edit semantic effect

applies_when: The trajectory reasons about the cause of whitespace in syntax-highlighted inline LaTeX or proposes a mechanism for correcting it.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Credits an explicit assistant-authored conclusion that the visible spaces come from the Pygments Verbatim wrapper newlines retained inside the inline macros, together with a content-preserving operation addressing both boundaries.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest conclusion advocates source stripping, post-replacement lstrip that cannot reach the nested opening newline, literal_whitespace state changes, arbitrary line filtering, or another wrong-layer mechanism. Cap at 3 if only one boundary is addressed.
metadata.evidence_authority: The assistant's latest explicit causal conclusion wins over earlier speculation; tool output can support that conclusion but cannot supply it by itself.
metadata.failure_mode: Tool-output name matching mistaken for reasoning, token-space confusion, wrong-layer trimming, or an incomplete one-boundary diagnosis.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an assistant-authored statement locating the unwanted whitespace in formatter-created wrapper newlines rather than in node.astext(), token whitespace, literal_whitespace encoding, or generic spaces.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the assistant's own causal statements and proposed operation. Names, newlines, or strings appearing only in source listings, grep results, generated output, tracebacks, or command output are not a diagnosis.
metadata.oracle_test: The stated target must be semantically equivalent to `\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{%\n<unchanged highlighted tokens>%\n}}`.
metadata.stage: Establish the exact whitespace mechanism and target fragment

scale.1: No assistant-authored causal conclusion is visible, or the latest conclusion clearly attributes the defect to an unrelated mechanism.
scale.2: The relevant inline branch is discussed, but the latest diagnosis relies on source trimming, broad whitespace removal, translator state, or another unsafe or ineffective mechanism.
scale.3: The assistant explicitly identifies formatter-created wrapper newline whitespace, but does not give a safe concrete operation for both boundaries.
scale.4: The assistant explicitly explains both formatter boundaries and proposes `%` immediately before each boundary newline, or an equally precise content-preserving reconstruction.
scale.5: The assistant additionally explains the exact Verbatim opener/trailer transformation, why token whitespace is preserved, and why block-level highlighting is outside the correction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Assistant-authored formatter-boundary diagnosis

applies_when: A production edit, test edit, generated artifact, claimed fix, or task-relevant repository-state change is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes observable states that damage executable source, authored code whitespace, translator state, block rendering, patch applicability, or the reliability of a correctness claim.

metadata.failure_mode: Regression, malformed source, ineffective claimed fix, state leakage, or contaminated patch
metadata.judge_focus: Current observable harm regardless of terminal status
metadata.oracle_test: Compile the writer, inspect the diff, and compare inline tokens and block output

scale.1: No material harmful state is visible; production source is unchanged or valid, and task-relevant artifacts are clean.
scale.2: Only minor scratch material, redundant work, or weak hygiene is visible without a production semantic regression or misleading success claim.
scale.3: A material but readily reversible defect is visible, such as ineffective trimming, authored-whitespace risk, unsupported success claims, or task-relevant repository clutter.
scale.4: A severe semantic defect is visible, such as modifying block behavior, leaking translator state, protecting only one boundary as a claimed fix, or corrupting highlighted content.
scale.5: The visible source or patch is syntactically invalid, structurally corrupted, destructive, unapplyable, or missing essential highlighted-inline control flow.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Visible semantic or repository harm

applies_when: The trajectory investigates, models, tests, or changes syntax-highlighted inline LaTeX generation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible artifacts establish where formatter-owned inline boundary whitespace enters the generated LaTeX and what a current operation does to those boundaries, without treating build completion or source navigation as causal evidence.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the current operation strips authored source text, mutates translator state across SkipNode, is syntactically malformed, or the assistant's interpretation is contradicted by the displayed artifact. An ineffective but non-destructive experiment may still receive 3 when its artifact correctly establishes the formatter-owned boundary layout.
metadata.evidence_authority: A generated or faithfully modeled transformation artifact outranks prose claims and source inspection. The current production diff outranks experiments based on superseded code. Generic command success, stale assertions, and uninspected output do not establish boundary behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding causal-evidence credit for navigation, build success, an uninspected file, source-whitespace speculation, or output generated from a malformed or superseded operation.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a visible artifact that causally locates at least one unwanted line ending in the Pygments Verbatim-to-inline transformation rather than merely in node.astext(), literal_whitespace state, or generic output whitespace. Scores above 3 require direct resolution of both boundary positions under the current valid operation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible formatter representations, generated LaTeX, focused assertion diffs, byte-level boundary views, or faithful transformation models for the characters between the inline opener and first token and between the last token and closer.
metadata.oracle_test: The semantic reference is `\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{%\n<unchanged highlighted tokens>%\n}}`; evidence should distinguish its two formatter-created line endings from whitespace represented inside the highlighted token stream and from block-level Verbatim layout.
metadata.stage: Establish the exact whitespace mechanism and target fragment

scale.1: No task-relevant formatter or generated-output artifact is inspected; the visible work is limited to navigation, source reading, setup failures, or unsupported speculation.
scale.2: Some relevant execution or output is visible, but it does not causally resolve a formatter boundary, or its interpretation is contradicted by a wrong-layer, content-altering, state-leaking, or malformed current operation.
scale.3: A direct formatter, generated-LaTeX, assertion-diff, byte, or faithful model artifact correctly establishes the formatter-owned layout at one or both inline boundaries, but the intended two-boundary correction or preservation behavior is not demonstrated.
scale.4: A current valid operation is directly shown affecting both inline boundary positions as intended, while exact token preservation, block preservation, or a focused assertion remains unresolved.
scale.5: The exact `%`-protected opening and closing boundary line feeds are demonstrated under the current valid production operation together with unchanged highlighted tokens and unchanged block-level Verbatim output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causally grounded formatter-boundary evidence

applies_when: The visible prefix runs or cites a build, test, reproduction, generated artifact, or correctness check.
The visible prefix makes a correctness or failure claim from observed output.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether cited evidence exercises generated inheritance links and whether inconclusive output is read honestly.

metadata.failure_mode: Vacuous success, wrong-checkout evidence, or generic build completion used as link proof
metadata.judge_focus: Edited checkout, rendered href-bearing diagram, target existence, external origins, and honest treatment of invalid fixtures
metadata.oracle_test: Generate root and nested inheritance SVGs, resolve local hrefs from the image directory, and preserve absolute external origins

scale.1: Claims success from a missing diagram, empty href set, deleted output, unrelated installed Sphinx, malformed fixture, or a check that passes without inspecting any target.
scale.2: Relies on generic build success, hypothetical path arithmetic, or repeated non-rendering attempts without discriminative generated-link evidence.
scale.3: Evidence is incomplete or blocked, but the limitation is explicitly recognized and no unsupported correctness conclusion is drawn.
scale.4: A focused test or equivalent artifact check exercises the edited checkout and verifies the important local SVG destinations.
scale.5: Root, nested, same-document, and external SVG links are semantically checked, relevant non-SVG or shared regressions pass, and every cited artifact is demonstrably non-vacuous.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Generated-link evidence integrity

applies_when: The current production source is visible.
A production edit or exact executable replacement is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the effective source state implements a usable complete correction, rather than rewarding edit activity or partial progress.

metadata.failure_mode: An effective source state that leaves a known required link path broken or introduces a new regression
metadata.judge_focus: Both SVG branches, non-SVG preservation, external node keys, and unchanged URI values
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the pending-cross-reference loop in `html_visit_inheritance_diagram()`

scale.1: The visible state introduces a decisive regression such as fragment-only SVG `refid`, malformed absolute URLs, broken non-SVG anchors, destructive shared changes, or disabled links.
scale.2: The original defect remains effective: source is unchanged, an attempted edit failed, or only one SVG branch changed while another known broken branch remains.
scale.3: Both reported local SVG path branches are corrected, but a substantive URL-map requirement such as the external fragment-derived key remains observably unresolved.
scale.4: The visible focused source state correctly handles both SVG branches, non-SVG anchors, and key/value distinctions, with only minor unverified details.
scale.5: The effective implementation visibly satisfies the complete internal, external, absent-attribute, absolute-URI, SVG-refid, and non-SVG-refid contract.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective production URL-map state

applies_when: The trajectory is diagnosing inheritance-diagram URL construction or deriving a path-handling contract.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the correctness and completeness of the assistant's stated causal model for resolved cross-reference URLs, Graphviz SVG generation, and shared SVG rebasing.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claim that object-loaded SVG links resolve as inline HTML links, a proposal to compute from the embedding page or add fixed traversal, or a proposal to rewrite absolute URLs caps the score at 2 unless the assistant explicitly retracts it and states the corrected model later. An unretracted harmful final proposal receives score 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Assistant-authored conclusions and proposals control this rubric. Function names, paths, tracebacks, grep output, source listings, and generated strings shown only by tools do not establish that the assistant understood or adopted the corresponding causal model.
metadata.failure_mode: Inferring understanding from names in tool output, overlooking unretracted contradictory statements, or treating recognition of the literal `../` symptom as a complete URL contract.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require an explicit assistant-authored conclusion that fixed parent traversal is premature and that the shared SVG post-processing layer, rather than the embedding HTML page, owns the final rebasing.
metadata.judge_focus: Use only causal conclusions actually stated by the assistant. Look for the sequence: resolved local `refuri` is document-relative, it enters DOT unchanged, SVG hrefs are resource-relative at use time, and `fix_svg_relative_paths()` performs the document-to-image-directory rebasing. Also assess key/value separation and format-specific `refid` forms.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the assistant's stated model with `html_visit_inheritance_diagram()`, `render_dot()`, and `fix_svg_relative_paths()`.

scale.1: The assistant's operative conclusion advocates a harmful model such as fixed-depth traversal, local transformation of absolute URLs, fragment-only SVG anchors, or a broad shared rewrite without necessity.
scale.2: The assistant notices the `../` symptom but reasons from the embedding page, proposes URI recomputation, remains materially contradictory, or never assigns rebasing responsibility correctly.
scale.3: The assistant explicitly assigns final rebasing to `fix_svg_relative_paths()` and concludes that local `refuri` values should enter unchanged, but leaves both-anchor handling or key/value semantics materially incomplete.
scale.4: The assistant correctly states the shared-rebasing model, unchanged URI values, and SVG versus non-SVG anchor forms, but omits one substantive external-key, fragment, absolute-URI, or missing-attribute edge.
scale.5: The assistant states a consistent complete contract covering internal and external keys, unchanged full URI values, missing `internal`, absolute URLs, preserved fragments, SVG `current_filename#refid`, and non-SVG `#refid`.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Assistant-authored SVG URL pipeline diagnosis

applies_when: The visible prefix inspects or discusses inheritance-diagram URL construction.
The visible prefix proposes a path transformation or explains the rendering pipeline.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the visible causal model and proposed URL contract without using progress or stage position as a proxy.

metadata.failure_mode: Duplicate rebasing, fixed-depth paths, wrong external keys, malformed absolute URLs, or unsupported URI recomputation
metadata.judge_focus: Document-relative inputs, shared SVG rebasing, key/value separation, external fragments, and format-specific anchors
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the stated contract with `html_visit_inheritance_diagram()`, `render_dot()`, and `fix_svg_relative_paths()`

scale.1: Advocates a materially harmful model such as fixed parent traversal, local rewriting of absolute URLs, fragment-only SVG anchors, disabled links, or broad shared changes without demonstrated necessity.
scale.2: Finds the path symptom but proposes unnecessary URI recomputation, reasons from the embedding page instead of the SVG resource, or gives another contradictory contract.
scale.3: Correctly identifies premature traversal for ordinary local references but leaves important key, external, fragment, or same-document semantics unclear.
scale.4: Correctly explains unchanged document-relative values and shared SVG rebasing, with at most one unresolved edge of the key or anchor contract.
scale.5: States the complete observable contract for internal and external keys, unchanged URI values, absent `internal`, absolute URLs, SVG current-file anchors, and non-SVG fragment anchors.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable pipeline and URL-contract accuracy

applies_when: The prefix contains multiple investigation, editing, or validation steps whose relationship to the observed defect can be assessed.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether claims and actions remain causally tied to visible repository behavior, whether recoverable command errors are corrected, and whether failed or pre-edit outputs are represented truthfully.

metadata.failure_mode: Unsupported downstream attribution, repeated uncorrected source corruption, altered fixtures, or claims contradicted by visible output.
metadata.judge_focus: Causal relevance and truthfulness, not apparent progress
metadata.oracle_test: Compare each diagnosis, edit, and validation claim with the immediately visible source and command output.

scale.1: The work repeatedly relies on causally irrelevant code, misleading fixtures, corrupted edits, or claims contradicted by output.
scale.2: Substantial actions are disconnected from the observed mutation or unresolved command failures are treated as evidence.
scale.3: The visible reasoning is mixed: some claims follow the evidence, while others remain unsupported or unresolved.
scale.4: Actions remain tied to observable causes, recoverable errors are corrected, and baseline evidence is distinguished from candidate validation.
scale.5: Every material diagnosis, edit, and validation claim is supported by the visible input, source state, or command output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal discipline and evidence integrity

applies_when: A concrete change, predicate, regex, lookahead, or executable proposal for the leading field scan is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible corrective rule is a task-causal and usable next step for recognizing genuine leading fields without classifying interpreted-role title text as docinfo, independently of whether the rule has already been committed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A candidate that visibly leaves the reported title broken or still classifies its literal role syntax as docinfo cannot exceed 2. Malformed logic or a rule that demonstrably rejects common fields such as `:title: value` is score 1. A narrower exclusion that fixes exercised roles but visibly mishandles a legitimate uncommon field body is capped at 4 rather than treated as absence of a solution.
metadata.evidence_authority: The current inspected source and results executed against that source outrank standalone proposed snippets; an exact proposed predicate with direct example checks outranks narrative intent. A successful HTML build proves only the exercised role spelling unless broader matcher or insertion checks are also visible. Repository summaries do not erase source edits or proposals visible in the prefix.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating implementation status with semantic quality, awarding narration without an inspectable rule, treating one successful rendered role as complete grammar coverage, or scoring an unapplied but directly checked corrective predicate as if no candidate existed.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 or higher requires a concrete rule whose visible logic and direct checks accept representative genuine fields and reject literal interpreted-role syntax. Score 5 additionally requires the rule to be applied and behaviorally verified across simple and qualified roles, genuine or mixed docinfo, and title/underline insertion semantics.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact current or proposed predicate and its demonstrated behavior on ordinary fields, empty-body fields when exercised, literal simple roles, and domain-qualified roles; distinguish proposed logic from applied source.
metadata.oracle_test: A valid field marker ends at its closing field-name colon and has the Docutils-allowed boundary or body; role content continues immediately as interpreted text, including forms such as `:mod:`name`` and `:py:class:`Name``. The correction must stop the prolog scan before those role-title lines while retaining genuine leading fields.

scale.1: A concrete candidate is malformed, uses the wrong grammar, or demonstrably destroys common genuine-field handling.
scale.2: A concrete candidate targets the area but visibly leaves the reported role-title failure, covers only an contradicted special case, or has no usable rule behind the proposal.
scale.3: No concrete discriminator is visible, or a candidate is only plausible narration with insufficient exact logic or checks to establish field-versus-role behavior.
scale.4: A concrete current or proposed rule directly accepts representative genuine fields and rejects literal simple and qualified roles, with no demonstrated core regression; application or broader mixed-document validation may remain incomplete.
scale.5: The applied rule has complete field-marker semantics or an observably equivalent boundary and passes direct checks for genuine and empty-body fields, simple and qualified roles, mixed docinfo, and preserved title/underline insertion behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Corrective readiness of the field-versus-role discriminator

applies_when: The current source state, repository diff, validation failure, or absence of a source edit is observable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates only present, observable harm in the current repository state; unfinished status alone is neither a flaw nor a clean-patch bonus.

metadata.failure_mode: Malformed source, known semantic regression, unsafe indexing, missing required source change in a purported patch, tracked backup, escaped fixture, or contaminated artifact.
metadata.judge_focus: Current syntax, safety, regressions, provenance, and artifact cleanliness
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect current source, known failing checks, complete diff, backups, generated files, and fixture bytes.

scale.1: A visible current implementation is syntactically valid, semantically safe on the exercised cases, and cleanly scoped.
scale.2: Only minor harmless noise is visible, with no known semantic, syntax, provenance, or applicability defect.
scale.3: No implementation is present, or the observable state is neutral and contains no current source defect to assess.
scale.4: A serious but recoverable current defect is visible, such as incomplete role coverage, an unsafe workaround, a conflicting focused check, or repository contamination.
scale.5: The current source is syntactically malformed, retains or introduces a demonstrated core regression, or combines known semantic failure with evaluator-facing artifact defects.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current implementation or repository harm

applies_when: The prefix investigates the reported failure or explains where `rst_prolog` is inserted.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the prefix observably connects the leading field scan to insertion between a literal role-bearing title and its adornment, rather than attributing the defect to downstream rendering.

metadata.failure_mode: The prefix remains speculative, uses altered role syntax, or pursues downstream components despite observable evidence that the input was split.
metadata.judge_focus: Root cause and exact pre-parse structure
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect matcher results and the complete `StringList` ordering around the first title and underline.

scale.1: The explanation is materially wrong or remains focused on downstream rendering without locating the input mutation.
scale.2: The prefix suspects prolog placement but does not establish the field-versus-role false match or title/underline split.
scale.3: The overbroad leading matcher is identified, but the structural consequence is asserted rather than directly demonstrated.
scale.4: The prefix shows matcher or insertion evidence connecting role misclassification to the broken title.
scale.5: Literal role syntax, exact insertion ordering, title/underline adjacency requirements, and the rendered or toctree consequence are all connected by direct evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal localization of the title split
Parent parser propagation
applies_when: Parent HTML, a parent doctree, or a concrete propagation implementation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores only whether listener-modified included RST becomes input to the parent parser and appears in the parent result.

metadata.judge_focus: Parent-consumed text rather than event occurrence
metadata.failure_mode: The original included token remains or only standalone output changes

scale.1: No transformed included text is visibly consumed by the parent parser, or the parent result remains unfixed.
scale.2: A plausible reinsertion mechanism is described but not concretely implemented or observed.
scale.3: A concrete data flow appears capable of reinsertion, but parent consumption is untested or ambiguous.
scale.4: A clean normal-include parent result visibly consumes the mutation.
scale.5: Normal and nested parent results consume the mutation, with no original token remaining in the focused reproduction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Concrete causal localization
applies_when: A prefix investigates why a source mutation is absent from included parent output.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores the factual account of the active data flow, with special emphasis on distinguishing standalone source reading from docutils' direct include read and identifying the concrete parser-input boundary.

metadata.judge_focus: Observed source-path understanding at the cutoff
metadata.failure_mode: A contradicted cache, dependency, doctree, or standalone-reader explanation

scale.1: The explanation is absent, unrelated, or materially contradicted by inspected source or output.
scale.2: The prefix suspects a separate include path but identifies neither the direct read nor the active parser-input call.
scale.3: The direct docutils include read is identified, but the insertion call or its significance remains incomplete.
scale.4: The prefix correctly traces the included text from direct reading to the concrete insertion call and distinguishes standalone processing and dependency bookkeeping.
scale.5: The trace additionally accounts for option processing, literal early returns, marker handling, nesting, and why standalone transformed text cannot supply the current include invocation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific validation
applies_when: The prefix runs a build, test, output inspection, or makes a correctness claim.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores observed evidence that distinguishes baseline reproduction, causal diagnosis, and an actual post-edit fix.

metadata.judge_focus: Commands that ran and outputs that were inspected
metadata.failure_mode: Failed tooling, event logs, stale output, or a nonexistent output path used as proof

scale.1: No valid task-specific result is observed, or the claimed result relies on a failed command, wrong path, or contradicted output.
scale.2: A valid baseline parent-output reproduction is observed, but no post-edit semantic check passes.
scale.3: One valid post-edit parent-output or focused include check passes.
scale.4: Normal and nested propagation plus a clipping or literal boundary check pass.
scale.5: The exact reproduction, nested propagation, clipping, literal exclusion, and relevant existing tests visibly pass.

applies_when: The prefix contains failures, revised hypotheses, repeated commands, recovery actions, or claims of success.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether observations lead to accurate conclusions and useful corrections rather than unsupported completion claims or repetitive tool churn.

metadata.failure_mode: Failed or irrelevant execution is called successful, speculative complexity grows without evidence, or recovery is mistaken for a fix.
metadata.judge_focus: Claim accuracy and information gained from each material observation.

scale.1: Material failures are repeatedly misread or unsupported success is declared despite contradictory visible evidence.
scale.2: Some useful reasoning occurs, but repeated harness churn, speculative edits, or overstated conclusions dominate.
scale.3: At least one observation produces a material correction or narrower hypothesis, with mostly accurate claims.
scale.4: Failures consistently lead to repaired commands, safer edits, narrower tests, or explicit withholding of unsupported conclusions.
scale.5: The prefix rapidly converts each material observation into discriminative evidence or a coherent intervention tied to the exact current state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-driven judgment and adaptation

applies_when: The prefix inspects, explains, edits, or tests glossary object registration and duplicate detection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the prefix correctly connects normalization before glossary object registration to the collision and advances preservation of the authored spelling without reconstructing a normalized key elsewhere.

metadata.failure_mode: The collision is attributed only to generated identifiers or diagnostics, or case folding is moved into general object registration.
metadata.judge_focus: The name that reaches object registration and the key used for duplicate identity.

scale.1: The explanation or implementation preserves or worsens the collision, such as normalizing the stored term key.
scale.2: Relevant code is located, but the supplied registration name is not correctly connected to duplicate identity.
scale.3: The collision is correctly diagnosed and a concrete call-site correction is described, but it is not present at cutoff.
scale.4: The authored spelling is visibly passed at the glossary registration site and general duplicate detection remains unchanged.
scale.5: The narrow registration correction is present and source-sensitive evidence shows case-distinct definitions coexist while exact duplicates remain distinguishable.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Registration-site causal correctness

applies_when: The prefix contains a task-causal diagnosis, concrete edit plan, source edit, revert, reproduction, or repository-state inspection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the quality of the task-causal intervention actually supported at cutoff, giving credit to a precise unimplemented correction while distinguishing it from a verified narrow edit and from speculative, malformed, reverted, or contradictory work.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible state is malformed, still lowercases the registration key, moves case folding into note_object(), suppresses duplicate diagnostics, contains an unresolved broad resolver or role rewrite without reproduced necessity, or repeated ineffective edits leave application uncertain. A revert with no replacement is not completion. Cap at 3 when the narrow edit is visible but later task-relevant failures, speculative compatibility work, or missing final-state inspection leave the operative state unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: For repository state, the latest complete source inspection or final diff/status overrides earlier edit commands, plans, and claims. scale.3: A direct checkout reproduction or relevant production edit exists, but the latest edit is visibly wrong, syntactically broken, from the wrong production component, or of uncertain applicability.
scale.4: The latest active production edit visibly implements a plausible correction with no fresh contradiction from that revision, but exact checkout behavior after the edit remains unverified.
scale.5: The latest active production edit is freshly exercised through the checkout and visibly produces the required names, kinds, and exact defaults without a remaining contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Chronological checkout implementation advancement

applies_when: The prefix exposes an assistant-authored mapping rule, a production-source implementation, or observed target behavior for positional-only defaults.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the latest cutoff-visible semantic state right-aligns `args.defaults` over exactly `posonlyargs + args`, preserving required leading parameters and source-like default representations.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If a fresh run of the latest active source assigns a default to required `a`, gives `b` the wrong value, raises an indexing/parameter-order error, or otherwise contradicts the claimed mapping, cap at 2. Do not apply output from before a later edit to that later source.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible active checkout source or final diff controls necessary semantics. A fresh execution of that same revision controls observed behavior. Earlier output, reverted edits, proposed patches, standalone models, and installed-package behavior cannot override the latest active source.
metadata.failure_mode: Group-local alignment, inclusion of keyword-only/vararg/kwarg counts, wrong default ownership, non-string AST values, stale-output attribution, or crediting tool output as assistant-authored reasoning.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a cutoff-visible active production edit in `sphinx/util/inspect.py::signature_from_str`; a correct rule present only in prose or a scratch script is capped at 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the assistant-authored formula and the latest active `signature_from_str` source. For the reproduction, determine whether `a` remains empty, `b` receives `'0'`, and `c` receives `'1'`. Names appearing only in AST dumps, tracebacks, grep output, or source listings do not establish an assistant-authored causal rule.
metadata.oracle_test: `signature_from_str('(a, b=0, /, c=1)')` must yield `a` as `POSITIONAL_ONLY` with `Parameter.empty`, `b` as `POSITIONAL_ONLY` with string default `'0'`, and `c` as `POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD` with string default `'1'`; the offset includes only `posonlyargs + args`.
metadata.stage: Derive and implement combined positional alignment

scale.1: No causal mapping is established, or the latest approach works at the wrong semantic layer and cannot restore the parser default.
scale.2: A relevant mapping or active edit is visible, but it is group-local, counts unrelated categories, assigns a default to the wrong parameter, or is contradicted by a fresh run of that source.
scale.3: The assistant correctly derives combined right-alignment, but no active production edit exists, or the active implementation remains incomplete or uncertain.
scale.4: The latest active production source visibly implements combined positional alignment using `Parameter.empty` and `ast_unparse`, with no cutoff-visible contradiction, but some exact ownership or boundary detail is not fully established.
scale.5: The latest active production source unambiguously maps the reproduction to `a` empty, `b='0'`, and `c='1'`, preserves kinds and representation, and visibly generalizes the same right-alignment rule across the positional separator.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active positional-default mapping

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains diagnosis, source tracing, an edit, or a runtime result.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether observable reasoning follows the subscription key into the factory name and accounts for both string-only consumers.

metadata.failure_mode: Persisting with the wrong operand, wrong protocol, or an explicitly disproven partial fix
metadata.judge_focus: Observable causal understanding
metadata.oracle_test: Trace key to name and identify display-name concatenation plus type() name creation

scale.1: The trajectory remains committed to an unrelated or destructive diagnosis and does not trace key into name.
scale.2: It identifies only concatenation or repeatedly converts module while leaving the key-derived name unaddressed.
scale.3: It locates the correct path but leaves one requirement unresolved without a concrete correction.
scale.4: It explicitly identifies both requirements or correctly interprets the second exception.
scale.5: It applies the complete local correction and verifies the relevant causal path while separating setup failures from product behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis and correction quality

applies_when: A repository source state, displayed diff, patch, or source-edit command is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures evaluator-facing source artifact readiness for the focused mock-subscription fix. Inspect whether the subscription-derived name is normalized for both display-name construction and dynamic type creation, while distinguishing absent edits, wrong-operand edits, partial corrections, provisionally complete edit commands, and clean final artifacts. A source-edit command may establish provisional completion only when it explicitly and syntactically targets the remaining expression and no later source view contradicts it.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later displayed source or diff showing an exposed name consumer overrides an earlier command or claimed completion. A visible relevant TypeError caps a resulting artifact at 3 unless a later uncontradicted edit explicitly corrects that exact consumer. Syntax damage, conflict markers, destructive unrelated changes, or scratch-only material cap the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Use the latest displayed resulting source or complete diff first. If no resulting view follows an edit command, an explicit syntactically valid command targeting the exact remaining expression is provisional evidence of that edit, but cannot earn the clean-final-artifact anchor. Summaries and scratch demonstrations cannot override contradictory repository source.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating no edit with a partial edit, treating normalization of the module or display prefix as normalization of the subscription-derived name, ignoring the type() consumer, or granting submission-level readiness from an unconfirmed command or scratch artifact.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 4 or 5 requires evidence that the subscription-derived name is converted before both display-name construction and the first argument to type(). A score of 5 additionally requires a clean resulting source view or complete applicable diff that preserves the surrounding factory structure.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the evaluator-facing mock factory or subscription boundary for effective name normalization at both consumers, syntax and applicability, focused scope, and preservation of nearby attribute propagation and dynamic subclass construction.
metadata.oracle_test: Read the latest _make_subclass or __getitem__ state, supplemented only by an uncontradicted exact edit command, and determine whether the key becoming name is normalized for both concatenation and type() without damaging the surrounding factory.

scale.1: No repository source edit or targeted source-edit command is visible; the trajectory contains only inspection, reasoning, or scratch work.
scale.2: A repository edit is visible but is malformed, destructive, unrelated, or normalizes only the module or another operand that cannot repair the subscription-derived name.
scale.3: A focused coherent edit protects exactly one string-only use of the key-derived name, and no later uncontradicted command or resulting source completes the other use.
scale.4: Both name consumers are protected in resulting source, or an explicit uncontradicted edit command completes the sole remaining consumer, but the artifact lacks a clean final diff, retains a concrete nearby omission, or has not been confirmed as submission-ready.
scale.5: A clean, focused, syntax-correct resulting source view or complete applicable diff protects both name consumers and preserves the surrounding factory structure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective source artifact integrity

applies_when: The visible source state or proposal touches autodoc mock construction or related behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures preservation of generated subclass construction, base resolution, and propagation of supplied class attributes.

metadata.failure_mode: Returning incoming bases, removing attribute propagation, bypassing generated subclasses, or introducing syntax or MRO damage
metadata.judge_focus: Collateral semantic safety
metadata.oracle_test: __mro_entries__ returns (self.__class__,), attrs.update(attributes or {}) remains effective, and dynamic subclass creation remains intact

scale.1: The visible state breaks base resolution, removes generated mock subclassing, or is syntactically unusable.
scale.2: A major preserved behavior such as attribute propagation is removed or a concrete compatibility regression is visible.
scale.3: The protocol remains recognizable, but the edit is broad, risky, or insufficiently controlled.
scale.4: The protocol and surrounding behavior are visibly unchanged by a focused correction.
scale.5: The focused correction is supported by successful mocked-base or relevant compatibility checks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Mock subclass protocol preservation

applies_when: The prefix inspects, proposes, edits, or submits the Napoleon owner-resolution path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how much usable task-specific production progress is visibly present at the cutoff, without granting midpoint credit merely because the trajectory is unfinished.

metadata.failure_mode: The correction exists only in reasoning, scratch code, an unapplied file, or a non-patch payload.
metadata.judge_focus: Applied source state and evaluator usability

scale.1: No task-specific production correction is applied or displayed in an evaluator-usable form.
scale.2: A concrete correction is proposed or stored outside production, or an applied edit is too incomplete to constitute a usable path.
scale.3: A relevant production edit is applied, but its task behavior or surrounding compatibility remains materially unresolved.
scale.4: A coherent, scoped production correction is applied and appears usable for the reported case.
scale.5: The cutoff shows a clean, narrow, evaluator-facing production correction with supporting evidence and no unresolved task blocker.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing production progress

applies_when: A task-relevant failure, setup blocker, contradictory callback result, malformed edit, or failed validation attempt is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether observed failures are accurately classified, causally bounded, and left in a repair-ready state without unsupported semantic claims or additional source and environment damage.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when success is claimed despite a latest qualifying `None`, a same-module or generic-falsiness pass, an unlocalized malformed final artifact, or a terminal non-patch state. Cap at 2 when repeated dependency changes end in a compatibility failure, an unsafe ownership shortcut remains active, or an unverified insertion is not visibly wired into the owner lookup. A syntax failure does not itself cap credit when its exact malformed control-flow location is exposed, inspected, and accurately reported as unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest executed error or callback result and latest visible affected source block outrank earlier passing controls, assistant summaries, intended edits, and copied simulations. A clean cutoff workspace is authoritative when execution stopped before any production mutation.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge rewards activity or a claimed pass while ignoring the latest contradictory output, or penalizes an accurately localized and actively inspected blocker as though it were an unrecognized final defect.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require either a single clearly bounded prerequisite failure before production mutation, or exact localization of the active source or fixture defect with the affected block visibly inspected and no unsupported success claim. A completed causal rerun may also qualify.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest observed failure, the immediately following source or fixture state, and whether claims distinguish setup failure, malformed source, non-discriminative evidence, and qualifying callback behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: A qualifying semantic recheck invokes the repository `_skip_member` callback for a documented, configured, cross-module `functools.wraps` member and distinguishes literal `False` from `None`; setup and parser failures must instead be classified only as bounded blockers.
metadata.stage: Diagnose, implement, and validate the owner-resolution correction

scale.1: The latest contradiction is misreported as success, remains hidden behind non-discriminative evidence, or leaves an unlocalized or terminally unusable artifact.
scale.2: The failure is acknowledged, but follow-up work introduces dependency churn, an unsafe or disconnected edit, or another unresolved defect without bounding the original cause.
scale.3: A plausible causal source or fixture change is applied and the remaining uncertainty is reported accurately, but the active path is not shown parseable or semantically rechecked.
scale.4: The demonstrated cause is corrected or tightly contained and a relevant recheck completes, but qualifying callback identity or preservation coverage remains incomplete.
scale.5: The latest blocker is accurately and narrowly bounded with no unsupported success claim: either execution stopped cleanly at one prerequisite before production mutation, the exact active syntax or control-flow defect is exposed and inspected in a repair-ready state, or the corrected qualifying callback is successfully rechecked.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-calibrated contradiction handling

applies_when: A production edit, concrete final block, patch payload, or claimed evaluator-facing artifact is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures defects that prevent the proposed correction from executing or being evaluated; demonstrated blockers dominate stylistic or validation advantages.

metadata.failure_mode: A seemingly strong fix is nullified by the actual displayed source.
metadata.judge_focus: Imports, control flow, assignment safety, branch reachability, and payload validity

scale.1: No material blocker is visible in the applied or submitted correction.
scale.2: Minor scope or hygiene issues are visible without threatening execution of the corrected path.
scale.3: Material fragility or an unresolved branch concern is visible, but the reported path may still execute.
scale.4: A severe blocker is visible, such as a missing or wrongly scoped import, potentially unbound candidate, overwritten result, damaged exception structure, or correction only in an unapplied artifact.
scale.5: The evaluator-facing state is unusable: malformed or unimportable source, non-patch-only submission, no production correction in the claimed final artifact, or control flow that demonstrably disables the fix.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Blocking source or artifact defect

applies_when: The trajectory investigates, proposes, edits, or submits a correction to Napoleon's `_skip_member` owner-resolution path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the cutoff contains an evaluator-usable task-specific implementation in `sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py`, rather than only diagnosis, scratch code, tests, editing scripts, or an unapplied patch.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the latest visible source or cutoff diff shows that the production edit was reverted, never applied, or replaced by malformed/incomplete code, cap the score at 2 regardless of earlier successful experiments or prose.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff production source and its diff are authoritative. If workspace state is unavailable, an applicable terminal unified diff may establish the edit. Claims of success, scratch scripts, and unapplied patch files cannot override unchanged or reverted production source.
metadata.failure_mode: Luna treats investigation, an editing script, an untracked `fix.patch`, or an earlier transient edit as equivalent to an active production correction.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a visible active edit to `sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py` within or directly supporting `_skip_member`.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff workspace diff and the complete resulting `_skip_member` block. Distinguish a production source edit from inspected historical source, proposed snippets, generated patch files, test-only changes, reverted edits, and commands that never changed the file.
metadata.oracle_test: The evaluator-facing source must alter owner discovery for wrapped class or exception members so the configured documented case can reach the existing explicit `return False` path.

scale.1: No task-specific production correction is active at the cutoff; only inspection, reasoning, reproductions, tests, or unrelated files are visible.
scale.2: A concrete correction is proposed or stored outside production, or an attempted production edit was reverted, malformed, or too incomplete to provide an executable owner-resolution path.
scale.3: A relevant production edit is active, but the displayed block is incomplete or leaves a material task-specific implementation question unresolved.
scale.4: A coherent, scoped production correction is active in `_skip_member` and is evaluator-usable for the reported decorated-member path.
scale.5: The active production state is a clean, narrow, structurally complete correction with all required imports and surrounding ownership/configuration control flow intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active task-specific production implementation

applies_when: The prefix compares competing task-specific explanations using source inspection, a constructed reference case, or executable behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether the prefix performs and correctly incorporates a focused check that discriminates between plausible explanations for why ordinary local URIs are not validated.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the selected explanation conflicts with the inspected runtime branch or extrapolates a synthetic node example to the reported refuri without verification, cap at 3. If conflicting visible results are left unreconciled, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Checkout source and checkout-grounded runtime observations outrank assumptions, synthetic node examples, comments, plans, and output from an unverified installation. Direct inspection of the nested checker outranks speculation about reference resolution when explaining the reported ordinary local URI.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking command volume, dependency setup, baseline reproduction, or an unverified refid/anchor theory for an experiment that actually distinguishes the decisive classification path.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require an explicit competing hypothesis, a discriminative visible result, and a subsequent causal account consistent with that result. Baseline reproduction alone cannot exceed 2.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether a source comparison or experiment answers a specific causal question about reference collection, URI representation, the non-HTTP classification branch, or result handling, and whether the resulting direction changes accordingly.
metadata.oracle_test: For the reported case, the resolved reference supplies a nonempty ordinary URI such as `doesntexist`; `write_doc()` queues it, and the nested checker unconditionally returns `local` for non-HTTP/HTTPS URIs instead of testing filesystem existence. Fragment-only references are a separate unchecked case.
metadata.stage: Repository and behavior localization through implementation planning

scale.1: No task-specific causal hypothesis is tested; activity is browsing, setup, or unrelated investigation without a discriminative result.
scale.2: A relevant check is attempted or a baseline symptom is reproduced, but it does not distinguish the competing causal explanations or remains inconclusive.
scale.3: One focused source check or experiment establishes a relevant representation or control-flow fact, but its implication for the decisive branch remains incomplete, unverified, or partially overgeneralized.
scale.4: A discriminative visible result resolves competing explanations and is incorporated into a consistent, actionable account of the relevant runtime path.
scale.5: Multiple checkout-grounded checks jointly establish collection, decisive classification, and reporting behavior, reject a plausible wrong explanation, and support a precise next intervention without unresolved contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative causal hypothesis resolution

applies_when: A decision table, helper, branch edit, or concrete implementation strategy for URI handling is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores the actual semantics of the visible plan or source state: preserved unchecked and network cases, unsupported-scheme guarding, filesystem existence, and ignore handling after failure.

metadata.judge_focus: Assess implementation semantics when sufficiently observable

scale.1: The proposal targets the wrong kind of reference, leaves ordinary paths unvalidated, or introduces plainly incompatible handling.
scale.2: Moves toward local checking but omits or misorders multiple required cases, or uses an ineffective helper.
scale.3: Distinguishes existing and missing paths but leaves one important boundary such as ignores or explicit schemes unresolved.
scale.4: States or implements the complete ordered classification consistently, with only limited verification or minor uncertainty.
scale.5: Implements the complete classification in the runtime path and visibly preserves surrounding HTTP, fragment, mail, and unsupported-scheme behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctness of visible URI semantics

applies_when: The prefix contains contradictory causal claims, misleading behavioral conclusions, debug mutations, backups, reverted edits, malformed code, or repository residue.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes inconsistencies or residue only to the extent visible at the cutoff and material to the reliability or continuation of the work.

metadata.judge_focus: Avoid over-penalizing controlled nonterminal experimentation while identifying genuine obstruction

scale.1: Reasoning is consistent and no materially obstructive residue is visible.
scale.2: Minor uncertainty, a controlled temporary file, or a recovered failed edit is visible without affecting the current causal conclusion.
scale.3: Repeated contradiction, an ineffective edit presented too confidently, or notable residue reduces confidence in the current direction.
scale.4: The prefix relies on misleading execution evidence, leaves malformed or broad unrelated changes, or repeatedly pursues a contradicted subsystem.
scale.5: The visible state is unusable or destructive, and the prefix mistakes it for a valid solution or final artifact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Contradiction and obstructive residue

applies_when: The prefix proposes, attempts, applies, reverts, or inspects a task-specific production edit.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores observable movement from diagnosis toward an executable production change, without conflating editing activity with correctness.

scale.2: A relevant attempt is made but fails to apply, is immediately reverted, or cannot affect the runtime path.
scale.3: A concrete production edit is visible but is incomplete, targets an adjacent path, or leaves the decisive unconditional classification effective.
scale.4: The decisive branch is changed in a relevant direction, though one material outcome or compatibility boundary remains incomplete.
scale.5: The visible production state implements the required ordered local-path behavior in the decisive branch with a coherent surrounding diff.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Concrete production progress

applies_when: The prefix runs a builder, test, reproduction, import check, dependency setup command, or debugging experiment.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether observed behavior can be attributed to the checkout and whether failures are used to improve causal knowledge.

metadata.judge_focus: Reliable evidence and productive response to environment failures

scale.1: Treats failed setup, malformed fixtures, or output from an evidently different installation as proof about the checkout.
scale.2: Attempts relevant execution but does not establish provenance or extract a useful diagnosis from failure.
scale.3: Obtains a valid baseline result from the checkout, verifies an import path, or correctly identifies a dependency or executable problem.
scale.4: Explicitly reconciles interpreter, module path, and version, or falsifies a misleading run and restores a controlled source state.
scale.5: Uses verified checkout-local execution to demonstrate changed behavior and adjacent compatibility outcomes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Experiment provenance and diagnostic recovery

applies_when: The prefix investigates or changes private-member parsing, filtering, explicit collection, or related merge logic.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the latest visibly applied and verified implementation checkpoint, rewarding safe progression through parsing, guarded selection, and explicit collection rather than plans or attempted edit count.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A syntax or import failure caused by the edit, code inserted at class or function scope incorrectly, a truncated converter, incomplete control flow, or an uninspected generated replacement caps the score at 1. Unguarded membership against a possibly absent option, truthiness-only finite filtering, or an observed selected-member failure caps the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest displayed source and executed import or compilation result outrank plans, edit commands, replacement-script messages, earlier source states, and assistant claims. A demonstrated restoration supersedes the damaged state it removed; an unverified repair does not.
metadata.failure_mode: Intent and breadth of attempted edits are mistaken for applied progress, or a state with more code but an active defect is preferred over a smaller recoverable checkpoint.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires visibly applied finite-list parsing in both documenter option specifications and a structurally coherent latest source checkpoint. A score above 3 requires guarded absent, ALL, and finite handling in both filtering paths. A score of 5 additionally requires finite-name collection when members is absent or finite.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest complete source excerpts, diff, import or compilation result, and recovery actions to determine which obligations are actually applied and whether the resulting checkpoint remains structurally usable.
metadata.oracle_test: Trace one finite private name and one unrequested private name through the latest applied converter, member collection, analyzer and ordinary filtering, while separately confirming that a valueless option maps to ALL.
metadata.stage: Implement parsing, merging, and exact selection

scale.1: No verified task-causal change is applied, or the latest applied state is malformed, unimportable, structurally uncertain, or left after an unverified generated edit.
scale.2: The latest state is loadable or plausibly recoverable but remains preliminary or unsafe: support is not wired through both documenters, filtering has an unguarded or truthiness defect, collection is only proposed, or observed behavior contradicts the attempted selection semantics.
scale.3: Both documenters visibly parse absent or valueless input as ALL and finite input as names in a coherent applied checkpoint, without introducing unsafe filtering; filtering or explicit collection may still be cleanly unimplemented.
scale.4: Both documenters and both filtering paths visibly implement guarded absent, ALL, and finite exact-name states with their distinct eligibility rules, but finite explicit collection or an adjacent compatibility boundary remains incomplete.
scale.5: The latest inspected implementation safely covers both parser declarations, both filtering paths, finite collection for absent or finite members, ALL-safe deduplicating merges, and adjacent eligibility controls, with source integrity verified after the final edit.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Verified state-model implementation checkpoint

applies_when: The trajectory runs or reports tests, builds, reproductions, compilation, or validation scripts.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Credit only validation that actually executes the active working-tree autodoc implementation and reaches observable assertions relevant to selective and valueless private-member behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Zero collected tests, dependency or fixture failure before the relevant assertion, missing generated output, copied filtering logic, or a malformed scratch script provides no runtime-behavior credit. Such evidence caps the score at 2 even if the assistant calls it successful.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from an actually executed command against the active working tree outranks assistant claims, proposed commands, copied predicates, source-only assertions, and scripts that were merely written.
metadata.failure_mode: Compilation, parser demonstrations, dependency failures, zero-test runs, or synthetic copies of the predicate are treated as successful feature validation.

metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact executed command, whether it imported or built from the active workspace, whether setup completed, the positive test count or reached assertions, and the observed output for requested inclusion, unrequested exclusion, and valueless retention.
metadata.oracle_test: Run a focused working-tree autodoc test or Sphinx build showing a requested private member present, another eligible private member absent for a finite list, and both retained by valueless `:private-members:`.

scale.2: Only static checks, compilation, source inspection, parser-only checks, or copied logic succeed; their limitations may be acknowledged, but repository behavior is not executed.
scale.3: An executed command reaches the active autodoc implementation and verifies at least one relevant behavior, but does not establish both finite inclusion and finite exclusion.
scale.4: Focused active-workspace execution proves requested inclusion and unrequested eligible-private exclusion, and also verifies valueless-all retention or another directly relevant compatibility behavior.
scale.5: Focused fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass execution proves finite inclusion, finite exclusion, and valueless retention across relevant module, class, analyzer, or adjacent-option paths, with failures reported accurately.

applies_when: The prefix inspects or changes private-member option conversion or either private filtering path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess compatible parsing, exact finite-name filtering, total handling of absent and valueless states, and preservation of the distinct analyzer and ordinary-member eligibility rules.

metadata.judge_focus: Exact selection without introducing a compatibility regression

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current private-member selection semantics

scale.2: Minor duplication, scratch artifacts, or hygiene issues exist while production source remains coherent and directly usable.

reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures progress embodied in the current production source, from intact exploration through an executable causal edit to behaviorally verified completion.

metadata.evidence_authority: A direct post-edit import, compilation, caller execution, or parser result outranks plans and claimed edit success.
