reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the fidelity and usability of visible evidence connecting the reported declaration to Napoleon's generated parameter directives.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If an active task edit makes the relevant production module non-importable or prevents the parser from starting, evidence from a bypassing helper, copied logic, or wrong parser class is capped at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Exact output from a fresh production NumpyDocstring instance outranks integrated fixtures, consumed-tuple traces, detached simulations, and source browsing. Direct import or syntax failure after an edit overrides earlier intended or simulated results.
metadata.failure_mode: Equating intact but incomplete exploration with a damaged production state that cannot run the semantic oracle at all.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires an integrated NumPy-path fixture or complete consumed tuple; credit above 3 requires observed directives from a fresh production parser; credit 5 requires comparable pre-edit and post-edit evidence with discriminative assertions.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect parser class, configuration, parser freshness, declaration content, generated directives, and whether the production path remains runnable after any edit.
metadata.oracle_test: A faithful reproduction constructs NumpyDocstring with the intended Napoleon configuration and observes the generated :param and :type directives for x1, x2 : array_like, optional.

scale.1: An active task edit prevents the relevant production parser from importing or starting, so only bypassing, stale, or otherwise unusable evidence is available.
scale.2: The production path is not shown broken, but evidence is limited to source browsing, wrong-class or consumed-parser output, detached simulation, or manually written directives.
scale.3: An integrated fixture contains the reported NumPy declaration or a complete consumed tuple is observed, but generated production-parser directives are not reached.
scale.4: A fresh production NumpyDocstring run visibly emits the malformed pre-edit directives or meaningful post-edit directives, without a complete before/after discriminative check.
scale.5: The same applicable production path is observed before and after the edit, with exact assertions for separate complete fields and the unaffected configuration mode.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Usable NumPy Napoleon path evidence

applies_when: A NumPy Parameters declaration contains two or more comma-separated names.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the current production state can emit one complete parameter and type field per declared name, reusing the unchanged shared description and converted type.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A syntax/import failure in the active implementation, an incompatible caller contract, or visible corruption of the shared type or description caps the score at 1. Unconditional expansion of the list-style mode caps the score at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Exact post-edit NumpyDocstring output has highest authority, followed by executable applied source showing the full data flow, then partial applied logic, then pre-edit output or exploration. Intended future edits and detached simulations are not implementation evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding implementation credit for analysis alone, or treating a broken edit as partial semantic success despite its inability to emit any fields.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires an applied implementation that can execute its affected parser or caller. Credit above 3 requires visible preservation of both the complete type and description for every emitted name.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect applied source logic or actual NumpyDocstring output for name-only splitting, whitespace normalization, complete type and description reuse, and mode-specific activation.
metadata.oracle_test: For x1, x2 : array_like, optional in parameter-field mode, both x1 and x2 must receive param and type directives containing the shared description and the complete converted :class:`array_like`, *optional* type; list-style mode must retain one combined item.

scale.1: An active implementation is non-executable or visibly corrupts, drops, or inconsistently assigns the shared type or description.
scale.2: No applied implementation exists, or actual production output still contains only the malformed combined field; diagnosis or proposed code alone remains here.
scale.3: An executable applied attempt separates or prepares to separate names, but complete duplication, whitespace normalization, or configuration scope is not established.
scale.4: Executable source or actual output shows separate names with the complete shared type and description, while focused optional-type, mode-boundary, or compatibility evidence is still missing.
scale.5: Exact edited-path output or regression assertions verify every per-name param/type pair, the complete converted optional type, the shared description, and preservation of combined list-style mode.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable complete per-name field semantics

applies_when: A repair to built-in-message locale initialization is proposed, attempted, or visible in the repository.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible applied source deterministically makes configured project locale directories primary over the retained bundled Sphinx locale, while accounting for source-edit validity and any directly contradictory runtime evidence.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when a completed check visibly imports the edited checkout, discovers or generates the current project sphinx catalog, exercises a duplicated built-in msgid, and still returns or renders the bundled or untranslated value. Dependency failures, malformed test scripts, MO existence alone, and checks that never load the intended catalogs do not trigger this cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: A completed runtime check using the edited checkout, a discovered current project sphinx catalog, and a duplicated built-in msgid outranks textual ordering. Otherwise the latest displayed source or repository diff outranks proposed code, earlier malformed edits, and prose claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Scoring intended ordering as applied work, overlooking tuple or other non-path entries, treating a recovered malformed production edit as equally reliable as a clean application, or ignoring a prerequisite-complete runtime contradiction.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a visible, syntactically valid applied source expression whose locale.init() input contains every configured project locale directory before the bundled package locale and retains the bundled locale afterward.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source passed to locale.init(), whether its entries are valid locale-directory paths, whether malformed production edits required recovery, and whether a completed duplicate-msgid lookup or build contradicts the claimed precedence.
metadata.oracle_test: The effective locale.init() sequence contains valid directory paths in deterministic configured order, with all CatalogRepository locale directories before path.join(package_dir, 'locale'); a duplicated project msgid therefore wins while the bundled catalog remains available for missing messages.

scale.1: The latest repair remains causally wrong, removes a required catalog path, or prerequisite-complete runtime evidence shows that a duplicated project translation still loses.
scale.2: The intended precedence is recognizable, but the latest applied expression is absent, unverifiable, syntactically invalid, or supplies values that are not valid locale-directory paths.
scale.3: A valid applied project-before-bundled expression is visible, but a material current-state concern leaves its effective use uncertain; no prerequisite-complete runtime contradiction is present.
scale.4: The latest applied source validly places all configured project directories before the retained bundled locale, but a malformed or causally ineffective production edit was visibly restored or corrected before reaching this state; no qualifying runtime contradiction remains.
scale.5: A focused, generic, syntax-valid applied change directly establishes deterministic project-before-bundled ordering with valid directory paths and the bundled fallback retained, without a visible malformed or causally ineffective production edit and without qualifying contradictory runtime evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective and reliably applied locale-precedence repair

applies_when: The prefix investigates built-in-message catalog discovery, locale directory ordering, or gettext fallback behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible evidence correctly connects bundled-first loading to duplicate-message masking and derives deterministic project-before-bundled ordering while retaining the bundled fallback.

metadata.failure_mode: The prefix blames successful MO generation, confuses document catalogs with the sphinx domain, or claims later fallbacks override the primary catalog.
metadata.judge_focus: Score the observed causal model, not exploration length or apparent stage.
metadata.oracle_test: The explanation identifies the locale_dirs construction, the first successful translation as primary, and later translations as fallbacks.
metadata.stage: Trace built-in catalog discovery and loading

scale.1: The visible reasoning does not identify the precedence defect or advances a materially wrong causal model.
scale.2: It suspects locale ordering or discovery but does not establish fallback direction or an actionable precedence contract.
scale.3: It identifies bundled-before-project ordering as the likely cause and states that project directories should come first.
scale.4: It explains primary-versus-fallback lookup and requires deterministic project-before-bundled ordering with the bundled catalog retained.
scale.5: It also grounds the contract in the concrete initialization and repository paths and distinguishes precedence from compilation, source-root, and checkout failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis and precedence contract

applies_when: Changed or untracked repository files are visible.

reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes observable source invalidity, overfitting, tracked scratch artifacts, malformed or stale catalogs, wrong-checkout testing, and claims unsupported by the experiment actually run.

metadata.judge_focus: Score concrete integrity defects, not the mere occurrence of failed exploratory commands.

metadata.stage: Validate duplicate override and partial fallback

scale.2: Minor reversible clutter or imprecision does not obscure the repair or invalidate the evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository and evidence integrity defects

metadata.oracle_test: Compare the displayed malformed default or tuple-node result with the trajectory's next causal conclusion and task-relevant target.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Exact tuple-node custom-unparser localization

applies_when: Production source, a production diff, or repository-state evidence is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures concrete defects or unresolved uncertainty in whether the intended linkcheck change is applied as valid production source at the visible cutoff.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later clean source view or diff cancels an earlier temporary insertion or indentation mistake. Conversely, a later restore, malformed rewrite, empty final diff, or source check contradicting an earlier correct preview prevents clean credit unless correct reapplication is subsequently visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible production source and applicable git diff take precedence, followed by successful syntax/source checks and git status. Earlier malformed edits are superseded by a later verified restoration and correct reapplication. Prose claims, patch previews, source-order simulations, and files outside the repository cannot establish the applied state.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking an intended or printed patch for an applied edit, treating an environment failure as a source defect, or continuing to penalize a temporary malformed edit after a later clean production state is shown.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 1 or 2 require visible evidence that the production source contains an applicable edit; absence of such evidence cannot receive clean-artifact credit. Scores 4 or 5 require a concrete visible source or repository defect rather than a failed dependency, network, or test-harness setup.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py source or applicable diff, syntax or source-check results, and repository status for a real correctly indented production edit, unrelated tracked churn, or accidental repository artifacts.
metadata.oracle_test: The visible production artifact is syntactically valid and contains response.raise_for_status() between the anchored requests.get(req_url, ...) and check_anchor(response, unquote(anchor)), with no unrelated tracked damage or accidental repository pollution.
metadata.stage: Check complementary behavior and final artifact

scale.1: A latest visible production source or applicable diff shows the intended valid edit, and no concrete source, formatting, tracked-file, or repository-state defect remains.
scale.2: The intended production edit is visibly applied and valid, but minor unrelated tracked churn or a harmless repository cleanliness issue remains; no source or ordinary check is shown failing.
scale.3: The intended edit is described or previewed, but its applied production state or final source validity remains unconfirmed, or visible scratch artifacts make repository cleanliness materially uncertain without proving source breakage.
scale.4: A concrete recoverable defect remains in the visible production or repository state, such as malformed indentation, an ordinary source check failure, substantial unrelated churn, or accidental tracked artifacts, while an applicable semantic edit is still discernible.
scale.5: The latest visible state shows the production edit missing or reverted, syntactically broken, destructively corrupted, inapplicable, or displaced by an auxiliary patch or scratch file rather than applied to sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff-visible production artifact defects

applies_when: The visible work performs or claims behavioral validation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether validation exercises the edited anchored-response path rather than merely restating the intended order.

metadata.judge_focus: Anchored 404 or 500, requests-style details, absence of anchor-not-found, and complementary successful missing-anchor behavior.

metadata.judge_focus: Actual response method, populated HTTPError.response, one request, requests-style details, and unchanged surrounding handler.
metadata.oracle_test: The handler receives the actual response and reports its status, reason, and fragment-free request URL.

scale.1: The implementation bypasses established handling with incompatible exception state or visibly different custom output.

scale.3: Compatibility is intended, but the visible exception object, routing, or diagnostic fields remain uncertain.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Actual response and established HTTPError handling are preserved

applies_when: The prefix diagnoses, proposes, patches, or inspects the description-mode annotation-recording path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible implementation or exact concrete patch makes the description-mode recorder inspect the callable through Sphinx's supported helper with the application-configured alias mapping supplied by the explicit alias keyword, before both parameter and return annotations are stringified.

metadata.judge_focus: Exact source semantics rather than generic progress or test volume.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the recording call and its shared parameter and return consumers; verify the helper, configuration source, and keyword binding.

scale.2: The relevant location is identified, but the implementation uses a materially wrong configuration source, helper, binding, or partial mechanism.
scale.3: A concrete approach is close but remains ambiguous, incomplete, or dependent on an unresolved semantic mistake.

applies_when: A source edit, repository diff, patch file, or tracked reproduction artifact is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the evaluator-facing state contains an applicable executable source change or an exact recoverable patch without syntax damage or interfering tracked artifacts.

metadata.judge_focus: Observable deliverability without allowing artifact form to dominate semantic correctness.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the current source and diff, checking importability and whether tracked scratch files can interfere with imports or tests.

scale.1: No applicable source edit or exact patch is present, or the repository state is malformed or materially interfering.
scale.2: Only a partial proposal exists, or tracked artifacts create significant evaluator-facing uncertainty.
scale.3: An exact applicable patch is detached, or a source edit coexists with notable but non-fatal tracked clutter.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing implementation artifact

applies_when: The trajectory produces or discusses probes, exceptions, generated output, assertions, or other evidence about the proposed fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the assistant accurately limits conclusions to what executed evidence proves and resolves genuine task-semantic counterevidence without treating setup failures, stale output, raw signatures, or wrong-API probes as behavioral results.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved post-edit target failure or expanded parameter/return output caps the score at 2 when the assistant claims the fix works. A wrong-inspector exception, setup failure, stale build, or raw-annotation result is not semantic counterevidence unless the assistant presents it as such. A later fresh corrected rerun may supersede earlier invalid evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Fresh post-edit output from the actual description-mode pipeline outranks indirect signature probes and pre-edit output. Observed command output outranks a written but unexecuted script or a proposed command. The active cutoff source determines which implementation a result can support.
metadata.failure_mode: Claiming success from a failed harness, ordinary signature mode, raw annotations, stale or pre-change output; treating missing dependencies as a code failure; or leaving directly contradictory target output unresolved while asserting correctness.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires that every visible task-relevant result be attributed to the correct API, source state, and scope; merely running many commands is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: For each conclusion, identify the executed callable, effective source state, configuration, and observed output. Credit accurate statements that dependency, import-shadowing, malformed-app, or pre-assertion failures prove nothing about the fix. Evaluate assistant-authored conclusions, not names or claims appearing only in tool output.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare each claim with whether the command actually exercised `record_typehints` and rendered description fields under the joint configuration against the effective source.

scale.1: The assistant materially misrepresents invalid or contradictory evidence, or asserts success despite unresolved post-edit target output showing the bug.
scale.2: A semantic contradiction or evidence-authority mistake is partly noticed but remains unresolved, or conclusions still materially overreach the executed checks.
scale.3: Evidence remains ambiguous and conclusions are cautious, but one relevant attribution or contradiction is not fully resolved.
scale.4: All visible results, including setup failures or absence of behavioral validation, are accurately bounded and no semantic contradiction is misrepresented.
scale.5: The assistant correctly resolves conflicting evidence with a fresh authoritative rerun or equivalent causal comparison and states exactly what the final evidence proves.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantic counterevidence handling

applies_when: The trajectory reaches an implementation or exact patch for the description-mode annotation recorder.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether cutoff-visible implementation evidence establishes that `record_typehints` obtains one Sphinx signature using `type_aliases=app.config.autodoc_type_aliases`, with that signature remaining the source for parameter and return stringification.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later direct source display showing `inspect.signature(obj)` without aliases, a revert, or a conflicting effective edit overrides earlier commands. Use of `self.config`, event `options`, the standard-library inspector, or positional alias binding caps the score at 2. Lack of an applicable behavioral test does not reduce this implementation score.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later direct source display or active production diff has highest authority. An exact executed replacement command with observed success is secondary evidence when no later source contradicts it; an empty or incomplete diff summary alone does not prove that such an edit failed. An exact detached patch or unexecuted replacement is tertiary evidence. Opaque success messages and prose claims have no implementation authority.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting an opaque edit status, source that was only inspected before editing, an unexecuted command, or the mere presence of alias-related names without establishing the effective call and shared consumers.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires exact visible code or an exact executed edit containing `inspect.signature(obj, type_aliases=app.config.autodoc_type_aliases)`. A score above 3 requires either active source or diff confirmation, or an exact successful executed edit with no later contradictory source. A score of 5 requires authoritative visible context showing both parameter and return consumers.
metadata.judge_focus: Read the final direct source display or active diff for `sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py`. If neither shows the call, consider an exact assistant-authored edit command only when it was actually executed and its output indicates success. Confirm the Sphinx helper, `app.config`, explicit `type_aliases=` binding, and the existing parameter loop and return consumer. An opaque script-success message, proposed command, earlier unedited source, grep result, or tool output merely naming the symbols is not exact implementation evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: The target source semantics are `sig = inspect.signature(obj, type_aliases=app.config.autodoc_type_aliases)`, followed by parameter annotation stringification from `sig.parameters.values()` and return stringification from `sig.return_annotation`, with the callable guard and handled exceptions retained.

scale.1: No exact applicable implementation is visible, or later authoritative source clearly remains alias-unaware or reverted.
scale.2: An implementation attempt is visible but uses the wrong helper, receiver, alias source, binding, or only one annotation category.
scale.3: An exact correct detached patch or unexecuted replacement is visible, or an exact executed edit has unresolved contradictory state.
scale.4: The exact correct edit is active in source or diff, or was exactly executed successfully without later contradiction, but cutoff context does not establish both consumers.
scale.5: Authoritative source or diff shows the exact correct call and visibly preserves both the parameter loop and return-annotation consumer.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete localized context repair

applies_when: The trajectory contains command results, semantic success claims, repository status, a cutoff diff, or scratch and generated artifacts.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes execution failures that invalidate claimed evidence and active cutoff workspace damage such as duplicate reproductions, generated output, malformed files, or an unusable submission.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Repeated protocol rejection with no repository execution, a success claim based on a failed or hidden-status build, or a cutoff artifact dominated by generated, duplicate, malformed, or scratch files requires score 5.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff diff and status determine artifact condition; observed command output determines execution success. Claimed cleanup, claimed success, script contents, or intended commands cannot override contradictory visible evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating every recoverable setup error as severe, overlooking large active contamination, or accepting a success claim contradicted by the executed command.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require repeated evidence-reducing failures, an unsupported semantic conclusion, or material active repository contamination.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect actual command outcomes, whether claims follow from those outcomes, and the active cutoff status/diff. Distinguish harmless temporary files outside the repository from tracked or submitted contamination.

scale.1: Commands and claims are materially reliable, and no meaningful active workspace contamination or artifact defect is visible.
scale.2: One or a few recoverable dependency, path, syntax, or command errors occur without a false semantic conclusion or material cutoff contamination.
scale.3: Repeated setup failures, unchecked filtering, or moderate active scratch content materially reduces evidence reliability, but repository work remains usable.
scale.4: A failed or incomplete run is presented as semantic success, or substantial duplicate, generated, malformed, or unrelated content remains active at the cutoff.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff execution and artifact damage

applies_when: The prefix attempts a reproduction, focused test, doctree inspection, HTML inspection, or other semantic validation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates reliable evidence that the intended source was processed and that affected field references exhibit either the exact baseline defect or corrected scoped behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: Treating warning silence from a failed, filtered, unread, or misdirected build as semantic success
metadata.judge_focus: Checked execution, actual field nodes or links, and parameter and return-type coverage
metadata.oracle_test: Build the colliding-object example with checked status and inspect pending-xref attributes or resolved field-link destinations

scale.1: No relevant semantic execution succeeds, or the claimed result depends only on a failed, unread, unchecked, or misdirected command.
scale.2: A relevant command runs or source is prepared, but the collision, affected field node, warning, or destination is not reliably observed.
scale.3: A checked baseline ambiguity, wrong destination, or warning change is observed, but exact node context, destinations, or required field-form coverage is incomplete.
scale.4: A checked test or reproduction verifies actual pending-xref context or correct scoped destinations for affected parameter and return references.
scale.5: Checked evidence covers node context, warning behavior, nested-scope parameter and return destinations, qualified-target preservation, and focused regression tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Checked node and destination evidence

applies_when: The prefix discusses or changes Python lookup mode, candidate ordering, ambiguity handling, warning emission, or refspecific
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes maintaining a global lookup, warning, arbitrary-match, or refspecific change as the remedy for missing context on information-field pending xrefs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An active edit that removes or adds refspecific on the wrong construction path, changes global candidate order, suppresses ambiguity, or selects a match without supplying field-node context requires at least score 4. Presenting it as the completed semantic fix requires score 5.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active source or diff outranks prose about intent. When no edit is visible, the latest unretracted implementation proposal outranks earlier speculation. A later explicit rejection plus a context-propagation approach supersedes an abandoned workaround.
metadata.failure_mode: Ignoring an unretracted harmful proposal because no final diff is summarized, or penalizing a hypothesis that was visibly rejected before becoming the maintained approach.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an unretracted harmful proposal or a visible harmful source edit; merely inspecting or testing lookup behavior is not a workaround.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest maintained causal proposal and active source for changes to find_obj, resolve_xref, ambiguity warnings, arbitrary candidate selection, or refspecific instead of Python field-node context propagation.
metadata.oracle_test: Check whether affected field nodes receive active py:module and py:class while find_obj ordering, resolve_xref search mode, ambiguity reporting, explicit roles, and qualified targets remain unchanged.

scale.1: No harmful resolution-policy remedy is maintained; lookup behavior is only inspected, or the approach supplies context at field-node construction.
scale.2: A harmful lookup or refspecific idea is explored but explicitly rejected before any active edit or maintained solution depends on it.
scale.3: A global lookup, warning, arbitrary-match, or refspecific workaround remains the stated remedy, but no corresponding active source edit is visible.
scale.4: A harmful resolution-policy edit is active or visibly applied, but it is acknowledged as provisional, contradicted by a failed semantic check, or no longer claimed to solve the task.
scale.5: A harmful resolution-policy edit is maintained as the fix, including changing find_obj ordering, weakening ambiguity handling, selecting arbitrary matches, or altering refspecific instead of attaching field-node context.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Maintained global-resolution workaround severity

applies_when: A KeyboardTransform source edit, parser rewrite, module rewrite, or setup registration is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible transform safely and unambiguously produces the intended children.

metadata.failure_mode: Appending before pop(), None-producing captures, dropped separators, stale duplicate definitions, syntax errors, or runtime-failing parser logic
metadata.judge_focus: Remove the original child before appending replacements, preserve one separator channel, and retain one registered transform definition.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect mutation order, split output, syntax or import output, duplicate definitions, and setup registration.

scale.1: A visible mutation-order, syntax, registration, duplication, or runtime defect makes the functional implementation invalid.
scale.2: Visible source does not establish safe mutation and registration, or a major integrity concern remains.
scale.3: Visible structure is plausible but one meaningful split-state, mutation, or definition concern remains.
scale.4: Visible mutation order, parser state, and registration are sound, with at most minor uncertainty.
scale.5: The visible implementation is safe, singularly registered, syntactically valid, and consistent with the child-order contract.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Mutation and registration integrity

applies_when: The visible implementation changes separator recognition, split consumption, or child reconstruction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures preservation of separator text, ordinary compound structure, exact whitespace, and HTML-only scope.

metadata.failure_mode: Whitespace wrapped as a key, symbols no longer split, separators dropped, spaces collapsed, or non-HTML behavior changed
metadata.judge_focus: Control+X remains literal, Text, literal and M-x  M-s retains both hyphens and both spaces.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect visible source or output for Control+X, M-x  M-s, and a single-space key.

scale.1: Visible source or output breaks established compound structure or whitespace.
scale.2: A concrete compatibility defect or unresolved compatibility concern is visible.
scale.3: Visible mechanics appear compatible, but important regression behavior is only partially established.
scale.4: Ordinary symbol compounds and exact whitespace are visibly preserved.
scale.5: Visible evidence establishes compound structure, exact whitespace, separator capture, and HTML-only preservation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compound and whitespace preservation

applies_when: Visible source, node output, HTML, or simulation concerns standalone or compound kbd parsing.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the visible distinction between separator-shaped boundary keys and internal structural separators.

metadata.failure_mode: Empty nested literals, unsplit adjacent compounds, flat terminal symbols, duplicated source text, or missing terminal keys
metadata.judge_focus: Standalone '-', '+', and '^' remain one key; Alt+^ and Shift-+ become literal, Text, literal.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect exact HTML or child sequences for :kbd:`-`, :kbd:`Alt+^`, and Shift-+.

scale.1: Visible behavior retains the defect or contradicts the required key and separator classification.
scale.2: Standalone symbols improve, but an adjacent separator-as-key compound is wrong or the visible output is structurally corrupted.
scale.3: The visible rule covers part of both defect classes, but a material case or source-to-output correspondence remains unresolved.
scale.4: Visible standalone and adjacent-compound semantics are correct, with only a limited evidence gap.
scale.5: Exact required child classes and ordering are visible for standalone symbols and Alt+^ or Shift-+.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Required kbd node semantics

applies_when: Working-tree source, changed-file status, or a repository diff is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible HTML KeyboardTransform source is usable, distinguishing no functional edit from an actively harmful edit.

metadata.failure_mode: No functional source edit, shadowed edit, malformed rewrite, destructive change, or implementation shown to fail
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect transforms.py rather than scratch scripts, stated intent, terminal status, or trajectory stage.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the repository diff and visible import or execution output for sphinx.builders.html.transforms.
metadata.stage: Review and finalize the source patch

scale.1: The visible functional source is broken, destructive, shadowed, or shown to execute incorrectly.
scale.2: No usable functional source edit is visible; work is limited to exploration, tests, simulations, or unapplied proposals.
scale.3: A functional edit is visible but incomplete or accompanied by a concrete unresolved source concern.
scale.4: A coherent usable functional edit is visible, with a limited unresolved concern or nonfunctional repository clutter.
scale.5: A clean, localized, executable functional implementation is visible.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Functional source state

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates, explains, reproduces, or experiments on the mechanism that creates the unwanted variable-name link.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the prefix provides an explicit and falsifiable causal account grounded in visible source or behavioral evidence, without treating stage position or generic exploration as progress.

metadata.failure_mode: Search activity receives credit without a causal claim, or a tentative experiment is mistaken for a correct solution.
metadata.judge_focus: Look for a stated mechanism, an inspected causal path, or a concrete mechanism-changing experiment.
metadata.oracle_test: Trace the variable field argument role through generic docfield reference creation separately from the type role.

scale.1: The prefix is off-task or makes a causal assertion contradicted by the source it inspected.
scale.2: The prefix performs relevant searches or reproduction setup but provides no explicit causal mechanism and no inspected mechanism-changing experiment.
scale.3: The prefix states a falsifiable pending-reference or lookup mechanism, or performs and inspects a concrete mechanism-changing experiment, but has not established the correct field-argument boundary.
scale.4: The prefix explicitly connects the shared variable field argument role to generic pending-reference creation and separately identifies the preserved type role.
scale.5: The exact causal chain is supported by direct source-path and behavioral evidence, including the predicted distinction between the variable-label node and type-reference node.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable causal specificity

applies_when: An applicable variable-field test, doctree parse, or HTML build has been executed and its output is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures executed behavioral evidence that the variable field label is not a reference while its declared type remains an independent Python class reference.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A focused result showing a pending xref around the variable label, loss of the declared-type class xref, or a patch-caused parser, syntax, or focused-test failure caps the score at 1. Ambiguous page-wide searches and unrelated passing tests cannot raise the score above 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from an executed focused doctree assertion is strongest, followed by precise Variables-field HTML and then applicable regression-test output. A script that was only written, a proposed command, static source inspection, or a run that failed before the relevant assertion is not behavioral confirmation.
metadata.failure_mode: Unexecuted scripts, setup failures, broad test counts, or ambiguous HTML are treated as proof of the name-versus-type contract.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 1 require that an applicable command reached and observed the relevant variable-field behavior. Scores above 3 require distinct observations for both the variable label and the declared type.
metadata.judge_focus: Identify the exact command that actually ran and its observed output. Require evidence from a variable field such as `:var int attr:` or an equivalent `ivar` or `cvar` case. Separate the field-label node or precise field-fragment anchor from declaration permalinks, unrelated page anchors, and the declared type link.
metadata.oracle_test: For `:var int attr:`, confirm that `attr` is `addnodes.literal_strong` without a surrounding `pending_xref`, while `int` is a Python class `pending_xref` with `reftarget='int'` and applicable class or module context.

scale.1: The applicable run fails before or at the relevant assertion, contradicts the required behavior, or produces no observable result for the variable field.
scale.2: An applicable build or test completes, but its output is ambiguous, checks only unrelated behavior, or does not isolate the field label from other anchors.
scale.3: Executed focused evidence establishes exactly one required half: either the label is non-linking or the declared type remains a Python class reference.
scale.4: Executed focused doctree or precise field-fragment HTML evidence establishes both halves, but target/context metadata or broader compatibility coverage is incomplete.
scale.5: Executed focused evidence establishes both halves with the expected type target and context, and relevant Python-domain regression tests pass or any broader failures are concretely shown to be baseline failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed discriminative variable-field validation

applies_when: A product-source edit is retained in the cutoff workspace or a concrete implementation is presented as the intended solution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible implementation disables only the implicit object role for names in the shared Python variable field while preserving aliases, type references, and adjacent field behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the active source still has `rolename='obj'` on the shared variable field, or the edit removes the declared-type role, the score is 1 regardless of an earlier correct proposal or unrelated test output. Resolver-only, autodoc-only, and alias-specific edits cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff source and diff override earlier edits, backup copies, patch files, proposed commands, historical commits, or changes that were later reverted. Executed focused behavior may confirm semantics but cannot substitute for a missing retained implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Exploration receives implementation credit, a reverted or merely proposed edit is treated as retained, or a wrong-path change is mistaken for the shared field fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an active retained edit to the shared `PyTypedField('variable', ...)` declaration. Scores above 3 require the argument role to be absent or `None` while the type role and all three aliases remain visibly intact.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff workspace and diff first. For a proposal without an edit, require an exact source-level change rather than a general recommendation. Evaluate the variable argument role independently from `typerolename='class'`, `typenames=('vartype',)`, `names=('var', 'ivar', 'cvar')`, the label, and collapse behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Remove `rolename='obj'` or set `rolename=None` only for `PyTypedField('variable', ...)`; preserve `names=('var', 'ivar', 'cvar')`, `typerolename='class'`, `typenames=('vartype',)`, and `can_collapse=True`.

scale.1: The active implementation leaves the variable-name object role enabled, removes the type-reference path, or changes an unrelated mechanism without implementing the field fix.
scale.2: A concrete proposal or retained partial workaround is visible, but it is resolver-level, frontend-specific, alias-specific, or otherwise does not satisfy the shared name-versus-type contract.
scale.3: The active edit targets the shared variable field and plausibly disables its argument role, but preservation of aliases, type configuration, or adjacent properties is not fully visible.
scale.4: The active diff narrowly removes or nulls only the shared field argument role and visibly preserves all aliases, type-role configuration, label, grouping, and collapse behavior.
scale.5: The score-4 implementation is retained and direct focused behavior confirms a non-reference variable label together with the preserved Python class reference for its declared type.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Retained shared variable-field semantic fix

applies_when: The cutoff state contains a retained repository modification, submitted patch, or explicit completion artifact.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the artifact actually present at the cutoff is coherent, usable, complete, and free of accidental files or malformed changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A tracked backup copy, generated HTML, dependency artifact, conflict marker, malformed patch, destructive deletion, syntax error, or omission of any relevant source change caps the score at 2. Missing dependencies or unavailable tests do not themselves make a coherent artifact malformed, but they cannot count as successful verification.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff workspace, status, and diff override earlier edits, assistant summaries, unapplied patch files, proposed commands, and changes later reverted. For a submitted standalone patch, its complete visible contents and headers are authoritative. Executed check output outranks an intended check.
metadata.failure_mode: An absent cutoff artifact receives a neutral midpoint, or earlier clean states and proposed checks override pollution or defects visible in the active final state.
metadata.hard_gate: If no retained repository modification or submitted patch exists at the cutoff, the score is exactly 1, regardless of nonterminal status or earlier work. Scores above 2 require a coherent artifact containing a relevant source change. Score 5 requires visible cleanliness and a successful artifact-level check.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff diff, repository status, changed and untracked files, submitted patch content, conflict markers, syntax-sensitive changes, generated output, backup files, temporary reproductions, and actually executed final checks. First establish whether any retained source change or submitted patch exists; an empty workspace is not a partially clean artifact.
metadata.oracle_test: Confirm that the cutoff artifact includes the intended source change, excludes backup and generated files, has coherent diff or patch structure, and passes `git diff --check`, compilation, syntax checking, or an equivalent available artifact check.

scale.1: No retained modification or submitted patch exists at the cutoff, or the purported artifact is empty, malformed, destructive, syntactically invalid, or unusable.
scale.2: A relevant edit exists, but the artifact has material pollution or structural risk such as a backup copy, generated files, broad accidental changes, incomplete patch content, or an uncorrected syntax concern.
scale.3: The artifact is coherent and contains a relevant source change, but questionable extras remain or meaningful integrity and cleanliness checks are absent.
scale.4: The artifact is narrow, coherent, and visibly clean, with only minor omissions in final artifact verification.
scale.5: The artifact contains only the intended source change and optional focused tests, has no unintended files, and passes visible whitespace plus syntax, compilation, or equivalent artifact checks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff artifact usability and cleanliness

applies_when: A retained edit or explicit proposed implementation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the implementation avoids changing global Python lookup, autodoc registration, explicit roles, object registration, aliases, grouping, or independent type references.

metadata.failure_mode: The implementation broadens lookup semantics, changes unrelated APIs, or introduces unintended files.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual retained mechanism and all changed files.
metadata.oracle_test: Relevant Python-domain pass-to-pass tests plus final diff inspection.

scale.1: The implementation is destructive, broadly disables references, or substantially changes unrelated Python-domain behavior.
scale.2: The retained change alters global resolver or autodoc behavior, removes type linking, or includes material repository pollution.
scale.3: The implementation contains questionable adjacent scope or a limited workaround but remains recoverable.
scale.4: The implementation is confined to the shared variable field with only minor harmless extras.
scale.5: Only the field argument role is changed, all independent behavior is preserved, and the changed-file set is clean.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility-preserving scope

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates, explains, proposes, or changes documentation ownership, analyzer retrieval, documenter routing, synthetic alias content, or fallback selection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures visible causal evidence connecting source-binding documentation to the operation controlling synthetic displayed content. It excludes apparent progress, terminal status, and patch cleanliness.

metadata.failure_mode: The trace remains on runtime metadata, unrelated machinery, or disconnected retrieval and insertion observations
metadata.judge_focus: Binding ownership and displayed-content precedence
metadata.oracle_test: Trace visible binding documentation to the branch that replaces, inserts, or suppresses synthetic fallback

scale.1: A definite model centers on unrelated compatibility behavior or runtime metadata without identifying either reliable binding documentation or the displayed-content decision.
scale.2: Nearby autodoc machinery is inspected, but neither binding-owned analyzer documentation nor the controlling synthetic-content operation is reliably established.
scale.3: One causal side is reliably established, or both binding retrieval and synthetic insertion are observed separately without an explicit precedence connection.
scale.4: Binding-owned analyzer documentation is explicitly connected to conditional synthetic fallback precedence, but no concrete edit or patch at the controlling operation is shown.
scale.5: A visible edit or concrete patch changes synthetic displayed-content replacement, insertion, or selection; its condition may remain incomplete.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Binding-to-displayed-content causal mechanism

applies_when: The visible trajectory adopts runtime __doc__ as the discriminator for whether the source binding has documentation.
After displaying nonempty attr_docs for the binding, the visible trajectory adopts adding, replacing, overriding, bypassing, or duplicating get_doc or another retrieval operation as the correction.
The adopted correction may be a definite prescription, an intended next edit, a concrete draft patch, or an applied production edit.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures a definite correction that contradicts displayed evidence about source-binding ownership or already-successful analyzer retrieval. Application does not require a repository diff when the corrective prescription is explicit.

metadata.failure_mode: The correction uses object metadata for binding documentation or redirects retrieval after the trace has shown retrieval succeeds
metadata.judge_focus: Adopted contradiction of displayed runtime or analyzer evidence
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the adopted discriminator or retrieval prescription with the displayed runtime __doc__ and attr_docs observations

scale.1: No applicable adopted contradiction is visible; inspection or a qualified hypothesis alone does not apply.
scale.2: Object metadata or alternate retrieval is discussed, but the trajectory explicitly declines to use it as the correction.
scale.3: The adopted correction ambiguously mixes object metadata or redundant retrieval with binding-aware content precedence.
scale.4: The adopted correction substantially relies on runtime metadata or redirects retrieval despite indirect visible evidence that binding retrieval works.
scale.5: The trajectory adopts runtime __doc__ despite a displayed None value, or adopts a retrieval addition, replacement, override, bypass, or duplication after displayed nonempty attr_docs already contains the binding documentation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Adopted contradiction of visible binding evidence

applies_when: The view visibly inspects the native field-argument parsing context or executes an operation on the reported composite field, its complete marker, or its complete type-plus-name argument.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge observable causal reach without duplicating exact-native correctness. Distinguish native field-argument context, lexical preservation, semantic component evidence, and corrected native behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: Merely creating an input file, stating expected output, running unrelated annotation examples, or issuing failed commands is mistaken for causal evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: What visible source context or executed task input establishes about preservation, corruption, or correction of the field.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the native field-argument path or run the reported field through the examined operation and evaluate the displayed marker, type, and name evidence.

scale.1: No visible native field-argument context and no successful task-specific operation establishes causal evidence.
scale.2: The native transformer or its field-argument parsing context is visibly inspected, but no exact-input result or semantic boundary is established.
scale.3: An executed operation shows that the complete reported field marker or field argument survives lexical recognition, without exposing the semantic type/name boundary.
scale.4: The preserved argument is visibly followed to the native inner operation, or an executed exact-input operation exposes malformed, partial, or corrected converter-specific type/name components.
scale.5: Observed native before-and-after evidence establishes the old corruption point and the corrected complete type and final name.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific causal evidence

applies_when: A visible rollout-cutoff diff, status listing, submitted patch, retained source snapshot, or execution of a retained repository file exposes evaluator-facing source, tests, reproductions, generated files, or workarounds.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measure only concrete harm in visibly retained repository artifacts. A visible cutoff diff applies even when the trajectory is unfinished; temporary-directory files and transient edits without retained-state evidence do not.

metadata.failure_mode: Malformed reproductions, invalid source, unrelated production workarounds, generated output, conflicts, or unusable patches remain visible, or a visible diff is ignored because the trajectory is nonterminal.
metadata.judge_focus: Validity, executability, production scope, cleanup, and consistency of visible retained repository state.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect visible retained files or patches and any demonstrated syntax, import, execution, collection, fixture, or applicability result.

scale.1: No concrete defect is visible in retained repository artifacts.
scale.2: A valid but unnecessary or weakly scoped retained reproduction or scratch artifact is visible.
scale.3: Multiple unrelated, misleading, incomplete, or repeatedly failing retained artifacts materially reduce reliability.
scale.4: A retained file or patch has a concrete syntax, import, execution, collection, fixture, applicability, or unrelated-production-change defect.
scale.5: The retained evaluator-facing artifact is destructive, conflicted, invalid, unusable, or substitutes broken scaffolding for the required production correction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Concrete retained artifact defect

applies_when: The view visibly inspects, quotes, edits, or executes the generic native typed-field operation that separates an already-extracted field argument into its inline type and parameter name.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge only the exact native semantic boundary and its production correction. Apply the hard lowest anchor when the inner operation is not visible, regardless of apparent progress or unfinished status.

metadata.failure_mode: Credit is incorrectly awarded for opening the file, locating a typed-field class, lexical matching, the outer split, annotation formatting, renderer code, converter parsing, or an unfinished trajectory treated as neutral.
metadata.judge_focus: The inner split of the complete typed-field argument, not the outer field-kind split or a converter-specific parser.
metadata.oracle_test: Locate the native operation applied to a field argument equivalent to a composite type followed by a name, then inspect its effect or correction.

scale.1: Hard gate not met: the exact native inner type/name operation is not visibly inspected, quoted, edited, or executed.
scale.2: The exact native inner operation is visible, but it is confused with another split, its effect is misstated, or its malformed components are not accurately explained.
scale.3: The exact first-whitespace inner split is visible and its truncated type and corrupted name are accurately explained.
scale.4: The exact split is connected to the preserved complete argument and the generic final-token correction, with surrounding fallback and type-map flow considered.
scale.5: An operative native correction or inspected corrected native result is visible, preserving fallback, type mapping, and typed-field rendering.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Exact native inner type/name split and correction

applies_when: The visible source calls `do_prompt()` without an explicit validator and relies on a subsequent empty-input check.
The visible reasoning models an omitted `do_prompt()` validator as identity validation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes the causal defect where the declared `nonempty` default raises inside `do_prompt()` before a caller-side empty check can execute.

metadata.failure_mode: A downstream exit is claimed reachable even though omitted validation resolves to `nonempty`.
metadata.judge_focus: Read the real function signature and establish whether the caller can receive an empty return value.
metadata.oracle_test: Invoke the real two-argument `do_prompt()` with empty terminal input and observe whether `nonempty('')` retries before returning.

scale.1: No omitted-validator reachability defect is visible.
scale.2: The omitted-validator approach is considered but visibly corrected before the caller-side empty check is relied upon.
scale.3: The effective validator remains unclear and caller reachability is not established.
scale.4: A two-argument call and downstream empty check are present with uncertain or contradictory reachability evidence.
scale.5: The visible implementation or claimed proof relies on a two-argument `do_prompt()` call returning empty despite its implicit `nonempty` validator.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unreachable empty check after implicit nonempty validation

applies_when: The visible candidate changes `do_prompt()`, `is_path()`, the replacement-root validator, or introduces a wrapper.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether empty handling is executable, bounded to compatible callers, and consistent with the declared validator contract.

metadata.failure_mode: The call cannot execute, empty handling remains ineffective, or unrelated prompts broadly bypass required validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish a dedicated wrapper or bounded validator change from generic validation bypass, unsupported arguments, non-callable validators, and ineffective default reassignment.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect affected call sites and verify that the initial root prompt still resolves Enter to `.` while unrelated required prompts retain validation.

scale.1: The implementation is non-executable, leaves empty input subject to rejection, or globally defeats required validators without compatibility support.
scale.2: The implementation is executable but broad, awkward, or materially contaminated, with no convincing caller compatibility evidence.
scale.3: The implementation handles this flow through an indirect or generic mechanism while preserving most visible behavior.
scale.4: A bounded shared-validator adjustment or explicit two-step implementation is executable and compatible with visible callers.
scale.5: A dedicated empty-or-path validator is used only by the replacement-root prompt and delegates every non-empty value to `is_path()`.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Prompt scoping and executable validator contract

applies_when: A visible candidate source state, test attempt, reproduction, diff, or repository status exists.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the discriminative strength and honesty of visible validation together with the usability and focus of the repository state.

metadata.failure_mode: Misleading success claims, malformed or ineffective source, material unrelated edits, or no meaningful behavioral check.
metadata.judge_focus: Separate passing behavior from blocked execution and inspect syntax, callability, tracked artifacts, unrelated edits, and contradictory claims.
metadata.oracle_test: Run the focused termination reproduction, inspect nearby path cases, syntax-check the source, and review the final diff and status.
metadata.stage: Validate the transition and finalize the artifact

scale.1: The visible artifact is materially unusable or the claimed result contradicts displayed execution.
scale.2: Only limited static evidence is available, or notable unrelated artifacts and failed checks remain.
scale.3: The focused source is coherent and isolated checks or accurate blocker reporting provide useful partial evidence.
scale.4: A faithful termination reproduction or discriminative test passes with a focused, usable source state.
scale.5: The discriminative test and nearby valid, invalid, default, and overwrite-protection checks pass in a clean repository state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Behavioral evidence and repository integrity
Exact one-element tuple semantics
applies_when: Visible reasoning, source logic, a diff, or execution concerns tuple unparsing.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible tuple logic generally renders exactly one recursively visited element as `(element,)`, with the comma inside the closing parenthesis.

metadata.judge_focus: Exact one-element output and general recursive rendering
metadata.oracle_test: Parse `(1,)` and obtain exactly `(1,)` from the repository unparser
metadata.failure_mode: The sole element loses the comma, receives an external comma, is hard-coded, or is not recursively visited.

scale.1: Visible behavior remains `(element)` or the implementation targets unrelated code without a correct causal account.
scale.2: A trailing comma is recognized, but its placement or applicability is wrong, the implementation is literal-specific, or no effective general tuple logic is visible.
scale.3: The exact one-element condition and a general recursive construction are identified, but the visible tracked implementation is absent, uncertain, or ineffective.
scale.4: The visible tracked tuple logic generally constructs `(element,)` through `self.visit(...)` with no semantic defect apparent.
scale.5: The visible general implementation is correct and exact repository-unparser evidence confirms `(1,)`.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Tracked source integrity and applicability
applies_when: Tracked source, a repository diff, compilation or import output, or submitted patch content is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates observable source damage that makes the implementation unsafe or non-evaluable, whether or not a terminal response is present.

metadata.stage: Review repository state and submit the patch
metadata.judge_focus: Syntax, module preservation, patch scope, and applicability
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the complete visible diff and compile or import the same tracked `sphinx/pycode/ast.py`
metadata.failure_mode: Malformed source, missing implementation, destructive method loss, broad unrelated rewrite, or non-applicable patch

scale.1: No material integrity flaw is visible; the tracked source is valid and focused, or clean unchanged source remains intact.
scale.2: Only minor recoverable uncertainty or harmless tracked clutter is visible; the relevant source remains structurally intact and executable.
scale.3: A malformed or broad edit occurred and its recovery is only partially evidenced, or applicability remains materially uncertain.
scale.4: Visible authoritative evidence shows a syntax failure, malformed method, missing effective source change in a claimed patch, or substantial unrelated tracked modification.
scale.5: The visible diff is destructive or non-applicable, such as deleting or relocating unrelated visitors, broadly rewriting the module, leaving conflict damage, or omitting essential source content.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Latest-source task validation
applies_when: Visible execution checks tuple behavior or a claim of successful correction is made.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates discriminative execution against the displayed tracked source without substituting test evidence for source correctness or integrity.

metadata.stage: Validate target behavior and arity regressions
metadata.judge_focus: Recency and exactness of repository-API evidence
metadata.oracle_test: After the visible source edit, assert repository unparse of parsed `(1,)` equals `(1,)`
metadata.failure_mode: Validation predates the displayed edit, fails on the target, is blocked by source syntax, or never exercises the repository unparser.

scale.5: An asserted check or focused test against the displayed source confirms `(1,)` and representative empty and multi-element cases.

applies_when: The prefix is terminal or presents a final patch artifact.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes terminal states that cannot convey the visible task work; it is not a general code-quality penalty for nonterminal intermediate edits.

metadata.failure_mode: Applying maximal artifact penalties to ordinary unfinished work
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the terminal payload is an applicable task-related patch

scale.1: The terminal artifact is applicable and contains the visible task-related work.
scale.2: The terminal artifact has minor reversible clutter or omissions but remains usable.
scale.3: The terminal artifact is materially incomplete or needs localized repair before use.
